role.description: Which zone ground role the painted tread takes (`regions[].ground`); omitted = `road`. `road`: inside a zone that overrides `road`, its surface replaces `surface`. `paving`: a town street or square, painted with the zone's `paving` (cobble); `town-ground` writes it on the streets it builds. `none`: always `surface`. A zone that overrides nothing leaves `surface` as it is.

excludeScatter.description: When omitted or true, exclude scatter and ground cover across the whole town pad. Set false for landscaped towns whose roads and building foundations provide local clearances.

cover.description: Let ground cover (grass, flowers) grow on the pad while scatter stays excluded. Streets keep it off through the road clearance, building plots through `clearings` (one per plot, `cover: true`) — install those first, or grass stands inside the buildings. Omitted = no cover on the pad. Implied by `excludeScatter: false`.

tier.description: How big a place this is. It sets the pad's size and, later, what gets built on it; `worldgen towns` buckets a world into a few capitals on the coast, some cities, and a long tail of villages and hamlets, because a world of forty identical 45 m discs reads as forty identical places. Absent on a recipe written before tiers existed — read it as "capital" when `tags` says so, "town" otherwise.

keep.description: Pinned in place: `worldgen towns` keeps this town where it is (id, centre, tier) instead of re-siting it, exactly as a `pinned` tag or `--keep <id>` does, but recorded in the recipe so a plain rerun keeps it too. `worldgen towns --keep` writes it; `worldgen town-pins` sets or clears it without re-siting anything; `--release <ids|all>` lets a town move again. Unlike the `pinned` tag it does not stop `worldgen terrace` from re-cutting the town's shelves.

falloff.description: Distance beyond `radius` over which the pad blends into natural terrain.

flatten.description: How hard the whole footprint is pulled to `groundY`. 1 is a table top. A TERRACED town sets this to 0 and leaves the hill alone — its `terraces` are the flat ground, and the slope between them is the point.

terraces.description: Shelves stepped up the site, for a town with verticality. Written by `worldgen terrace`, which also cuts the ramps between them as ordinary roads (`<town>-ramp-*`). Empty for a town on the flat.

gates.description: Ways in. A town with gates is entered ONLY through them: `worldgen paths` and `worldgen trails` route to the gate mouth that faces where they come from instead of to the centre, and the pad is a wall to every route not arriving at one. Leave empty for an open village whose lanes are the road.

landformCalm.description: Discs where anchor `landform` families (and river valleys) are faded out, so authored places — towns, dressed sites, height patches, terrace walls — keep the ground they were built on when a profile is added or retuned. Written by `worldgen landform-calm`. Omit = no calm (and no cost).

heightPatches.description: Raster elevation edits applied after ordinary heightfield features. Affect terrain mesh, collision and placement together; later patches win. Existing 3D density modifiers still apply.

lakes.description: Standing water at its own level, basin carved beneath. Written by `worldgen rivers`.

bridges.description: Road decks spanning rivers. Written by `worldgen roads`. The streamer draws each as a PLACEHOLDER (a flat slab and box piers); a real bridge is a `bridgeSpans` entry (`worldgen bridge-place`, the world-kit bridge kits).

bridgeSpans.description: Real bridges across gaps (stone arch bridges / aqueducts with piers founded on the ground or seabed, or rope suspension bridges) — authoring truth. `worldgen bridge-place` fits each to the ground and writes its `solved` pieces plus the derived `bs-<id>*` height patches and clearing; `--refit` re-solves them after the terrain changes.

fills.description: Sediment-filled hollows on the river network. Written by `worldgen rivers`.

riverPaths.description: Hand- or agent-drawn river centrelines. AUTHORING input: `worldgen rivers` solves each into `rivers`.

tunnels.description: Carved cave passages. Written by `worldgen caves`.

height.description: 0 = a sphere. Above 0 the blob is a VERTICAL CAPSULE this tall, rising from `center` — which is what turns the escape hatch into a monolith: a desert pillar is one line of JSON rather than a stack of spheres, and it stays one line when you drag it somewhere else.

topRadius.description: Radius at the TOP of a capsule (needs `height`). Omit for a uniform column. A value below `radius` is what turns a pillar into a needle — a spire tapering as it rises reads as weathered stone, a cylinder reads as a prop.

passages.description: Bounded rectangular flat-floor passage cutters applied after blobs. Signed exterior samples avoid tunnel floor snapping. They remove rock only; a supported floor and roof must already exist. Render, collision and placement share this field.

operators.description: LANDFORM OPERATORS — authoring truth for shaped ground: `{ id, op, ...params }` (terrace, path, ...; the engine spec's `landformOperators` lists them). Agents write these, never raw carve boxes. `worldgen op <world> --apply` compiles each into derived features with ids `op:<id>:*` (regenerable, never hand-edited; re-applying replaces exactly them) and stamps `compiled`. The field reads only the compiled pieces. docs/voxel-worlds.md "Landform operators".

kitWalls.description: Retaining-wall RUNS on shelf risers, COMPILED by a landform operator (`terrace`; ids `op:<id>:wall-<n>`); never hand-edited. The streamer places each world-kit piece (2 m straights + caps); the field carves each face cut down to the wall foot. docs/voxel-worlds.md "Landform operators".

landmarks.description: LANDMARKS: baked rock built from a landform operator's solve (`ledges` mode landmark; ids `op:<id>:landmark`), never hand-edited. The streamer places the prefab (merged DC mesh + trimesh collider, the terrain material) in the cell its origin stands in; the operator's height patch keeps the terrain inside it. docs/voxel-worlds.md 'Landform operators'.

ribbons.description: Path RIBBONS: solved walk surfaces laid over graded ground (steps, switchbacks, retaining walls). COMPILED by the `path` landform operator (ids `op:<id>:ribbon`); never hand-edited. The streamer draws each as a surface mesh with a collider; the field carves its wall faces; vegetation keeps its outline clear. Paths are ribbons: never carve a path.

fallSites.description: Agent-crafted waterfalls: a solved fall split into a cascade of pools and dressed with rocks. Written by `worldgen fall-site`; see docs/world-editing/rivers-and-falls.md.

name.description: What players call this one — 'The Warren Mouth'. Set by a story; a bare generated POI has none and is labelled by its id.

zone.description: Region id this POI stands in (recipe `regions`), or empty in an unzoned world. Stamped by `worldgen pois` and re-stamped whenever the zones are redrawn, so a zone's contents can be listed, dressed and quested over without anything having to re-run point-in-polygon over 1000 landmarks.

radius.description: Area of effect for kinds that have one — a waystation's sanctuary circle (metres).

tags.description: Free-form; "safe" marks a sanctuary (no player-on-player damage within `radius`), "pass" a zone-border pass.

terraceWalls.description: Terraces held up by real retaining walls (pad outline, drop, inserts) — authoring truth. `worldgen terrace-place` fits each to the ground and writes its `solved` pieces plus the derived `tw-<id>*` height patch, passages and clearing; `--refit` re-solves them after the terrain changes. `worldgen terrace` writes the `<town>-riser-*` ones for towns when `townTerraces.walls` is on.

clearings.description: Patches kept clear of scatter and/or ground cover (a site's footprint, a hall pad, a town's building plots, streets and door paths), feathered at the edge. Terrain is untouched. Written by `worldgen vegetation --clearings <file>`; see docs/voxel-worlds.md section 31.

camps.description: Enemy camps — where monsters live. Written by `worldgen spawn`, which also patches the matching spawnArea entities into the scene (ids `camp-*`, rewritten on every run); hand-written camps are kept.

verticalRange.description: The vertical band actually meshed per cell. A voxel world is not infinite in Y for free.

textureFilter.description: Magnification filter for every terrain surface texture. Set 'nearest' for PIXEL ART so it stays chunky instead of being smeared smooth up close. Emitted onto the terrain material by `worldgen material`.

macroNoise.description: Noise multiplied over the whole blended terrain to break up texture repetition, emitted onto the terrain material by `worldgen material`. It lives HERE and not only in the material because the material is derived data — anything written straight into it is lost the next time the palette changes and it gets re-emitted.

waterMaterial.description: Material asset id for the water emitted into streamed cells (lakes, and rivers without a `riverMaterial`), clipped from each cell's terrain. Without it rivers are carved but dry. `worldgen init` writes one beside the terrain material.

riverMaterial.description: Material asset id for river water specifically — a water material with `flowMode: "field"`, so the water visibly runs downstream along the current each vertex carries. Falls back to `waterMaterial` (standing water). `worldgen rivers` writes `<waterMaterial>-river` and sets this.

marshMaterial.description: Material asset id for the marsh sheet (zone anchors with a `waterTable`): still, murky standing water. Falls back to `waterMaterial`.

bridgeMaterial.description: Material asset id for the placeholder decks emitted for `features.bridges`. `worldgen roads` writes a plain timber-coloured one when the recipe has none.

splat.description: How the terrain mesh carries its surface weights. `dense`: every vertex carries a weight per palette surface (ceil(N/4) vec4 attributes) and the shader blends every layer — fine to 16 surfaces. `indexed`: every vertex carries the ids and weights of the FOUR layers it blends (two 4-byte attributes), the shader samples those four from one texture array, and the palette can be 64 deep (zone ground textures). A palette past 16 is meshed indexed regardless. `worldgen material` must be re-run after changing it.

zoneGround.description: How zone ground overrides (`regions[].ground`) blend across zone borders.

rockSkins.description: ROCK SKINS — the world's stone follows the place. Cliff surface NAME -> body slice (`rockCap.bases` index) of the world's rock-cap material. Every scatter rock, boulder and cliff mass (rules with `cap`, `rockBase` or `rockBaseByCliff`) samples the cliff the terrain draws where it stands (zone `ground.cliff` overrides included, so it is its zone's stone, or the sea cliff / butte it leans on) and wears that slice; this table wins over a rule's `rockBase` / `rockBaseByCliff`. Key "*" is the fallback. The slice should be the cliff's own tile (the zone's rock texture or its cliff tile at the 40 texels/m standard): `worldgen rock-skins` measures the tone of each. Same meshes, one material, one batch per model. Omit for the legacy per-rule bases. Written by `worldgen init` / `zone-textures`.

oceanFloor.description: Ground height far out to sea, well below seaLevel so open water is unmistakably water. Keep it above `minY` or the sea bed falls through the world's solid floor.

landFloor.description: Metres above seaLevel that the INTERIOR of a landmass is held at or above. Above 0 this switches the continent from a height blend to a shore PROFILE: the ground rises from oceanFloor to this floor across the coast band and the terrain's own relief fades in on top of it, so the coastline is exactly the warped outline of the continent and nowhere else. That is what keeps the ocean from bleeding into every inland dip — with the interior held above the sea, standing water inland is only ever a LAKE at its own level. 0 = the legacy blend (inland hollows below seaLevel fill with ocean).

shelf.description: Where in the coast band (0 = open sea, 1 = inland) the shoreline sits when `landFloor` is set. Lower = more of the band is beach and shallows.

limit.description: THE WORLD BOUNDARY: distance from the origin beyond which everything is open ocean at oceanFloor, whatever the continents say. Streaming skips cells past it, the ocean plane is sized to it, and nothing is placed beyond it. Omit for no hard edge.

limitFalloff.description: Metres over which land is pulled under approaching `limit`.

center.description: World-space XZ centre of the landmass.

radius.description: Distance from the centre that is solidly inland — the terrain here is whatever the noise bands make it.

falloff.description: Width of the band over which land descends to the ocean floor. The coastline sits inside it, so a WIDE falloff gives beaches and shallow bays and a narrow one gives sea cliffs. Mountains caught in this band are compressed rather than clipped, which is what puts lowlands around the rim instead of peaks meeting the water.

warp.description: Coastline raggedness as a fraction of `falloff`: 0 is a clean arc, ~0.6 gives peninsulas, headlands and bays. Above 1 the coast breaks into islands.

warpScale.description: Metres per lobe of coastline wobble. Small values fray the coast into inlets; large ones bend the whole landmass.

coastVariation.description: How much `falloff` varies around the coast, as a fraction. 0.6 means some stretches of shore descend over 40% of the band (steep: headlands and sea cliffs) and others over 160% (gentle: beaches and shallow bays). This is what gives one island a beach on one side and cliffs on the other.

coastVariationScale.description: Metres per cycle of the falloff variation — how long a stretch of cliff or beach coast is.

lobes.description: Extra discs [dx, dz, radius], relative to `center`, smoothly UNIONED with the main one. This is what stops a continent being a circle: two or three lobes make a crescent, an L, a landmass with a peninsula and a gulf. Each lobe still gives an exact distance to its shore, so the shore profile and the land floor hold everywhere.

lobeBlend.description: Metres over which lobes merge into one another instead of meeting at a crease. Wider = softer bays where they join.

frequency.description: Cycles per world unit. 0.0008 = continents, 0.01 = hills, 0.08 = rocks.

amplitude.description: World units this band contributes (ridged bands run 0..amplitude, others +/-amplitude).

ridged.description: Sharp crests, flat valleys — the difference between rolling hills and a mountain range.

seed.description: Added to the world seed so two identically-tuned bands still differ.

erosion.description: Slope-weighted octaves: fine detail is damped where the band is already steep, so valleys come out smooth and walkable while ridgelines stay crisp. This is the single biggest lever against terrain that reads as jagged noise — plain fBm puts the same 30 m crinkle on every slope in the world. 0.3-0.6 on the mountain band; costs ~40% more per octave (derivative noise).

crest.description: Ridged bands only: round the crests. The ridged fold puts a knife-edge crease at every ridgeline and summit of every octave, and the voxel mesh renders each one as a corner it cannot smooth — the 'cliffs that come to a sharp edge at the top'. 0 (default) keeps the crease; 0.2 rounds each crest over about a fifth of the band's swing without moving the summit line. Free.

cliff.description: How much steeper the land gets at the waterline where the coast noise says 'rugged'. 0 makes every shore a beach, which is the failure this fixes: a height-band beach rule applied to a uniformly gentle coastline rings the entire world in one unbroken strip of sand.

band.description: World units above and below sea level the steepening reaches. Roughly the height of the headlands.

frequency.description: How often the coast alternates between cliff and cove.

amplitude.description: World units of dune crest. 0 disables the band entirely, and with it the extra climate lookup per column.

stretch.description: Elongation across the prevailing wind. 1 is lumps; 3-4 is the long parallel ridges that read as sand.

angle.description: Wind direction in radians — the axis the ridges run along.

amplitude.description: World units of table height. 0 disables the band.

steps.description: Strata per table: each is a riser and a tread.

sharpness.description: How square the risers are. 0 is a smooth dome.

height.description: The highest the ground can be, asymptotically. Peaks approach it and never reach it.

softness.description: Metres below `height` at which the compression begins. Wider = gentler summits.

variation.description: Opt-in. Metres the ceiling `height` wanders up and down with low-frequency noise, so the summit line is not one altitude: a few ranges stand above the rest instead of every big peak converging on the same flattened top. Keep `height + variation` under `maxY`. Omit = one flat ceiling.

variationFrequency.description: Frequency (1/m) of the ceiling wander. Default 0.00035 (~3 km): whole ranges rise and fall, not single peaks.

variationSeed.description: Seed of the ceiling wander. Default 1931.

step.description: Metres of altitude per terrace — the height of one riser, and roughly the height of one cliff band.

sharpness.description: How square the riser is. 0 leaves the slope untouched; 0.72 spends ~28% of each band's altitude on the riser and flattens the rest into a tread. Past ~0.9 the riser is vertical enough that the voxel lattice, not this number, is what limits it.

strength.description: How much of the terraced profile to blend in where the mask is full. Below 1 the risers soften back toward the raw slope.

rounding.description: Fraction of each riser's height spent easing into the tread at its top and foot, instead of meeting it at a crease. 0 is the raw clamp — a riser that hits the tread at a corner, which the mesh renders as a knife edge along every cliff top. 0.25 rounds the crest and the foot over a quarter of the riser each while the middle half stays as sheer as `sharpness` asks.

minBands.description: How many `step` bands of mountain relief a place must have before it is terraced at all, fading in over the next 1.4 bands. This is what keeps cliffs ON MOUNTAINS: without it the edge of the mountain band — a hillock with one band's worth of height — gets a single enormous step, which reads far harsher than the mountain itself does because there is no mountain around it to explain it, and it is visible from a long way off.

mask.description: WHERE the terracing happens. Without this every mountain in the world is terraced from base to summit and reads as a ziggurat, which is not what a mountain range looks like — a range is mostly smooth flank with cliff bands breaking out of it here and there. Widen the start..end gap for cliffs that fade in; raise `start` for rarer, more dramatic ones.

jitter.description: Metres the band boundaries wander from place to place. Without it every terrace in the world is a perfectly level contour ring at the same altitude, which reads as a contour map rather than as rock.

frequency.description: Cycles per world unit. 0.0012 is a cliff band a few hundred metres across.

start.description: Mask value at which terracing begins to appear.

end.description: Mask value at which it is in full.

offset.description: Musgrave's offset: the ridge height each octave folds about. 1 = classic.

gain.description: How strongly a ridge's own height lets the next octave add detail (detail on crests, calm valleys).

H.description: Spectral exponent: octave weight falls as lacunarity^(-i*H). Higher = smoother.

rotate.description: Radians each octave's lattice is turned, so no octave lines up with another (no grid alignment).

angle.description: Default range direction, radians (anchor `landform.rangeAngle` overrides per anchor).

stretch.description: Ranges are this many times longer than wide along their direction (noise and mask).

warp.description: Metres of a large, low-frequency domain warp that bends ranges so they wander instead of running ruler-straight.

strength.description: World units the surface can bulge horizontally. 0 = a pure heightfield.

slopeStart.description: Only steep ground gets overhangs — flat fields must stay walkable.

__schema69.description: Steepness (sin of the slope angle, over a wide stencil) where ground starts turning into planar rock. 0.6 is 37 degrees.

__schema71.description: Steepness where the planar rock is in full. 0.82 is 55 degrees.

__schema73.description: Fraction of `terrain.overhang`'s fBm bulge removed where planar rock is in full. The bulge is the 'smeared wall' look; 1 replaces it outright.

__schema75.description: Tilted strata: the layer planes and the per-band offsets that turn a riser into ledges, set-backs and lips.

thickness.description: Metres per stratum band, measured along the layer normal. Keep it at least ~4 voxels so each band can hold its own ledge and lip: a feature thinner than a voxel makes the QEF fold triangles over (measured: 0.1% of the area at 5 m on 2 m voxels, 0.01% at 8 m).

dip.description: Radians the layer planes tilt from horizontal. 0 = level ledges (contour-map look); 0.1-0.3 reads as bedded rock.

azimuth.description: Radians: the compass direction the strata dip toward.

offset.description: Metres a band can stand out from the face: each band draws its own push in [0, offset] from a hash, so neighbouring bands make ledges and set-backs.

lip.description: Extra metres the TOP of each band juts out: a crisp overhanging lip with a planar underside. 0 = no lips.

lipHeight.description: Fraction of the band's thickness the lip occupies.

ramp.description: Metres over which one band's push hands over to the next. Short = a sharper ledge edge, but keep it near the voxel size: below it DC folds triangles over the ramp.

__schema84.description: Faceted faces: a 3D Voronoi over the cliff band, one tilted plane per cell, planar grooves between.

size.description: Metres between Voronoi sites: the typical facet width. Keep it at several voxels or the facets alias.

depth.description: Metres a facet stands proud of the face at most. 0 = no facets.

groove.description: Slope of the V-groove flanks between facets (push per metre of distance to the cell border). Lower = wider, shallower joints.

tilt.description: How far each facet's plane tilts off the face (push per metre across the facet).

jitter.description: How far each site wanders inside its grid cell (0 = a regular grid of facets).

__schema91.description: How steep ground is rebuilt. 'warp' (v1): the heightfield's own slope, pushed sideways by strata and facets — a rough steep hillside. 'terrace' (v2): vertical WALLS — flat treads at quantized heights, risers made of big planes (one per Voronoi cell), hard lip and foot, chimney cracks, strata ledges. Use 'terrace' for cliffs.

__schema93.description: The 'terrace' profile's walls: riser height, wall planes, chimneys and lips.

step.description: Typical riser height in metres; the sequence mixes dominant walls and small steps around it (see dominant). Each tread is flat at its level.

levelJitter.description: How far the tread levels wander (smoothly, over ~140 m), as a fraction of the step, so walls do not share one set of altitudes.

cell.description: Metres between the 2D Voronoi sites: the width of one flat plane of wall. Keep it 6-20 m (several voxels).

jitter.description: How far each site wanders in its grid cell (0 = a regular grid of wall planes).

crackRate.description: Share of plane-to-plane joints that open into a chimney.

crackDepth.description: Metres a chimney cuts back into the wall at its joint.

crackWidth.description: Half-width in metres of a chimney's V at the face.

lip.description: Metres the top of every riser juts out: the overhanging lip under the tread edge.

lipHeight.description: Metres below the tread the lip starts.

dominant.description: Share of risers that are DOMINANT walls (0.75-1.65 x step tall); the rest are small steps (0.22-0.47 x step).

pinchStart.description: Noise level above which a tread pinches out (its riser comes forward to the one below): higher = more continuous rings, lower = more single tall faces.

pinchScale.description: Metres per cycle of the pinch noise: how long a tread runs before it ends.

talus.description: Scree apron height at a riser's foot, as a fraction of that riser's height (37-degree slope, varied by noise). 0 = none.

jog.description: Metres a wall plane may stand off the smooth contour. The joint between two planes is at most twice this: bigger = blockier, smaller = a smoother plan.

lipRamp.description: Metres over which the lip's underside slopes out (near the voxel size: thinner folds triangles).

__schema110.description: Metres of LOCAL RELIEF (the height range within +-16 m, read on an 8 m lattice) below which steep ground stays smooth: planar rock fades in between 0.6x and 1x this. Keeps a small steep hill from turning into one cubic block (a 26 m riser on a 20 m knoll). 0 = no relief test (every steep column qualifies).

__schema112.description: Relief (metres) at which wall planes jog in full. Between minRelief and this the plane jog and step-back shrink, so a modest hill gets a smoother plan instead of castle blocks. Default 2.5x minRelief; ignored when minRelief is 0.

__schema114.description: Metres from the nearest river, lake, road or town edge (field.featureClearance) over which planar rock fades in: none inside the first, full past the second. Keeps channels, falls, roads and towns on the ground they were solved and crafted on (13 of proving's 14 falls stand on cliff-mask ground), and the water sheet clipped by the heightfield it was built for. [0, 0] = no fade.

__schema116.description: voxelWorld.mesher 'auto': a cell is meshed by dual contouring when any planar mask lies within the cell plus this many metres, by marching cubes otherwise. The margin is what puts every MC/DC border on smooth ground: at 0 the border can fall inside the cliff band and open holes; 8 m (4 voxels) keeps the field on both sides unaltered.

__schema118.description: Metres over which one zone's cliff look hands over to the next (region entries). Narrower than zoneGround.band on purpose: zone borders follow ridges and cliffs, and inside the band both looks are evaluated (measured: the 150 m ground band made cliff chunks ~1.7x dearer; a cliff 12 m from a border still pays ~1.4x at 40 m).

__schema120.description: Per-zone variation: each entry overrides riser height, plane size, pinch, strata, strength or relief for one REGION (recipe.regions id, blended across zoneGround.band) or one climate ANCHOR (blended by zone membership). A region entry wins over an anchor entry. 'terrace' profile only. Empty = one look everywhere.

items.description: One zone's planar-cliff look. Set exactly one of `region` / `anchor`.

__schema122.description: recipe.regions id this entry applies to (blended across zoneGround.band).

__schema124.description: climate.zones.anchors id this entry applies to (blended by zone membership).

__schema126.description: Multiplies the cliff mask here: 0 = no planar rock in this zone, 1 = full.

offset.description: Metres a band can stand out.

lip.description: Extra metres a band's top juts out.

ramp.description: Metres a band hands over in.

jog.description: Metres a wall plane may stand off the smooth contour.

crackRate.description: Share of joints that open into chimneys.

__schema157.description: OPT-IN, 'terrace' profile: waterfalls, plunge bowls, gorges and banks as DC rock instead of fading rock out near water (featureClearance still keeps the terrace cliffs off them). Absent = unchanged, byte for byte.

__schema158.description: At every waterfall, a hard vertical wall ON the lip line (the line that already decides the carve, the water, the rims and the chunk cut): upstream of it the ground is the upper bed and its banks carried right to the line, past it the plunge pool's floor carried right back to it, so the curtain drops over a sheer face.

__schema160.description: Metres a wall's foot (the rock shelf it stands on) stands over the water beside it. Above the water, so the shoreline stays where the carve put it.

__schema162.description: Sheer walls the plunge bowl's sides climb in, from the pool to the upper water (1 = one wall the height of the drop).

__schema164.description: Metres per bench of the stepped gorge below a fall.

__schema166.description: Gorge (stepped walls) length as a multiple of the drop, before it eases to the banks; capped inside the fall's band.

__schema168.description: Share of a bench a wall may stand forward of its tread's contour (rock built up to the tread level). 0 = purely cut: widest shelves at each wall's foot.

__schema170.description: Benches the bank walls climb in (each `banks` metres): 1 = one low wall, 3+ = a stepped canyon where a river runs deep in cliff country.

__schema172.description: Height (metres) of the low rock walls a river or lake gets where it cuts through cliff country (where the cliff mask would be, before featureClearance). 0 = none.

__schema174.description: Metres from the bank's foot over which the bank walls fade out (full inside the first).

__schema177.description: Name of this stretch (tools and logs).

__schema179.description: recipe.regions id: the stretch is that zone's coast, plus `reach` metres outside its polygon so the foot, platform and stacks offshore are included. Set this or `along` (both = their overlap).

__schema181.description: [x, z] polyline drawn along the coast: the stretch is everything within `reach` metres of it. The usual way to pick one stretch of a zone's coast.

__schema184.description: Metres from `along` (or outside the region) the profile holds in full. Cover the top's inland join (`edge` + `inland`) and the stacks offshore.

__schema186.description: Metres over which the stretch hands back to the ordinary coast: along the coast the wall lowers to a bluff over this run and ends.

__schema188.description: [min, max] metres of the cliff top over sea level, wandering along the coast (the Cliffs of Moher run 120-214 m).

__schema191.description: Metres per cycle of the cliff-top height wander.

__schema193.description: Metres the flat top runs inland from the lip before it starts to join the natural land.

__schema195.description: Metres over which the top joins the natural ground inland: a long, gentle back-slope.

__schema197.description: Metres of gentle relief on the cliff top (0 = a level table).

__schema199.description: The wall's plan: headlands and bays, built of flat planes.

amplitude.description: Metres the wall line moves off the natural coastline: where the noise is positive a headland is built out to sea, where negative a bay is cut in. Keep amplitude / scale under ~0.1, or the line folds back on itself into thin spits.

scale.description: Metres per headland-and-bay cycle.

cell.description: Metres per flat plane of wall (one Voronoi cell); neighbouring planes meet at a joint.

jog.description: Metres a wall plane may stand off the smooth line (keep it <= 5: the heightfield and the planar wall must stay within a few metres).

__schema205.description: Horizontal strata in the wall (planar path only: marching cubes rounds them away).

thickness.description: Metres per horizontal band (shale/sandstone layers). At least ~4 voxels.

offset.description: Metres a band can stand out of the wall: neighbouring bands make ledges and set-backs.

lip.description: Extra metres the top of each band juts out (a ledge with a planar underside).

lipHeight.description: Fraction of a band the lip occupies.

ramp.description: Metres over which one band hands over to the next (near the voxel size).

dip.description: Radians the bands tilt (0 = dead level).

__schema214.description: The wall's foot: a narrow wave-cut platform, or deep water.

share.description: Share of the stretch with a wave-cut platform at the foot; the rest drops straight into deep water.

width.description: [min, max] metres of platform out from the wall.

level.description: [min, max] metres of the platform over sea level: a little under it is awash (foam, breakers), a little over is a dry boulder shelf.

scale.description: Metres per cycle of the platform/deep-water noise.

__schema222.description: Metres of water at the wall's foot where there is no platform.

__schema224.description: Sea stacks and arches offshore. density 0 = none.

cell.description: Metres per stack site (a jittered grid).

density.description: Share of sites holding a stack (only sites in the `offshore` band count).

offshore.description: [min, max] metres off the wall a stack may stand.

radius.description: [min, max] metres from a stack's centre to its faces at the top.

height.description: [min, max] stack top as a fraction of the cliff top's height over the sea.

taper.description: Metres of radius a stack gains per metre down from its top (a sea stack is broader at the waterline).

irregular.description: How far each face stands in or out of the regular prism, as a fraction of the radius.

arch.description: Share of stacks near the wall (18-70 m off it) joined to it by a fin with an arch through it.

shape.description: OPT-IN stack shape language (absent = the plain faceted prism, byte for byte): chamfered/notched or fin plans, set-backs, thin ledges, a cap band with an overhanging lip and a recess, a wave-cut notch and a boulder apron. Seed-stable per stack; every stack keeps its site, radius and top. The top stays flat (walkable: rope-bridge anchors).

__schema239.description: Plan of every stack: 'chamfer' = a rectangle with each corner chamfered by its own amount and notches bitten in (Moher), 'fin' = a thin blade, long and narrow (Pyke spires), 'mixed' = a share `fins` of fins. Straight segments, never a circle.

__schema241.description: With plan 'mixed': share of stacks that are fins.

__schema243.description: [min, max] long-axis / short-axis ratio of a chamfered plan (area kept: half-axes radius x sqrt(e) and radius / sqrt(e)).

__schema246.description: [min, max] the same ratio for a fin.

__schema249.description: [min, max] notches bitten into a chamfered plan's long edges (fins get none).

__schema252.description: [min, max] set-backs up the wall: the stack narrows in steps going up, each a shelf (girth variation). 0 = one straight wall.

__schema255.description: [min, max] metres each set-back steps in.

__schema258.description: [min, max] thin ledges (0.7 m out, 2.2 m thick) on the wall between the foot and the cap band, at uneven heights.

__schema261.description: Share of the stretch's even strata push kept on the stacks (1 = the wall's stripes in full: they read as stacked crates).

__schema263.description: [min, max] cap band thickness as a fraction of the stack's height over the sea.

__schema266.description: [min, max] metres the cap band stands out over the wall under it (the overhanging lip; a further 0.6 m weathered edge on its top 2 m).

__schema269.description: Metres the band just under the cap is cut in (the recess that makes the lip read).

__schema271.description: The wave-cut notch at the waterline, just over the boulder apron.

depth.description: [min, max] metres the wave-cut notch bites into the foot of the wall.

height.description: [min, max] metres tall the notch is.

__schema277.description: Boulder/talus apron round the foot. reach [0, 0] = none.

reach.description: [min, max] metres the boulder apron reaches out from the foot of the wall.

height.description: [min, max] metres over the sea the apron stands at the wall (concave, down to the sea floor at its reach).

boulders.description: Metres of blocky boulder relief on the apron.

__schema284.description: OPT-IN: the stretch's tops take the zone's turf. Stacks stand offshore, outside the zone polygon, so without this their tops (and the lip band, where zone ground fades over its border band) fall back to the base palette's dry grass and dirt.

zone.description: recipe.regions id whose ground roles (regions[].ground: grass, ground, cliff...) paint the whole stretch, stacks offshore included. Default: the stretch's `region`.

surface.description: A palette surface (e.g. the zone's `rockCap.layer` turf) laid over the flat tops of the cliff and the stacks.

amount.description: How much of the zone's ground (and `surface`) the stretch takes.

__schema289.description: Metres from a town, road, river, lake or big fill over which the profile fades in (none inside the first, full past the second): coastal paths and towns keep their ground. POIs and height patches are NOT cleared: a patch levels its own footprint over the finished wall and stacks.

__schema293.description: One field of buttes and mesas on a flat plain.

__schema294.description: Name of this field (tools and logs).

__schema299.description: Metres of flat plain round the centre (monuments stand inside it, clear of its edge).

__schema301.description: Metres over which the plain hands back to the natural ground.

__schema304.description: Metres of gentle relief left on the plain.

__schema306.description: Metres per monument site (a jittered grid): monuments stand far apart with long sightlines between.

__schema308.description: Share of sites holding a monument.

__schema310.description: Long, wide tables with notched, bitten edges.

weight.description: Share of monuments of this kind (normalised across the three).

length.description: [min, max] metres along the long axis of the wall's plan (at the cap).

height.description: [min, max] metres of the cap over the plain (apron included).

__schema319.description: Blocky rectangles and lozenges, taller than the apron is wide.

weight.description: Share of monuments of this kind (normalised across the three).

length.description: [min, max] metres along the long axis of the wall's plan (at the cap).

height.description: [min, max] metres of the cap over the plain (apron included).

__schema328.description: Thin fins, flat in one direction; they taper and some lean.

weight.description: Share of monuments of this kind (normalised across the three).

length.description: [min, max] metres along the long axis of the wall's plan (at the cap).

height.description: [min, max] metres of the cap over the plain (apron included).

__schema337.description: Share of buttes that keep a spire standing just beside them.

__schema339.description: [min, max] notches bitten into a mesa's edges (buttes get up to one).

__schema342.description: [min, max] talus apron height as a fraction of the monument's height. The wall above it is the cap rock.

__schema345.description: [min, max] how far the apron reaches out from the wall, as a fraction of the wall's width (1 = the apron's foot is twice the wall's width overall).

__schema348.description: Most a spire leans (metres sideways per metre up); some stand straight.

__schema350.description: [min, max] cap band thickness as a fraction of the sheer wall.

__schema353.description: Metres from a town, road, river or lake over which the plain fades in; monuments stand only where it is full. (POIs are not avoided: a site picked on the old ground is re-picked on the plain.)

slopeStart.description: Steepness at which the tunnel network may start reaching the surface.

slopeEnd.description: Steepness at which it fully may.

minDepth.description: The `minDepth` that applies on fully steep ground. NEGATIVE means tunnels are allowed to push past the surface, which is what actually cuts an opening; at 0 they only ever kiss it.

warp.description: World units the climate field is domain-warped by before it is read. This is the LARGE-scale raggedness: it makes a desert reach a peninsula into the meadow instead of ending on a smooth curve.

strength.description: Fine noise (in the climate's own 0..1 units) added to temperature and moisture. This is the SMALL-scale raggedness: it breaks the last few metres of every border into speckle, so the transition is a scatter of blighted ground in the grass rather than a line.

heightJitter.description: World units of noise added to the ground height that HEIGHT windows are tested against — the same trick for the snowline and the beach, which are height-driven rather than climate-driven.

size.description: Mean zone diameter in metres. A region should take minutes to cross, not seconds.

jitter.description: How far each zone's site wanders from its grid point. 0 is a checkerboard.

warp.description: Metres the zone borders are pushed around by noise, so they read as coastlines rather than as cell walls.

border.description: Width of the blend between two zones, in metres. Biome rules still see a gradient across it.

strength.description: How strongly zones sort by latitude. 0 = anchors are picked by weight alone.

scale.description: Metres from the cold pole to the hot one, centred on the origin along `axis`.

marsh.description: Opt-in tuning for every anchor's `waterTable`. Omit for the defaults.

seed.description: Added to the world seed for the zone layout alone, so the layout can be re-rolled without moving a single hill. Which anchor a zone gets is a draw, and a small world can draw no desert at all: a generator that needs every kind of place can sweep this until each anchor covers real land.

weight.description: How often zones pick this anchor, relative to the others.

latitude.description: Preferred latitude band, 0 = the cold pole, 1 = the hot pole (see `climate.zones.latitude`). A zone picks anchors by weight TIMES how close its own latitude is to this, so tundra collects at one end of the world and jungle at the other instead of both being sprinkled everywhere. Omit = anywhere.

relief.description: Multiplies the MOUNTAIN band here. 1 = a mountain zone; 0 = no peaks at all.

hills.description: Multiplies the hills band. 0 = a plain; 1.5 = broken country.

dunes.description: Multiplies the dune band (`terrain.dunes`) here. 1 = a dune sea.

mesas.description: Multiplies the mesa band (`terrain.mesas`) here. 1 = badlands: terraced tables and buttes.

flatten.description: Pulls the continent band down toward the land floor. 1 = a low, level plain hugging the waterline — swamp ground.

waterTable.description: Opt-in WATER TABLE: metres above the land floor (`seaLevel + bounds.landFloor`) at which this zone holds standing water. With it, `flatten` pulls the ground to this level plus `hummocks` noise instead of to the dry floor, and wherever the ground is under the table a shallow still sheet (kind "marsh", `marshMaterial`) covers it — clipped against the terrain like lakes and rivers, reported by `waterSurface`/`waterY`, so cover, scatter and swimming see it. The ground rises into a low dry rim where the zone ends and along wet rivers, so a sheet never ends in the air. Omit = a dry flattened zone.

hummocks.description: Metres of island/pool relief around `waterTable` (default 1): ground ranges about ±this, so islands and pools mix roughly half and half. Pools are soft-capped at `climate.zones.marsh.maxDepth` deep. Only read with `waterTable`.

landform.description: LANDFORM PROFILE (opt-in): the shape of ground here as a weighted mix of families — rolling, hummocky, drumlin, karst, cuesta, wetland, mesa — each with its own frequency/amplitude/sharpness, plus per-anchor cliff strength and range direction. Replaces the anchor's `hills` and `mesas` gains (relief, dunes, flatten and waterTable still apply). Omit = the gains as before, byte-identical.

__schema389.description: ROLLING: the world's own hills band (today's look). With a `landform`, this replaces the anchor's `hills` gain.

amplitude.description: Multiplier on the world's hills band (`terrain.hills`). 1 = today's rolling country.

__schema391.description: Share of this family in the mix (0 = off, 1 = full amplitude).

__schema393.description: HUMMOCKY: a jumble of small rounded knobs and kettle hollows (moraine, broken heath).

amplitude.description: Metres from hollow to knob top.

sharpness.description: 0 = soft swells; 1 = tight knobs with creased hollows between (billowed noise).

__schema398.description: DRUMLIN: stretched elliptical whalebacks all aligned to one grain (glaciated lowland).

frequency.description: 1/m across the grain; 0.005 = whalebacks ~200 m apart.

amplitude.description: Metres a drumlin stands over the ground between them.

sharpness.description: 0 = gentle swells; 1 = discrete flat-topped whalebacks with level ground between.

stretch.description: Length/width of each hill along the grain.

angle.description: Grain direction in radians. Default `terrain.dunes.angle` (the world's wind frame).

__schema405.description: KARST: cellular sinkholes (dolines) and steep limestone towers on a jittered grid.

frequency.description: 1/m; 0.007 = one sinkhole or tower per ~140 m cell.

amplitude.description: Metres: pit depth; a tower stands 1.6x this.

sharpness.description: How sheer the tower walls are (0 = domes, 1 = near-vertical).

towers.description: Share of cells that raise a tower instead of sinking a pit.

density.description: Share of cells that hold anything at all.

__schema412.description: CUESTA: tilted strata — long gentle dip slopes ending in one-sided scarps, ledged by terrace().

frequency.description: 1/m along the dip; 0.0028 = one scarp every ~360 m.

sharpness.description: How short (steep) the scarp face is against the long dip slope.

steps.description: Strata ledges on each dip slope (terrace()); 1 = a smooth dip slope.

angle.description: Dip direction, radians: scarps face the opposite way.

__schema419.description: WETLAND: a monotone pull of the ground down onto a low basin level (weight = how far). Dry ground unless the anchor also has a `waterTable`, which stays the way to hold standing water.

level.description: Metres over the land floor the ground is pulled toward.

__schema423.description: MESA: terraced tables and buttes (own band). With a `landform`, this replaces the anchor's `mesas` gain.

__schema426.description: Strength of `terrain.cliffs` terracing on this anchor's mountains (0..1). Any anchor setting it switches terracing on for the world even with `terrain.cliffs.enabled` false; anchors that omit it then get 0 (or 1 when `enabled` is true). Set it only where the profile wants scarps.

__schema428.description: Ranges run along this direction (radians) here, with `terrain.ridgedMultifractal` on. Default its `angle`.

__schema430.description: River VALLEY: around every authored river within this anchor, the ground is lowered toward a floor over the river's water surface across a band `width` channel widths wide — read from the solved beds before the channel cut, so the channel then sits in a valley rather than a slot. Weighted by zone membership.

shape.description: U: glacial trough (flat floor, steep walls) for cold anchors. V: a hill valley. flat: a lowland floodplain with a gentle rise at its edge.

width.description: Valley width as a multiple of the river's channel width.

depth.description: Most metres the valley lowers the ground (it never goes under the floodplain level).

floor.description: Metres the valley floor stands over the river's water surface.

__schema435.description: This profile's weight in the per-zone draw against `variants`.

__schema437.description: Alternative profiles: each Voronoi zone site of this anchor draws ONE of [this profile, ...variants] by weight (a stable hash), so two zones of the same anchor can have different silhouettes. Variants do not nest.

frequency.description: Frequency (1/m) of the hummock/pool noise. Default 0.018 (~55 m from one island to the next).

maxDepth.description: Soft cap on pool depth under the table, m. Default 1.1: marsh water is wading water, never a lake.

rim.description: Metres over the table the dry rim stands where a marsh ends (zone edge, coast, wet river bank). Default 0.4.

wetBias.description: Shifts the hummock noise down (>0, wetter) or up (<0, drier) by this many `hummocks` x 1.8 m, so more or less of a marsh sits under its table. Default 0 (about half wet in a marsh's heart; borders and levees are drier). ~0.25 brings a whole swamp toward half wet.

seed.description: Seed of the hummock noise. Default 2741.

name.description: Human/AI-facing label: grass, sand, rock, snow.

color.description: Tint, and the whole appearance until a texture is supplied.

map.description: Texture asset id (assets/textures/) — albedo, projected triplanar.

role.description: Which ground ROLE this base surface fills, so a zone can restyle it (`regions[].ground`): inside a zone that overrides the role, this surface's weight moves to the zone's surface, blended by zone membership. Tag every surface that plays the role (grass AND dry grass are both `grass`). Leave a zone's own override surfaces untagged: they are reached through the zone, never remapped themselves.

blend.description: Softness of the temperature/moisture/slope window edges, in those windows' own 0..1 units.

heightBlend.description: Softness of the `height` window edges, in WORLD UNITS — height is the one window measured in metres, so it needs its own blend or a 0.08 softness makes a razor edge across a hillside.

weight.description: Relative pull where several rules match equally.

cliffStart.description: Steepness at which `cliff` starts replacing `surface`, in sin(angle). 0.57 is 35 degrees, roughly the angle of repose: past it soil and sand stop staying put, which is why cover gives way to rock there. These are authored against `slope()` units, so anything that measures steepness differently silently means a different ANGLE here.

cliffEnd.description: Steepness at which `cliff` fully replaces `surface`. 0.82 is 55 degrees.

tint.description: Multiplied over the blended surface color — cheap per-biome variation.

zones.description: Zone anchor ids (`climate.zones.anchors[].id`) this rule belongs to. The rule's membership is multiplied by the blended zone weight, so a rule listed here exists ONLY inside those zones — which is how a blighted region and a badland can both be hot-and-dry without fighting over the same climate corner. Omit for a rule that applies wherever its climate/height/slope windows say.

label.description: Does this rule NAME the place? Cover-only rules — a crag rule that paints bare rock on steep ground in every biome — must set false. `biome().id` is the strongest rule by membership, and everything that asks 'which biome is this' reads it: scatter's `biomes` filter above all. A cover rule left labelling quietly renames every slope in the world, and the pines filtered to "meadow" stop appearing on hills.

surface.description: Palette surface NAME to lay down (matched case-insensitively).

biomes.description: Biome ids this may appear in; empty = anywhere. The gate is the biome's blended membership, so patches fade out across a border instead of stopping at it.

frequency.description: Cycles per world unit. 0.02 ~ 50 m blotches.

threshold.description: Noise level (-1..1) at which the patch starts. Higher = rarer, smaller patches.

blend.description: Noise range over which it fades in. Small = hard-edged scabs, large = soft mottling.

strength.description: How completely the patch replaces the ground under it at full mask. 1 = bare.

slope.description: Restrict to a steepness window — dirt worn through on flat ground, scree only on slopes.

mode.description: Two different motions, not one with a knob. `sway` BENDS the whole plant from a base pinned to the ground - displacement grows with height, so it leans as one piece. That is a bush or a reed. `ripple` shivers each leaf card on the spot with NO net lean, phase varying across the model so cards move against each other: the canopy shimmers while the tree stands still, which is what real timber does in a light wind. Putting `sway` on a tree is the classic mistake - the trunk swings like a blade of grass and the model reads as rubber.

strength.description: Peak displacement in METRES of world space, not a fraction of the model. A ripple wants 0.02-0.06; a bush sway 0.08-0.2.

canopy.description: `ripple` only: fraction of the model height where the canopy starts. Everything below is held perfectly still, which is how the trunk stays out of it. It is a HEIGHT test rather than a 'is this the leaf material' test on purpose: Blockbench exports every material as alphaMode MASK, so a cutout test catches the trunk too (the same trap `foliageNormals` documents), while height does not care where the trunk sits horizontally.

materials.description: Only move materials whose NAME, or whose colour texture's name, contains one of these (case-insensitive, COMMA-SEPARATED) — `leaves` for a model whose leaf texture is called Leaves, `leaves,bush` for one rule that covers a whole shelf of props whatever each model calls its own foliage sheet. The rest of the model stands still and the `canopy` height test is skipped, so the trunk stays put by NAME rather than by height. Name the texture or material in the DCC tool before export: Blockbench exports a pasted texture as literally 'pasted', which matches nothing, and an unmatched model gets no wind at all (`split-gltf.mjs --texnames` names them after the fact).

frequency.description: Cycles per world unit — the size of one grove. 0.004 ~ 250 m stands, 0.02 ~ 50 m thickets.

threshold.description: Noise level (-1..1) at which the clump starts. Higher = rarer, smaller, further-apart clumps.

blend.description: Noise range over which it fades in. Small = a hard treeline, large = a stand that thins out at its edge.

floor.description: Fraction of the density that survives OUTSIDE the clumps. 0 = real clearings you can walk across; 0.15 = a thinned scatter between the stands, which is what most woodland actually looks like.

seed.description: Added to the world seed, so two rules with identical settings clump in different places.

mode.description: Where on the cliff the props go, from a lattice point on its steep ground. "face": a column down the face (below). "crest": along the TOP edge, leaning out over the drop (`lean` tips OUT here), so a rounded lip reads as a jagged skyline and the zone cap marks it. "foot": a talus apron on the ground below the face, `apron` x the cliff's height deep, the props growing with distance out (scree near, blocks further).

orient.description: Face mode: "lean" = upright, turned out of the face and tipped back by `lean` (menhir-like props). "normal" = the model's UP axis on the face's own 3D normal (a slab or outcrop bedded INTO the face like a rock facet), `embed` then measured along that normal. Use "normal" for the rock kit: two thirds of the model's height sunk. "slope" = the model's UP axis up the face's fall line and its front (+Z) out along the face normal: a tall piece (the kit's `buttress`) lies against the face as a rib running up it, `embed` along the normal.

fit.description: CLIFF-SCALE MASSES: size each piece from the local drop instead of `scale` (which it replaces), so a 50-100 m cliff gets 10-40 m ribs, ledges and crest teeth and an 8 m bank never does. Face mode places the first piece AT the lattice point's own spot on the face (no march from the top, so a big piece stays within its owning cell) and `stack` more below it; crest mode on the lip. Few, big pieces: use a low density.

band.description: Face mode: metres between STRATA. >0 snaps each prop's height to a world level (a multiple of this), so neighbouring columns put their rocks at the same heights and the face reads as bedded layers rather than random boulders. 0 = free heights (the original behaviour).

apron.description: Foot mode: how far out the talus reaches, as a fraction of the cliff's measured height (a 30 m cliff at 0.6 = 18 m).

stack.description: How many props down one column, picked per lattice point. The stack stops early where the face does.

spacing.description: Metres of drop between one prop and the next. Set it under the model's height so they overlap and read as one mass.

spacingJitter.description: How much each step may vary, as a fraction of `spacing`.

embed.description: Depth pushed INTO the face along its inward normal, in MODEL units — it is multiplied by the instance scale, like `yOffset`, so resizing a prop does not leave it hanging off the wall. This is the field that decides whether the prop looks bolted onto the cliff or part of it; roughly a third of the model's depth is a good start.

embedJitter.description: Random variation on `embed`, in the same model units.

lateral.description: Metres each prop may slide sideways along the face, so a column is not a plumb line of rocks.

faceOut.description: How strongly each prop turns to face out of the cliff. 1 = square to the face, 0 = free yaw (the ordinary scatter behaviour).

yawSpread.description: Radians of random yaw either side of the outward direction. This plus `tilt` is what stops a stack looking like one model copy-pasted.

tilt.description: Radians of random tilt off vertical, about a random horizontal axis.

lean.description: Radians the prop tips BACK into the face (negative tips it out). A cliff recedes as it rises, so an upright prop bedded at its base has its top hanging in open air — which is exactly what makes a face read as planted menhirs instead of rock. Roughly `atan(model height / (2 x embed))` cancels it. This is NOT `alignToNormal`: that one lays a prop ONTO a slope, which on a cliff leans it further out.

minDrop.description: The face must fall at least this far below the lattice point for the column to start at all. Guards against decorating every short steep bank in the world.

search.description: Metres to march outward looking for the face at each step's height. Wider catches gentler faces, and it is the per-instance cost knob — but it is also how far a prop can end up from the lattice point that owns it, so keep it WELL under a quarter of `cellSize` or a cell starts emitting props that live in its neighbour and pop when it unloads.

fraction.description: Piece size as a fraction of the LOCAL DROP (the crest-to-foot height measured from the lattice point), picked per piece.

axis.description: Which model dimension the fraction sizes: "height" (a buttress, a crag) or "length" along the face (a ledge band).

scale.description: Instance scales a variant may be stretched over. The kit's body texture is model-space, so the fit picks the VARIANT whose own size needs a scale in this range (several do: a hashed, weighted pick) and clamps the rest. A drop too small for the smallest variant at the low end places nothing.

reach.description: Metres walked up and down the fall line from the lattice point to find the crest and the foot (one height read per 3 m).

at.description: Face mode: where the first piece's foot sits, as a fraction of the drop above the cliff's foot, hashed per lattice point. Set it to dress a WALL from candidates on the gentler ground above and below it (a vertical face has almost no plan area of its own, so a lattice point rarely lands on it): pair it with a low `slopeMin`. Omit = at the lattice point.

overlap.description: Face mode stacks: the next piece down starts this fraction of the piece above's height lower (under 1 = they overlap into one rib).

tint.description: Linear RGB multipliers for materials/textures named Bark/Trunk/Wood and Leaves/Leaf/Foliage/Branch/Bush. [1,1,1] preserves the original texture; other material roles remain unchanged.

weight.description: Relative selection weight; weights are normalized automatically.

multiplier.description: Uniform multiplier of the instance's sampled scale.

model.description: Model asset id of this variant (same kind, same scale class as `model`).

colliderSize.description: This variant's own model-space collider box (base at y = 0, NOT pre-scaled, like `colliderSize`). Omit to use the rule's.

kinds.description: Which shapes this rule makes, weighted. Keep `single` a minority.

members.description: Members per formation (rows and arcs; a cluster/spill uses up to this many around its anchor, a stack 2-3).

gap.description: Edge-to-edge spacing between neighbours, metres: negative = overlapping, up to ~1 m apart. Members touch or nearly.

taper.description: How much smaller the ends of a row/arc and the tucked members of a cluster are than the anchor (0.5 = half).

contour.description: Rows strike ALONG the slope contour (an outcropping band); false = a random strike.

lean.description: Radians: the shared lean of a row about its strike, and the tilt of a stack's leaning member is 0.45 + this.

spill.description: Spill: how far (m) the scree trail runs downhill from the cluster.

memberVariants.description: Models for the NON-anchor members (smaller rocks round a big one); omit to use the rule's own variants. Name models other rules already scatter with the same material and flags, or each new one is a new batch.

fillers.description: A member smaller than this fraction of the anchor is FILLER: no collider and `hlod: false` (culled with the full-render ring), while the anchor and the big members keep both, so the silhouette survives at distance.

kind.description: single: one rock. row: 3-7 along a line or gentle curve sharing a strike and lean, tapering to the ends (an exposed band). cluster: one big rock with smaller ones tucked against its base. stack: a rock leaning on the anchor, or two leaning together (a tent). arc: a broken half-ring (ruins, POIs). spill: a cluster with a scree trail running downhill from it. steps: stepping stones, even-sized and evenly spaced ACROSS a river's current (along the contour elsewhere); a stone the water gate refuses (too deep) leaves a gap.

weight.description: Relative weight among kinds (a stable hash picks one per formation).

mode.description: shore: on lake/sea banks, standing half in the water (denser on steep banks and headlands, sparse on gentle beaches). in: on the bed of shallow lake/sea water, the top breaking the surface. river: in a river's shallow runs (the deep centre stays clear), bigger below waterfalls. marsh: on a marsh's water table, rare.

top.description: in/river/marsh: metres the rock's top must stand above the water surface; the instance is rescaled within the rule's range to fit or dropped. Never a submerged blob.

maxDepth.description: in/river: deepest water (surface minus bed, metres) a rock is placed in.

reach.description: shore: metres from the candidate to look for the water's edge.

steepness.description: shore: how much a steep bank raises the odds (keep = 0.2 + steepness x slope).

waters.description: shore/in: which water's banks or shallows. lake = lakes and the sea (the old behaviour); river = river channels (not their plunge pools); both. A river's shore needs `snap` (its bank is read from the ground, not a lake outline).

snap.description: shore: read the waterline from a grid of water reads precomputed once per cell (`snapStep` m) and move each candidate within `reach` of it ONTO it, so every rock stands at the edge and rows run along it; also what `headland` measures. false keeps the old per-candidate reach probes (lakes and sea only).

snapStep.description: shore + snap: metres between the cell grid's water reads. Coarser is cheaper and blunter.

wade.description: shore + snap: where across the waterline the anchor stands, as a fraction of its footprint radius (+ into the water).

headland.description: shore + snap: odds added where the water wraps round the bank point (a headland, a spit, the outside of a point bar), by how far over half the ground round it is water.

keep.description: Share of the candidates this rule keeps before the bank/bend odds (river mode: of every shallow candidate).

bend.description: river, or shore on river banks: the OUTER bank of a bend, where the current drives into the bank, gets bigger blocks and more of them.

fall.description: river: the plunge pool below a waterfall gets bigger blocks.

turn.description: Radians the channel turns over 50 m at which a reach is a full bend (half of it counts half).

scale.description: Scale multiplier on the outer bank of a full bend.

boost.description: Odds multiplier on the outer bank of a full bend.

radius.description: Metres round a fall's foot that count as its plunge pool.

scale.description: Scale multiplier for rocks there.

only.description: Place this rule ONLY in plunge pools (the blocks below a fall), nowhere else on the river.

texture.description: Billboard texture asset id. With one set, each instance becomes intersecting textured quads (`crossQuads`) with an alpha cutout instead of a procedural triangle blade — which is how you get actual grass tufts, brambles or ferns rather than a coloured wedge. `bladeWidth`/`bladeHeight` are then the quad's world size.

crossQuads.description: Textured layers only: quads per instance, evenly rotated about Y. 1 is a single card and reads flat from the side; 2 is the standard cross and is nearly always right; 3 costs 50% more for a little more volume at close range.

alphaTest.description: Texture alpha below which a fragment is discarded. Cutout, not blending — so no sort order to get wrong.

surfaces.description: Terrain SURFACE names this may grow on (a voxel world's palette: grass, sand, dirt…). Empty = anywhere the host allows. Gating on the surface rather than the biome is what makes it agree with what you can SEE: a worn dirt patch inside a meadow grows no grass, because the ground there is not grass.

minSurface.description: Combined weight those surfaces must reach. 0.5 = the ground mostly reads as one of them; lower spreads a sparse layer over its fringes.

slopeMax.description: Steepest ground it will grow on, as sin(angle) — the same units as a biome's `cliffStart`. 0.7 is 45 degrees.

atlas.description: Textured layers only: `texture` is a PAGE of equal tiles, `columns` x `rows`, tile 0 top-left, row-major. Each instance draws one tile (see `tiles`), so poppies, daisies and lupins are ONE layer and ONE draw call instead of three. Keep a transparent gutter inside every tile: minification mips bleed across tile edges.

tiles.description: Atlas tiles this layer draws, picked per instance. Empty = every tile on the page. Repeat an index to weight it: [0, 0, 0, 1] is three parts tile 0 to one part tile 1.

tilePatch.description: How the tile is picked. 0 = independently per instance (a mixed meadow). > 0 = from smooth world-space noise at this many cycles per metre, so neighbours share a tile and the ground reads as DRIFTS — a patch of poppies beside a patch of daisies. 0.03 ~ 30 m drifts.

cap.description: Textured upright layers only: one extra TILTED card on top of each tuft carrying a top-down view of the flower heads, so a meadow still shows petals when looked down on — crossed upright cards go thin from above. Costs one quad per instance.

orient.description: `upright` = crossed vertical cards (tufts, reeds, flowers). `flat` = one horizontal card lying on the ground or water, yawed per instance — lily pads, duckweed. `bladeWidth` is then its size in both axes.

scaleRange.description: Per-instance size jitter [min, max], a multiplier on bladeWidth/bladeHeight.

biomes.description: Voxel worlds only: biome ids this layer may grow in (the same ids `scatter[].biomes` names). Empty = any. Combine with `surfaces`: the biome says which PLACE (wheat in grassland, not jungle), the surface says which GROUND inside it (not on the dirt path through that grassland).

clump.description: Gather the layer into patches with open ground between — a wheat field, a drift of flowers — instead of an even carpet. `density` stays the PEAK inside a patch. Same model as `scatter[].clump`.

water.description: Voxel worlds only: tie the layer to water. Without this, cover never grows in or under water; with it, the layer grows ONLY where the water rule holds.

id.description: Stable name; the host registers the layer as `cover:<id>`.

note.description: Why this layer exists / where it is meant to read. Ignored by the engine.

tiles.description: Cap tile for each entry of `tiles`, same order (-1 = no cap for that one). The cap is drawn from the SAME page as the body, so put the top-down flower heads on the body's page.

height.description: Where the cap sits, as a fraction of bladeHeight.

size.description: Cap card size in metres (square), before the instance scale.

tilt.description: Degrees the cap leans from horizontal. 0 = lying flat (only seen from above), 90 = another upright card.

frequency.description: Cycles per metre — the size of one patch. 0.02 ~ 50 m fields, 0.08 ~ 12 m drifts.

threshold.description: Noise level (-1..1) at which the patch starts. Higher = rarer, smaller patches.

blend.description: Noise range over which the patch edge fades in.

floor.description: Fraction of the density that survives OUTSIDE the patches. 0 = bare between them.

seed.description: Offsets the noise so two layers patch in different places.

mode.description: `shore` = grow on ground near water, in the band `level` relative to the water line (cattails, reeds). `surface` = float ON the water where the depth is inside `depth` (lily pads, duckweed; use orient flat). `bed` = grow on the lake/river BED under water where the depth is inside `depth` (eelgrass, pondweed).

level.description: `shore` only: ground height relative to the nearest water surface, [min, max] metres. A negative min lets emergent plants stand in the shallows.

reach.description: `shore` only: how far from a point to look for that water, metres.

depth.description: `surface` / `bed`: water depth [min, max] metres the layer floats on or grows under.

kinds.description: Which water counts. `lake` means ANY still inland water — lakes and every still-water kind the world adds; `marsh` alone = only a zone's marsh water table (a zone anchor's `waterTable`), for layers that belong to the bog and not to every lake. Rivers flowing faster than `maxFlow` never carry `surface` layers.

walls.description: Build every stepped town's shelf risers as retaining walls (`features.terraceWalls`, owner = the town) instead of voxel slopes, with the stage's ramps and stairs as wall inserts. Towns tagged `pinned` are never touched.

maxStep.description: With walls on: tallest shelf step (m) a town draws, so every riser fits one kit wall.

id.description: Stable slug, referenced by chat, placement and stories. Never rename one players have seen.

name.description: What players see: 'Ashfall Canyon', 'The Hollow Vale'.

story.description: Two to five sentences: what this place is, why anyone goes there, what is wrong with it. The seed the AI dungeon master grows consequences from; also the tooltip text on the map.

polygon.description: Border in world metres [x, z], clockwise or counter-clockwise, no self-crossing. Follow LANDMARKS a player cannot see across — ridge lines, river centrelines, gorge rims, the coast — never a straight line over open ground: the border is where a server swap can happen, and a swap must not show two worlds.

hub.description: Where an arriving player is placed and the map labels the region — normally a town centre inside the polygon.

landmarks.description: Feature ids inside or bounding the region (towns, rivers, canyons, peaks, pois) — what its borders were drawn on.

level.description: Intended character level band [min, max]; the spawn tables and the story pitch to it.

cap.description: Players per server copy of this region before another copy opens. Omit = the cluster default.

within.description: Id of the region this one is CUT OUT of: wherever this polygon lies inside its parent, this region wins (regionAt prefers the nested zone). How a town is a zone of its own inside the wilderness around it — a simple polygon cannot hold a hole, so the cut-out is declared, not drawn. Never overlaps otherwise.

ground.description: This zone's own ground: ground ROLE -> palette surface NAME (`{ grass: "shelf-grass", paving: "shelf-cobble" }`). Natural roles (grass, ground, cliff, accent) replace the palette surfaces tagged with that role (`surfaces[].role`); `road` and `paving` replace what roads with that `role` paint. Blended by zone membership across `zoneGround.band`, so a border is a gradient. A zone without it renders the base palette. Written by `worldgen zone-textures` from the cast's ground looks; a nested town zone uses its parent's unless it declares its own.

mood.description: Optional look of this zone: tinted sky/haze, sun colour and strength, shadow colour, fog and colour grade. Read by the `zone-mood` builtin, which eases it in over the day/night cycle and under the weather; a zone without one shows the scene's own look, and a nested town zone without one inherits its parent's.

sound.description: Optional sound of this zone: its own ambient bed, spot sounds, music and still-water bed per day/night band. Read by the `soundscape` builtin BEFORE the biome patterns; a place inherits its zone's, a nested town zone its parent's bed and still water.

ambient.description: Ambient particle layers that live in this zone (spores in a bog, ash in burned country). A place inherits its zone's and a nested town zone its parent's (a layer with the same id nearer the point wins). Read by `ambient-particles` on top of its scene `layers` param, so older scenes keep working.

vegetation.description: What grows in this region, over what the biomes choose: allow/deny species, thin or thicken, swap species (dead pines, no palms), lean the trees. Resolved most-specific region first (place > town > zone), field by field. Read by scatter and the cover gate alike; deterministic. Set with `worldgen vegetation --region`.

rockCap.description: This zone's rock cap: every scatter rule that opts in with `cap` wears it here, overriding the rule's own `cap` (auto ground sampling or a fixed layer). The nearest region on the chain place -> zone -> parent that declares one wins. Cosmetic and seed-stable: the same mesh and material everywhere, only the per-rock cap changes.

tags.description: "town" marks a town zone (hub = the town centre, landmarks[0] = its town id); "safe" makes the whole zone a sanctuary; "draft" = placeholder from worldgen zones.

__schema618.description: Colour the sky's ZENITH leans toward, by `amount` (a sickly marsh: #6f8a62; ash country: #6d625c).

__schema620.description: Colour the HORIZON, the fog and the painted horizon band lean toward, by `amount` — the strongest tone-setter, because distance is drawn in it.

__schema621.description: How far `sky` and `haze` go. 0.3 is a hint, 0.6 owns the zone, 1 replaces the world's sky.

__schema623.description: Multiplies the SUN's colour (#ffffff = unchanged; #ffd0a0 = a hot amber zone; #c8d8c0 = sickly).

__schema624.description: Multiplies the sun's intensity. Below 1 for an oppressive zone.

__schema626.description: Multiplies the ambient fill and sky light — the colour SHADOWS take (#c0d0ff = cold blue shadow; #d0e8b0 = green murk).

__schema627.description: Multiplies the fog density, on top of whatever the weather is doing.

__schema629.description: Multiplies the scene's ground mist (sky.fog.mist.amount — needs it enabled there). 2-3 drowns a marsh; 0 clears it.

__schema631.description: Multiplies postfx.grade saturation (needs the scene's grade enabled). 0.7 = drained; 1.2 = lush.

__schema633.description: Multiplies postfx.grade contrast (needs the scene's grade enabled).

__schema635.description: Added to postfx.grade temperature: + warm, - cold (needs the scene's grade enabled).

__schema637.description: Ground-relative mist: metres above the LOCAL LOW GROUND (the lowest ground or still-water surface the `zone-mood` builtin finds around the player) the scene's mist reaches while in this zone, instead of the scene's absolute `sky.fog.mist.top`. A swamp at any height then keeps its mist hugging its pools (2-4 m). Omit = the scene's absolute top. Needs the scene's mist enabled (amount > 0).

__schema639.description: With `mistTop`: metres over which that mist fades out below its top (small = a hard sheet, large = soft). Omit = the scene's `thickness`.

__schema641.description: Ambient bed LOOP per band (one sound id each, e.g. `ambience/biome/swamp-{band}.ogg` — `{band}` is filled in). Replaces the biome beds here (see `biomeMix`).

__schema642.description: Per day/night band (the same edges as the day-night script, crossfaded by the soundscape): a sound id, or a comma list. `*` = every band not listed.

__schema653.description: Gain of `bed` relative to a biome bed (1 = as loud as one).

__schema655.description: How much of the biome beds is still heard under `bed`: 0 = the zone's bed replaces them, 0.3 = a little of the land shows through.

__schema657.description: Spot one-shots per band: comma list of ids (an id without extension is a variant family, e.g. `spot/frog-croak`). Replaces the biome spot table here.

__schema658.description: Exploration tracks per band, comma list (`{daynight}` = day|night is filled in). Beats biome music; a town zone's town music beats an INHERITED one (a town zone inherits its parent's bed and still water, never its music or spots).

__schema659.description: Bed near still inland water here (marsh pools: `ambience/water/swamp-water.ogg`). Replaces the soundscape's lake bed; rivers and the sea keep theirs.

items.description: An ambient particle layer that lives in this zone (same fields as an `ambient-particles` layer, minus `zones`: the zone IS where).

__schema662.description: Layer id: drives the local player's child entity tagged `ambient-<id>` (the scene must carry that emitter).

__schema663.description: Comma list of biome ids it is limited to INSIDE the zone. Empty = the whole zone.

__schema665.description: Time of day it lives, eased across dusk and dawn.

__schema667.description: Town zones (region tag `town`): `never` keeps it out of the zone's towns.

__schema671.description: Extra rate x closeness to water (1.5 = two and a half times as many at the edge).

__schema673.description: Particles per second at full strength (live count ~ rate x lifetime, capped by the emitter's `max`).

__schema675.description: Extra rate per unit of storm; negative thins it out in a storm.

__schema677.description: Metres/second the wind carries it at full gust; 0 = the emitter's own aim.

__schema679.description: Vertical drift m/s added to the wind aim: negative falls (ash), positive rises (spores).

__schema681.description: Night brightness floor: 1 = self-lit (fireflies), 0.2 = moonlit only.

__schema683.description: Scatter (props: trees, bushes, rocks) inside this region.

__schema684.description: Scatter rule ids that MAY grow here; every other rule is off. Omit to allow all. Filters only: a rule still needs its own biomes/slope/height to place, so this can never put a palm in a taiga. Rocks are scatter rules too — list them or they vanish.

__schema686.description: Scatter rule ids that never grow here. Unioned down the region chain: a place cannot re-allow what its zone denies.

__schema688.description: Multiplier on every allowed rule not named in `rules`. Below 1 thins (0.25 = 'a few'); 0 removes. Above 1 only FILLS BACK what the rule's `clump` and `biomeDensity` thinned — never past the rule's own `density`, which fixes the lattice. To grow more than that, raise the rule's density and thin it elsewhere.

__schema690.description: Per-rule multiplier, rule id -> number; REPLACES `density` for that rule. { "pine": 0.2, "rock-small": 2 }.
