__schema692.description: Species swap, rule id -> rule id: a candidate of the first rule that survives every gate (its biomes, slope, density here) is emitted as the second rule's model, scale, collider and tint. { "pine": "dead-dried-tree" } turns a pine wood dead; { "palm": "pine" } keeps a beach wooded in a northern zone. The target may be a rule with density 0 kept only for this. Not applied to cliff-column rules.

__schema694.description: Wind-bent stands: trees in this region lean together. Collision follows the same rotation.

degrees.description: How far the tops lean, from vertical.

toward.description: World direction [x, z] the tops lean toward (downwind). North is -Z: [0, -1] leans north.

jitter.description: Per-tree random spread on `degrees`, so a stand is not a parade.

rules.description: Rule ids (as EMITTED, after `replace`) that lean. Empty = every rule with a cylinder collider (the trees).

__schema700.description: Ground cover (grass, flowers, reeds) inside this region.

__schema701.description: Cover layer ids (`cover[].id`) that may grow here; all others are off. Omit to allow all.

__schema703.description: Cover layer ids that never grow here. Unioned down the region chain.

__schema705.description: Multiplier on every allowed layer not named in `layers`. Below 1 thins; 0 = bare ground; above 1 fills back the layer's clump thinning only.

__schema707.description: Per-layer multiplier, layer id -> number; REPLACES `density` for that layer.

__schema709.description: Metres OUTSIDE this region's own polygon that it still governs, where no region contains the point. For a zone whose border was drawn along the waterline: its beach lies outside every zone, so without a margin the biomes alone decide there (palms on a northern shore). Not inherited.

__schema711.description: Why — the mood line this implements ('a few wind-bent pines').

layer.description: Palette surface NAME the rocks of this zone wear on top (`snow`, a grass for moss, `sand`, the zone's own ground...).

amount.description: How far it reaches: 0 = bare, 0.4 = flat tops, 0.7 = tops and ledges, 1 = all but the steep sides.

__schema716.description: World-space XZ control points; the feature is the polyline through them.

depth.description: How far below the surrounding land the floor sits.

rim.description: Horizontal distance the walls take to climb back to natural terrain.

steps.description: Terraces in each wall. 1 is a smooth ramp; 3-4 reads as bedded rock.

stepSharpness.description: 0 = the terraces vanish into a straight slope, 1 = vertical risers and flat treads.

height.description: Metres the crest stands ABOVE the natural terrain.

falloff.description: Horizontal distance the flanks take to meet natural ground on either side of the crest.

heights.description: Per-point crest heights (one per point), overriding `height`. The barriers stage sets each so the crest sits `height` above the HIGHER flank measured `falloff` out — a 35 m ridge on a 30 m slope is a step, not a wall, unless it is measured that way.

tags.description: "barrier" plus "zone:<id>" for each zone it separates, when written by `worldgen barriers`.

points.description: World-space XZ centreline of the shelf; a single point is a round pad.

radius.description: Half-width of the flat shelf, measured from the centreline.

falloff.description: Distance beyond `radius` over which the shelf's height blends into what is around it — the step's face.

groundY.description: The shelf's height. Unlike a town pad this is never inferred: a terrace exists to be at a chosen level.

at.description: World XZ of the gate mouth — where the town's own roads end and the world's begin. Every path to this town arrives HERE, not at the centre.

facing.description: Outward XZ direction the road leaves in, pointing away from the town. Normalised on use; [0, 0] is an error.

width.description: Clear width of the opening. A path arriving here is drawn no wider than this.

approach.description: Metres of DEAD STRAIGHT path laid outward from `at` along `facing` before the router takes over. This is what makes the road leave square-on through the arch instead of raking past it; 0 lets the router start bending at the gate itself.

id.description: Owner of the calm disc (a town, place region or patch id).

radius.description: Metres of full calm: inside, landform families and valleys do not apply.

falloff.description: Metres over which the families fade back in outside `radius`.

__schema774.description: World XZ of the first sample (northwest corner). Rows increase toward +Z.

__schema777.description: World XZ extent from first to last sample, in metres.

__schema782.description: Absolute world Y samples, row-major (row * columns + column). Bilinear interpolation; importers decode image brightness into metres before storing.

__schema784.description: Per-sample opacity in [0, 1], row-major like `heights` (bilinear). Present = a MASKED edit: the ground under the patch is pulled toward `heights` by this weight (times the edge feather), so where it is 0 the ground beneath shows through and is never frozen into the raster (a later road, a neighbouring patch or a terrain rebuild under the untouched part of the box still shows). Omitted = opaque: the raster replaces the ground inside the feather.

__schema787.description: Metres INSIDE every patch edge used to smoothstep from existing terrain to these heights. Exactly zero influence and zero blend derivative on the boundary; neighbouring chunks sample the same field. A MINIMUM: the evaluated feather is never narrower than two voxel steps and, unless `feather` is set, widens per edge until the blend is no steeper than `edgeSlope` for the height the patch differs from the ground along that edge (capped at half the extent).

__schema788.description: Explicit feather width in metres inside every edge (at least `blend`), replacing the automatic per-edge width. A feather narrower than two voxel steps draws as a sawtooth on any edge that is not level with the ground.

__schema790.description: Steepest rise/run the automatic edge feather allows (default 1 = 45 degrees). Lower = softer edges.

__schema792.description: Steepest rise/run allowed INSIDE the raster. Risers drawn steeper (a terrace or tier wall, a bench edge) are filled at the foot into a talus at this slope, keeping every top level where it is. Omitted = the raster as written. A wall steeper than about 1.6 between 2 m lattice samples draws as a zig-zag; `worldgen lips` reports where.

__schema794.description: Ground the river solve must NOT see (like terrace-wall `tw-*` and bridge-span `bs-*` patches): banks raised beside a channel, a lip shoulder. Without it the solve re-reads the raised ground and can move the river, its levels and its falls. The patch still shapes the finished ground, the water clip and every gate.

__schema796.description: Half-width in metres of the tent prefilter applied to the raster before sampling (default: the voxel step). Anti-aliases cliffs and terrace edges drawn sharper than the lattice so diagonal edges do not stair-step. 0 = raw raster.

polygon.description: World-space XZ outline of the shore. Omit for a disc of `radius` about `center`.

waterY.description: Surface height. The basin is carved to sit below it; land outside the outline is untouched past `bank`.

depth.description: How far below the surface the deepest water is.

bank.description: Distance over which the shore eases from the waterline back to natural terrain, and the bed from the shore down to `depth`.

carve.description: true (hand-placed lakes): dig the basin — everything inside the outline goes down to `depth`, and a `bank` outside it eases to the waterline, whatever the ground was. false (`worldgen rivers` writes this): the terrain already holds the basin the hydrology found, so only ground at or under the surface is deepened, blended over two banks, and ground standing over a metre above it — an island, or an outline that overshot onto a hillside — is left alone. Carving a traced outline dug craters with vertical walls where it strayed uphill.

material.description: Water material for THIS lake, overriding the recipe's `waterMaterial`. A swamp pool is still, murky and opaque; a tarn is clear — one water for both reads wrong in both.

surface.description: Palette surface NAME painted on the bed and a `shore` band around the outline — wet sand, gravel — so the ground under and beside the water is not the biome's grass. Empty leaves the biome's cover; an unknown name paints nothing.

shore.description: Metres beyond the outline the `surface` fades out over.

points.description: World-space XZ of the two abutments: where the road stops on one bank and resumes on the other.

deckY.description: Height of the deck surface; the roads on both banks end at this height.

waterY.description: Water surface under the span, for the WFC stage to size piers.

material.description: Material for the deck, overriding the recipe's `bridgeMaterial`.

items.description: A bridge across a gap: two anchors + kind + style; solved by `worldgen bridge-place` from the world-kit bridge kits.

__schema816.description: Stable id; its derived height patches and clearing are `bs-<id>*`.

__schema817.description: Who wrote it (a town, POI or zone id).

__schema819.description: arch: stone arch bridge / aqueduct (bays 6-16 m, piers founded on the ground or seabed, up to ~70 m piers). rope: rope suspension bridge (12-130 m, no piers): sea stacks, chasms, anything too deep or wet for piers; STRAIGHT in plan between NATURAL TOPS, the height taken as SLOPE (end to end <= 30 deg, the deck <= 35 deg): Derek's standing rule, never stairs, stages, towers or plinths to meet a deck; steeper means a different anchor pair. plinth: reserved (the kit's stone landing plinth is a future POI part; bridge-place refuses it).

__schema821.description: gnawspur: coursed rubble with dressed voussoir rings, string course, coping and paving (the Gnawspur aqueduct). coastal: dark lichened rubble, ragged voussoirs, weather-picked bosses. Rope bridges are always the Gnawbridge's lashed hull planks on tarred stringers (style ignored).

__schema824.description: World [x, z] of this end: where the deck meets the land (a cliff-top edge, a stack top).

__schema828.description: Deck height at this end (world Y), or "ground": the natural ground there. Arch decks are level (both ends within 2 m; the pads are levelled to the deck); a rope deck runs from one end's height to the other's.

__schema830.description: This end's seating, overriding the span's `seat` (a span from a headland onto a DC stack top: pad on the land, rock on the stack; stage: a timber landing stage, docks / sea-level landings only; plinth: refused for rope ends).

__schema832.description: plinth only: the far ends of the rope bridges landing on it (world [x, z]); the parapet opens toward each and the stair's roof hatch keeps clear of their landings.

__schema834.description: arch only: a true aqueduct, a water channel along the deck beside a 2.2 m towpath.

__schema836.description: arch only: 2 = a lower arcade under the top one (Pont du Gard). auto: 2 when a pier would be over 24 m tall.

__schema838.description: arch only: force the bay width (m). Omitted = chosen from the gap and the pier heights (taller crossings get wider bays).

__schema840.description: arch only: tallest pier (m, springing to footing) the fit may build.

__schema842.description: arch only: deepest water (m) a pier may be founded in; a layout that needs a deeper pier fails over to another bay width or fails (use a rope bridge).

__schema844.description: rope only: the deck's sag at mid-span as a fraction of the span (3.5 % = 3.2 m on 90 m).

__schema848.description: rope only: hidden rail colliders along the hand ropes (nobody steps off by accident).

__schema850.description: pad: level each end with a feathered height patch (the cliff top behind the face only). rock: no patch (an end on a DC cliff top or rock formation): a rope end slides to the rim and its deck eases level over it, the gate checks the rock seats it. stage (rope only): a timber landing stage off a steep lip, with a walkway / stair to walkable ground (world-kit bridges stage.mts).

__schema854.description: Written by `worldgen bridge-place`; never hand-edit. Absent = not fitted yet (nothing is built).

heading.description: Degrees about +Y that turn the kit's +X (along the span) onto A -> B.

origin.description: World point s = 0 of the span frame (the measured face A for an arch, deck end A for a rope bridge).

span.description: Arch: abutment face to face (bays x bay width). Rope: deck end to deck end.

deckY.description: Arch: the walked deck height. Rope: deck end A's height.

dy.description: Rope: deck end B minus end A.

tiers.description: Arch: 1, or 2 with a lower arcade (Pont du Gard).

drops.description: Rope: metres each end's landing falls over its length, following a rock top that falls inland (0 = level).

lowDrop.description: Rope: the deck's lowest point below end A (m).

pieces.description: Every kit piece, world placed. The streamer emits these; do not hand-edit.

position.description: World [x, y, z]: the pier centre at its springing (top).

ground.description: Lowest solid ground under its footing (density surface), world Y.

water.description: Water surface over it, or null when dry.

bottom.description: Bottom of its stepped footing (world Y): below `ground` by the burial.

kind.description: full: one stack to the top springing; two-tier: a lower stack under the lower arcade and an upper one standing on it; abutment: the course stack under an abutment; post: a rope bridge anchor post.

profile.description: The walked deck surface as [s, y] samples along the span frame (s from `origin`, y world): what the walk probe reads.

derived.description: Ids of the features this fit wrote into `features.heightPatches` / `clearings`; a refit replaces exactly these.

ground.description: Fingerprint of the ground the fit was solved on (mean natural height over the ends and the span); `bridge-place --check` reports STALE when it has changed.

stages.description: Timber landing stages at `seat: stage` ends.

role.description: Kit role: bay-deck, bay-channel, bay-tier, abut, pier-cap, pier-course-4, cutwater-cap, rope-bridge ...

position.description: World position of the piece origin (see the kit's frames in world-kit authoring/bridges/lookup.json).
World centre of the roof (the walked roof top).

base.description: World Y of the floor inside (the highest rock under the footprint).

height.description: Roof over base (m).

door.description: World point just outside the doorway, on the ground.

stair.description: World stair stations, door corner to the roof: what the walk probe follows.

prefab.description: The landing stage's whole-piece id (bridges/stage-<hash>); `pieces` carry its segments.

origin.description: World point of the stage frame: the rope deck end on the platform.

yaw.description: Degrees about +Y of the stage frame (+X out over the gap).

path.description: World deck-top centreline of the walkway, platform back edge to the walkable ground: what the walk probe follows.

ground.description: The walkable ground the walkway reaches.

feet.description: World foot of every post / strut (the footing gate checks each is in rock or ground).

polygon.description: World-space XZ outline of the hollow.

y.description: Height the floor is raised to: the hollow's spill level, a little over.

bank.description: Distance beyond the outline over which the raise eases out.

points.description: World-space XZ, head first, mouth last.

width.description: Channel width at the mouth; the head is narrower unless `widths` are given.

points.description: World-space path in 3D — unlike rivers and roads, a cave goes up and down as well as along.

radius.description: Passage radius. Keep it comfortably ABOVE the world's voxel size (cellSize / resolution): marching cubes cannot represent a hole much narrower than one voxel, so a thinner tunnel is silently sealed in the mesh and in the collider cooked from it, however open the field says it is.

endRadius.description: Radius at the last point; omit for a uniform tube. Lets a passage open out into a chamber.

start.description: Box entrance centre or ellipse near-end centre at the flat floor datum, in world metres.

footprint.description: Box passage, or elliptical chamber centred halfway along length. Both preserve a flat floor; ellipse width/length are the protected diameters.

length.description: Box straight length or ellipse axial diameter in metres. A box has rectangular terminal planes; an ellipse is centred halfway along this length.

width.description: Protected field width in metres. Noise only recesses the sidewalls outward. Coarse MC can bevel floor-wall corners; validate the extracted mesh before claiming this entire width is flat.

height.description: Protected base ceiling above the exact flat floor datum; optional arch/roof noise adds clearance above it. Validate extracted headroom at coarse sampling.

wallNoise.description: Maximum outward wall recess, metres; sidewalls for box, all radial directions including both ends for ellipse. Never intrudes into protected air or changes the flat floor.

noiseDetail.description: Fraction of outward wall relief sampled at half noiseScale; zero preserves the original single-scale profile.

roofRise.description: Additional arched clearance above height: across a box passage, radially over an elliptical chamber. Never lowers the protected base ceiling; roof maximum is floor+height+roofRise+roofNoise.

roofNoise.description: Maximum additional outward roof recess, metres; fades at footprint edges and never changes the floor or protected base height. Thick rock backing above the full roof maximum must exceed the three-lattice-step roof skirt depth.

noiseScale.description: Wall-noise wavelength in metres; use a scale resolved by the world lattice.

seed.description: Deterministic wall-noise seed, combined with the world seed.

falloff.description: Exterior signed-sampling margin in metres; bound terrain influence and use at least two full-detail voxel steps. Coarser LOD is an approximation.

connectionBand.description: Noise fades to zero within this distance of both end planes and floor/ceiling, preserving stable terminal profiles and flat boundary bands.

__schema919.description: Slug. Its compiled pieces are `op:<id>:*`; re-applying replaces exactly those.

__schema920.description: Registered operator: see the engine spec `landformOperators` (terrace, path, ...).

digest.description: Hash of the compiled pieces as installed. A mismatch = a piece was hand-edited (never do that: change the params and re-apply).

ground.description: Fingerprint of the ground the operator read (its bounds, without its own output). A mismatch = the ground moved under it: re-apply.

id.description: `op:<operator id>:wall-<n>` — one run per riser stretch.

pieces.description: Kit pieces in run order: a 2 m straight and its cap per module.

cuts.description: One `face` cut per module: the low side the field carves down to the wall foot.

position.description: World position of the piece origin (its start vertex on the face line, at the wall foot).

run.description: Length (m) the piece runs along its face from its origin (body pieces).

overrides.description: Prefab overrides for this placement: the run-space UV phase variant of its meshes (the texture runs on unbroken from the piece before).

kind.description: face: the low side of a wall face (the terrain riser stands inside the wall body, and `height()` reads the foot there); door: a doorway's keep-clear box.

origin.description: World XZ the cut's frame starts at.

dir.description: Unit XZ direction of the frame's s axis (the face's walking direction); n is to its right (the low side).

n.description: Extent along the low-side normal (m): negative is behind the face, inside the wall.

y.description: Floor and top of the carved box (world Y). The floor is exact: the foot of the wall.

id.description: `op:<operator id>:landmark` — compiled by a landform operator (`ledges`); never hand-edited.

prefab.description: Baked landmark prefab (`landmarks/<operator id>-<digest>`): merged DC mesh + trimesh collider. Written by `tools/ledge-landmark.mts`.

position.description: World origin of the prefab (the landmark's footprint centre at y 0); it streams in the cell this stands in.

radius.description: Horizontal reach of the solids from `position`, metres (bounds, culling, previews).

digest.description: Hash of the CSG solids the prefab must be baked from; a bake with another digest is stale.

items.description: A solved path ribbon: compiled by the `path` landform operator; never hand-edit.

__schema949.description: Palette surface name; omitted = the zone's `road` (dirt) or `paving` (cobble, slab) tile at the ribbon's middle.

__schema956.description: [x, walkY, z, shoulderLeft, shoulderRight] every ~1 m along the centre. A negative shoulder = a retaining wall on that side, its face that far out.

from.description: Sample index where the stair starts.

treads.description: [s0, s1, topY] of every tread and landing, s = metres along the ribbon.

__schema961.description: Retaining-wall kit pieces, world placed. The streamer emits them; do not hand-edit.

__schema963.description: Oriented boxes the field carves in front of every wall face (same contract as terrace walls).

__schema965.description: Outline kept clear of scatter and ground cover (the ribbon plus a metre each side).

items.description: An agent-crafted waterfall: one solved fall re-shaped (a cascade of tiers and pools) and dressed with rocks. Written by `worldgen fall-site`, or by an agent from its `--snapshot` context. Bounded to the fall's own span (a few dozen metres); re-solved live by the field, so it follows the river if the world is regenerated.

__schema970.description: The FOOT of the solved fall this site dresses (WorldField.falls[i].x/z; `worldgen fall-site <world> --list` prints them). Matched to the nearest drop of at least 2 m within 25 m, so a site survives small re-solves; a site that matches nothing does nothing.

__schema973.description: single: the fall as solved, dressed only (rocks). cascade: the drop split into `tiers` — each its own lip, curtain, mist and splash — with a level pool between them held up on a rock ledge the field builds.

__schema975.description: cascade only, top to bottom. Empty = three even steps with 16 m pools. Keep every step at least 3 m (under that it is a rapid, not a fall).

share.description: Fraction of the fall's total height this step drops (normalised over all tiers).

pool.description: Length (m) of the level pool below this step, before the next lip. Ignored on the last tier: it lands in the river's own pool.

__schema978.description: Optional: the river's centreline redrawn through the site, upstream to downstream, as world XZ points. The river's own points between the nearest point to the first and the nearest point to the last are replaced by these (bed, width and depth interpolated along), then the field splines and solves it as usual. Use it to bend a dead-straight traced reach: a gentle S through the pools, a dog-leg at a lip. Keep both ends ON the river (within a channel width of it) and every point within 60 m of the site.

__schema980.description: Stacked rocks and boulders that make the site read as placed: along the pool rims, on the lip, in the plunge pool. Each is stood on the MESHED surface (blobs and overhangs included) and bedded so its footprint does not hang off a slope.

rule.description: Id of an existing scatter rule whose model to place (its collider, LOD and wind come with it, and it batches with that rule's other instances: no new draw call).

at.description: World XZ; stood on the ground there.

lift.description: Metres above (or into, if negative) the ground.

__schema986.description: Automatic scree: rocks of one scatter rule RESTING at each tier's foot around the plunge pools, on bench ledges and at the wall toes (clustered there, bottom-up, on the ground or on a rock below: support within 0.2 m under the lowest points, around the centre of mass). Never on a face steeper than 45 degrees, in the channel, on a lip line or over the rim. Big masses and wall faces are not this: they are rock volumes. Seeded by the site id (stable between runs).

rule.description: Id of an existing scatter rule whose model is the scree (same instanced batch as its other instances: no new draw call). rock-medium's model is 1.6 x 1.14 x 2.47 m (origin at its base).

max.description: Most scree rocks for the site.

scale.description: Instance scale range (model units); larger rocks go down first, lowest on each tier.

band.description: [below, above] metres around each station's water level searched for ground to rest on.

reach.description: How far (m) out from the channel centreline to look for ground.

upstream.description: Metres upstream of the top lip line where the dressing starts. Above the lip is the lake shore: keep 0 unless the channel is walled there.

__schema993.description: Faceted DC rock masses fused with the gorge walls: shoulders flanking every curtain, buttresses, ledge outcrops and pool-rim blocks (core rockFormations). Generated and baked by `tools/rock-formations.mts <project> <world> <site> --scene <scene>`, which reads these options; the scree (`walls`) rests on the same masses and keeps out of them. Absent = no formations.

seed.description: Extra seed mixed into the site-id hash (a different, equally valid set).

spacing.description: Mean spacing (m) of wall buttresses along each side; default 8.

scale.description: Scales every mass; default 1.

margin.description: Clearance (m) past the measured water edge no rock may enter; default 1.5.

clear.description: Keep-clear discs: a mass whose centre falls inside one is left out (a stair, ledge line, fight space or sight line); every other mass is unchanged.

voxelSize.description: Volume lattice spacing (m); default 1 (dual contouring keeps the facets crisp).

wallSurface.description: World surface name for the faces; default 'rock'.

accentSurface.description: Surface brushed faintly on some fronts; default 'cliff' ('' for none).

radius.description: Disc radius (m).

__schema1005.description: cascade only: the SITE-SCALE shape of the gorge, built from the solved tiers — a rounded bowl under every pool (wider than the channel, oval, longest downstream), a curved amphitheatre headwall at every tier, and side walls stepping back in benches whose width wanders along the span. Only ever cuts, and eases out to the land at `reach`. Absent = on with these defaults; `{ "enabled": false }` keeps the plain slot the river carve makes.

enabled.description: false: no site-scale shape, only the river's own slot carve.

bowl.description: Widest pool bowl: the channel with its bed widened this many times, plus the channel's own bank reach to the waterline (1 is the channel's water; 1.5-2.5 reads as a plunge pool). The pool's water fills the bowl to where its ground rises out, and necks back to the channel at every lip.

depth.description: How far (m) the middle of each bowl sits under its pool's water.

rim.description: Freeboard (m): how far the bowl's rim stands over its pool before the walls begin.

step.description: Height (m) of one bench of the stepped side walls.

slope.description: Mean rise over run of the stepped walls (benches plus risers). The risers stand about 2.1x this; keep them under 2.

wander.description: How far (m) the foot of each side wall wanders out from the bowl, per side, independently.

wavelength.description: Along-channel wavelength (m) of that wander (a second octave runs at 0.6x).

curve.description: Headwall curvature: at d metres across the channel a tier's cliff face stands curve·d² metres further downstream than at the lip (a concave amphitheatre).

reach.description: How far (m) from the channel the shape extends; it eases out to the land over its last 15 m.

lastPool.description: Length (m) of the bowl below the last tier, in the river's own pool.

items.description: A terrace held up by retaining walls: pad outline + drop + inserts; solved by `worldgen terrace-place`.

__schema1023.description: Stable id; its derived height patch and clearing are `tw-<id>`.

__schema1024.description: Who wrote it (a town or POI id). `worldgen terrace` owns the `<town>-riser-*` terraces of the towns it steps and rewrites them.

__schema1026.description: masonry-common: coursed rubble (houses, lanes, fields). masonry-stone: dressed ashlar (civic works, capitals). natural: rock shelves from the rock kit.

__schema1028.description: natural only: the masonry style to build with while the natural shelf kit (world-kit rock-kit shelf-lookup.json) does not exist. Omitted = a natural terrace fails until it does.

__schema1030.description: Outline of the upper pad, world XZ, any headings (wall runs are laid on a 2 m / 5 deg run grid from their first vertex; an all-axis outline snaps to the 2 m world grid). Either winding.

__schema1031.description: Footprint edge indices that carry wall (the rest meet the hill as feathered banks). auto: every edge whose outside ground lies at least `minDrop` and 60 % of the steepest edge's drop below the pad.

__schema1033.description: auto walls: smallest drop (m) worth a wall. With a dictated `height` an edge must also drop a quarter of it (the strip is cut down to the foot).

__schema1035.description: auto walls: the way the ground falls ([x, z], any length). Only edges whose outward normal is within 60 deg of it get wall — a wall running UP a slope would need its foot dug into the hill.

__schema1036.description: Pad level. Omitted = solved from the ground (median over the footprint; nudged so a doorway keeps a roof).

__schema1038.description: Wall drop (m), snapped to the kit's 0.4 m courses (1.5 / 3 / 4.5 exact). Omitted = from the ground at the wall foot. A height the kit has no slices for is built by `build.mts make` on the first fit.

role.description: What replaces plain wall at this offset. stair: straight flights against the face (2 m of low ground). stair-turn: dog-leg stair for tight terraces (3.8 m of low ground). ramp: ~10.6 deg ramp along the face. drain / buttress: a straight with weep holes / a buttress. door-lintel (wall >= 3.2 m) / door-arch (>= 3.6 m): a doorway with a 2 m passage into the pad (its keep-clear box is carved; the pad must stand a lattice node above the passage roof).

edge.description: Footprint edge index: the edge from footprint[edge] to footprint[edge + 1]. It must carry wall.

at.description: Metres from that edge's start vertex, snapped down to the 2 m grid.

run.description: drain / buttress only: a 2 m or a 4 m module.

__schema1043.description: Metres of low ground levelled at the wall foot (stairs and ramps take their own footprint + 1 m).

__schema1045.description: Minimum width (m) over which levelled ground blends back into the hill. Default: 1.6 x the height difference, at least 4.

__schema1047.description: 0 kept, 1 weathered (drains), 2 run-down (buttresses, worn coping), 3 ruined (gaps in the coping).

__schema1051.description: Written by `worldgen terrace-place`; never hand-edit. Absent = not fitted yet (nothing is built).

style.description: The kit style the pieces came from (natural falls back to `fallback` until the natural shelf kit exists).

baseY.description: Wall foot: the levelled low ground in front of every face.

height.description: Wall drop on the kit's 0.4 m courses (topY - baseY).

runs.description: Footprint edges grouped into continuous wall runs.

faces.description: Wall face lines and their low-side normals. The lattice step under them is the wall's: `worldgen lips` exempts it.

pieces.description: Every body and coping piece, world placed. The streamer emits these; do not hand-edit.

cuts.description: Oriented boxes the field carves (any heading): the low side of every face and each doorway's passage. The field reads these directly.

sockets.description: Doorway sockets (interior / portal / arrival), world placed.

derived.description: Ids of the features this fit wrote into `features.heightPatches` / `passages` / `clearings`; a refit replaces exactly these.

ground.description: Fingerprint (mean natural height over the raster) of the ground the fit was solved on; `terrace-place --check` reports a terrace STALE when the ground under it has changed.

items.description: A patch where scatter and/or cover do not grow: a site's footprint, a hall pad, a quarry floor, a town's building plot, street or door path. Replaces burying additive blobs to suppress foliage. Terrain is untouched.

__schema1061.description: Stable id; `worldgen vegetation --clearing` replaces by id. Prefix with the owner (`hrimgard-hall-pad`, `brinehold-plot-12`).

__schema1062.description: Outline in world metres [x, z]. Give this OR center + radius.

__schema1069.description: Metres OUTSIDE the edge over which plants return, from `keep` to full. 0 = a hard edge (reads as a stencil).

__schema1071.description: Fraction that survives inside: 0 clears, 0.3 leaves a thinned site.

__schema1073.description: Clear scatter props. A prop's canopy footprint counts, so a big tree keeps its whole crown off the clearing.

__schema1077.description: Who wrote it (a POI or town id) — installers remove their own by owner.

center.description: World-space XZ. Ground height is sampled from the field, so no Y is stored — the camp follows the terrain when it changes.

zone.description: Region id this camp sits in (recipe `regions`), or empty in an unzoned world. What a difficulty tier, a faction or a story hook keys on.

area.description: The spawnArea component emitted onto the scene entity, verbatim.

tags.description: Free-form. `worldgen spawn` writes a distance tier ("near", "far") off the zone hub.

__schema1083.description: Metres from the area's origin within which a player wakes it: the packs simulate (spawning first if they have not been placed yet).

__schema1085.description: Metres within which the packs are PLACED: spawned out of sight, settled on the ground, then paused standing in their idle until a player comes within `radius`. Default: the server's interest radius + 30, so a creature is already standing there when it first comes into view instead of appearing (and dropping) in front of the player.

__schema1087.description: Once awake, the area sleeps only when no player is within this (hysteresis — keep it larger than radius).

__schema1089.description: Seconds with no player inside sleepRadius before the pack is paused in place. It does not despawn: a returning player finds it where it was.

template.description: NPC template: the id of an npc-tagged scene subtree, or a name registered on the server at runtime.

spread.description: Metres around the origin the pack is scattered in (uniform disc).

__schema1093.description: Metres from home an enemy may chase before it must turn back. Handed to each NPC's root script as the `leash` param (with `home`, `roam`, `spawnArea`); the server also fences at 1.5× as a backstop.

__schema1095.description: Idle wander radius around home, passed as the `roam` param.

__schema1097.description: Patrol route: points in metres relative to the area's origin, walked in order and back (ping-pong) while the pack is idle, instead of wandering inside `roam`. Handed to each NPC as the `patrol` param in world coordinates; the leash and the server's fence are then measured from the nearest point of the route, so the route itself may be longer than the leash. Empty = no patrol.

__schema1099.description: How the population is laid out. `pack` (the old behaviour): every spawn scattered within its `spread` of the origin, respawned in place by the server's NPC manager. `anywhere`: AMBIENT LIFE — each creature (or pair) spawns, and respawns after `respawn` seconds, at a random walkable open-air point anywhere inside `radius`, never within `hiddenFrom` metres of a player, so no spot can be camped; each one's `home` is its own spawn point and it roams `roamRange` metres round it. Use it for starter wildlife with a `mix` of singles and pairs. `route`: a WANDERING RARE — spawns at a random point along `patrol` (never its start), walks it in a random direction, and respawns after `respawn` seconds out of sight; `unique` keeps one alive per area. Caves: `pack` or `route` (`anywhere` samples the open-air surface).

__schema1101.description: Weighted table of what spawns: each roll picks one row by `weight` and spawns `count` of it together, until `population` are alive. Singles and pairs ([1,1], [1,2]) read as roaming life; [3,5] reads as a camp. Works in every placement (in `pack` the rolls are scattered within 6 m of the origin, on top of `spawns`). Empty = `spawns` only (in `anywhere` / `route` the `spawns` entries are then the table, weighted by their counts, one creature per roll).

template.description: NPC template: the id of an npc-tagged scene subtree, a `prefab:<id>`, or a name registered on the server.

weight.description: Relative chance this row is the one rolled.

count.description: [min, max] creatures spawned together by one roll: [1,1] a single, [1,2] a single or a pair. More than 2 reads as a pack, not ambient life.

near.description: Metres the members of one roll stand from the first of them (a pair grazing together).

__schema1107.description: Creatures alive at once across the area, rolled from `mix`. Default: the sum of the `spawns` counts in `anywhere` (6 with only a `mix`), 1 in `route`, and in `pack` 0 extra (a `pack` with a `mix` rolls this many on top of `spawns`; default the mix's row count). Ignored when `unique` is on.

__schema1109.description: [min, max] seconds, jittered per death, before a dead creature's corpse is cleared and a replacement spawns somewhere out of sight. `anywhere` and `route` only — `pack` keeps the server's fixed respawn at the spawn point.

__schema1111.description: `anywhere` / `route`: no spawn or respawn lands within this many metres of any player, so no spot can be camped.

__schema1113.description: `anywhere` only: [min, max] metres each creature roams round its own spawn point (rolled per creature, replacing `roam`). Its leash is then at least that roam + 20 m, so a long wander is never mistaken for a chase gone too far.

__schema1115.description: `route`: exactly one alive per area (a rare); its replacement waits `respawn` seconds and appears out of sight.

__schema1117.description: Default temperament for every creature of the area (a `mix` row's own wins), handed to mob-brain as the `temperament` param: hostile (attacks on sight, today's mobs), territorial (attacks only who comes within `territory` metres of it or its home), passive (never starts a fight; hit it and it fights back, then wanders off; never shouts — the server hands passive creatures `alertRadius` 0). Unset = whatever the template's brain says (hostile).

__schema1119.description: Metres a `territorial` creature defends round itself and its home, handed to mob-brain as `territory`. Unset = the brain's default (7).

__schema1121.description: PLACEHOLDER RARES: whenever one of this area's slots spawns or respawns (a camp member in `pack`, a roamer in `anywhere`, a walker in `route`) and a rare is neither alive nor locked out, the slot rolls its `chance`; on a hit the rare spawns in that slot instead, with the slot's spot, home, roam, patrol and temperament (or its own). When it dies the slot goes back to placeholder respawns. Listed on the area, not on a row: one rare may sit behind several rows, and one-alive is per area (or per `id`). The old `route` + `unique` wandering rare still works.

template.description: The rare's NPC template (a scene subtree id, a `prefab:<id>`, or a registered name). A scene subtree named here is held back by the server (never stands live at its authored spot): the rare exists only when a placeholder rolls it.

chance.description: Chance (0..1) that a placeholder's slot spawns the rare instead, rolled on every spawn and respawn of a slot (the area's first fill included, so the rare is not guaranteed up at boot). Kill the placeholder to give the slot another roll. Keep it low (0.05-0.2): above ~0.3 the rare is nearly always up.

placeholders.description: Templates (of this area's `spawns` / `mix` rows) whose slots may roll the rare. Empty = any slot of the area.

lockout.description: [min, max] seconds after the rare dies (jittered per death) before any slot may roll it again. [0,0] = none.

id.description: Shared key: rares with the same id are one creature — at most one alive across every area naming it (and one lockout). Default: one per area and template.

temperament.description: The rare's own temperament (a rare is usually hostile or territorial). Unset = its placeholder slot's.

territory.description: The rare's own `territory` metres (territorial). Unset = the area's.

props.description: `prefab:` templates only: prefab props set on the rare (e.g. `level`, `maxHp`, `xpValue`, `aggroRange`), so a stock body can be the rare without a scene template.

above.description: World units of air polygonized above the highest ground in a cell — headroom for overhangs and arches.

below.description: World units of rock polygonized below the lowest ground in a cell. This is what makes surface caves enterable, and it is THE vertical cost knob: it multiplies both the sampled volume AND the cave surface the mesher has to triangulate, so it hits twice. Deeper cave networks want vertical chunk sections, not a bigger band here.

scale.description: World units per cycle of the broad band.

strength.description: Brightness swing, plus and minus. 0 disables the whole overlay.

detailScale.description: Second band, near tile size (10-20). This is the one that hides the grid up close.

colorStrength.description: How far the overlay shifts COLOUR, per channel, on top of the brightness swing. Brightness alone makes a large area read as one material under uneven light; letting the channels drift apart slightly — warmer here, greyer there — is what reads as the ground actually being different from place to place. 0.06-0.15 is a natural mottle; past ~0.25 the terrain goes tie-dye.

colorScale.description: World units per cycle of the colour band. Defaults to `scale`. Set it larger for broad regional colour shifts that survive being seen from a distance.

warp.description: How far the texture PROJECTION is pushed around by noise before it is sampled, as a fraction of each layer's OWN tile, so one setting means the same thing to a 3.5m grass tile and a 9m cliff tile. This is the one that actually kills tiling: brightness noise can only shade OVER a grid, and the grid is still underneath it — on a big flat-lit face seen from a distance the eye finds it anyway. Warping the projection means neighbouring tiles no longer line up, so there is no grid left to find. 0.25-0.5 is usually enough; past about 0.6 the texture visibly smears.

warpScale.description: World units per cycle of the warp. Measured: keep it near TWICE the tile size, not far above it. A warp much coarser than the tile slides whole tiles around and leaves the motif inside each one perfectly intact, so a strongly patterned texture still reads as a pattern; a warp at roughly tile scale distorts the motif itself, which is what stops a big rock face looking stamped.

band.description: Width in metres of the blend across a zone border where a zone restyles its ground (`regions[].ground`): half outside the polygon, half inside, so two zones meet at 50/50 on the line and nothing is a seam.

jitter.description: Noise on the border, as a fraction of `band`, so the blend does not follow a clean offset of the polygon.

__schema1.description: Metres between lattice samples. A dungeon wants 0.2-0.3: fine enough that a 0.4 m step reads as a step, coarse enough to mesh in a second.

__schema3.description: World-space extent to mesh. Omit and it is derived from the nodes, which is what you want unless a node is deliberately unbounded.

__schema9.description: Surface names, index-for-index with the `terrain-splat` material's splat layers. Names are for humans; the indices are what the mesh carries.

__schema12.description: Default palette triple, used by any node that declares none.

__schema17.description: Applied IN ORDER over empty space. Later nodes win.

__schema20.description: `add` unions this shape into the solid, `sub` carves it out as air, `intersect` clips the solid to it.

__schema23.description: Prism footprint in local X/Z metres, extruded by height along Y. Simple non-self-intersecting boundary, either winding; concave outlines allowed. Do not repeat the closing vertex.

__schema31.description: Radius of a rounded edge on this primitive. 0 keeps the corner sharp, which is the whole reason to mesh a volume with dual contouring.

__schema33.description: Smooth-min radius against everything before it. 0 is a hard boolean; raise it where cut rock should melt into a natural cave.

__schema35.description: Palette indices this node paints. Omit to inherit the document default.

__schema36.description: Bounded displacement of this primitive in local metres (|displacement| <= amount). Use on cave cuts and on the natural-rock ROLE nodes of an imported stamp (tools/mesh-dc role noise); leave masonry, trim and treads unperturbed. On a primitive it disables distance-based block rejection; a volume made only of mesh nodes keeps block culling with a margin of 2 x the largest amount.

__schema37.description: Geometry noise for one CSG node.

__schema38.description: Peak displacement in metres. The surface never moves farther than this.

__schema39.description: Feature size in metres of the first octave (frequency = 1/scale).

__schema41.description: Perlin octaves, each 2.7x the frequency and 1/3 the weight of the last. Omitted = 2 (the original formula).

__schema43.description: Displace OUTWARD only: the solid grows by 0..amount and never thins, so a wall thinner than 2 x amount cannot open a hole. The noise is stretched so the relief spans the full 0..amount (peak-to-peak = amount).

__schema45.description: Regions where the noise fades to zero: doorways, stair treads, the walk lane along a route. Distances are measured in the node's local frame.

a.description: Capsule start, node-local metres (for an imported stamp: entrance-anchor frame, Y up).

b.description: Capsule end. Omit for a sphere at `a`.

radius.description: Inside this distance of the segment the noise is zero.

fade.description: Over this further distance the noise ramps (smoothstep) back to full.
Outside the box the noise ramps (smoothstep) back to full over this distance.

anyOf.description: Floor band: noise fades to zero in a band around each walkable floor, so noised rock walls meet the floor crisp and leave dressable floor.

__schema51.description: Walkable floor heights on a grid. tools/mesh-dc noise.mjs derives it from the stamp's own exposed up-facing faces, dilated past the floor edge so wall feet are covered.

__schema55.description: Cell size in metres (square cells in X/Z).

__schema58.description: One entry per cell (row-major, columns along X): flat [lo, hi, lo, hi, ...] floor-height ranges in that cell; [] = no floor.

__schema60.description: Up to this height above a floor the noise is zero (wall feet meet the floor clean and vertical).

__schema62.description: Down to this depth below a floor the noise is zero.

__schema64.description: Beyond the band the noise ramps (smoothstep, vertically) back to full over this distance.

__schema66.description: Required by, and only read by, `shape: "heightfield"`: the sampled surface this node thickens into a slab. Its footprint and thickness come from `size`.

__schema67.description: Heights sampled on a regular grid and thickened into a slab. The footprint is size[0] x size[2] in local X/Z centred on the origin, size[1] is the slab THICKNESS, and heights are bilinear between samples and clamped at the edges. Nothing outside the footprint is solid, so the node has a real boundary. Its distance field is an APPROXIMATION (exact under a flat patch, an under-estimate on a slope), which is why it disables distance-based block rejection the way `noise` does.

__schema68.description: Samples across local X, both edges included. Spacing is size[0]/(width-1) metres.

__schema69.description: Samples across local Z, both edges included. Spacing is size[2]/(depth-1) metres.

__schema70.description: width*depth heights in LOCAL metres, relative to the node's own origin. Row-major with X fastest: index 0 is the -x/-z corner, index width*depth-1 the +x/+z one. Either a plain number array or a base64 string of little-endian float32 of exactly that length — see `encodeHeightfieldValues`.

__schema73.description: Which side of the sampled surface the slab hangs on. `floor` is solid from h-size[1] up to h (ground you stand on); `ceiling` is solid from h up to h+size[1] (a vault you walk under).

__schema75.description: Required by shape mesh: closed indexed local triangle solids, unioned and sampled by the shared CSG/DC path. Node position/rotation apply; size is ignored. Triangle palette assignments remain repaintable with volume paint.

__schema76.description: Closed indexed triangle solids sampled as a CSG signed-distance field, then extracted by the shared dual-contouring mesh path. Geometry must be an embedded closed manifold; self-intersections are rejected with 1e-9 relative tolerance at shared edges/vertices. A 64-machine-epsilon coordinate-scale boundary band consistently counts exactly touching closed surfaces as solid; no voxel smoothing or lattice changes. No UVs or imported render mesh fallback.

__schema77.description: Flat local XYZ coordinates in metres, Y up. Every indexed vertex belongs to a closed surface; bake scale into coordinates. Node position/rotation transform these coordinates; size is ignored.

__schema79.description: Triangle vertex indices, three per triangle. Shared vertices must use shared indices within a solid. No zero-area triangles, open edges, nonmanifold vertices/edges, or inconsistent winding. A whole connected shell may have either winding.

__schema81.description: Triangle counts of consecutive closed solids; their sum must equal indices.length/3. Solids are UNIONED even when they overlap. Each solid owns disjoint vertex indices; touching solids may duplicate coordinates. Omit for one closed solid. Disconnected boundary shells within one solid use parity (for example a sealed cavity); overlapping solids must be separate ranges.

__schema84.description: One volume palette index per source triangle, in index order. Overrides this node's floor/wall/ceiling palette at its surface, including carved faces. Omit to inherit the node surface. Ordinary volume paint strokes apply afterward.

__schema86.description: Persistent ordered texture strokes, evaluated after the CSG surface palette.

items.description: Spherical texture stroke in volume-local metres. Smooth falloff; later strokes blend over earlier ones without changing density or collision.

__schema93.description: Optional local-space facing direction for an angle-limited area fill.

__schema95.description: Maximum angle in degrees from the chosen normal. 180 paints all facing directions.

__schema97.description: Uniform coverage inside radius instead of brush falloff. This is a bounded facing-angle fill, not a connected-component flood fill.

__schema99.description: Optional RGB vertex tint blended in with the same coverage as the layer, e.g. the biome grass tint so painted grass tops match the terrain around them.

__schema101.description: RGB vertex tint the whole volume is multiplied by (the terrain-splat material's tintByVertexColor). Omit for white. Set it to the terrain's biome tint where a volume must match the ground it is fused with.

sheet.description: Spritesheet data-asset id. Its grid is the flipbook: columns are frames, rows are colour variants.

row.description: Sheet row. 5 is the greyscale variant in the purchased library — leave it and let `color` tint.

size.description: Metres — the quad's width; height follows `aspect`.

orient.description: billboard faces the camera; ground lies flat (marks, runes); vertical stands upright and yaws toward the camera (a slash, a wave); facing stands upright with its face along the spell direction (a portal); velocity is a camera-facing quad rolled onto the anchor's motion; world is fixed IN THE WORLD, never turning to the camera: the art's top along the motion (a projectile) or, at rest, upright and square to the spell direction (a stuck spear). Pair it with `crossed`.

crossed.description: world: a second quad crossed at 90° around the long axis, so the shape holds from every side (the PSX crossed-plane trick) instead of vanishing edge-on.

spin.description: Radians/sec the quad turns in its own plane. Lying on the ground that is a yaw; standing up it is a roll around a horizontal axis, which reads wrong on most symbols — the symbol catalog says which may.

yaw.description: Fixed rotation around the facing axis, radians.

randomYaw.description: Roll `yaw` per play — cheap variety for repeated impacts.

cell.description: [col, row] of ONE sheet cell shown as a static SYMBOL (a sigil, a glyph, an arrow) instead of playing the sheet as a flipbook. `fps`/`loop` are ignored; the symbol lives for `duration` (0 = the phase, or 0.6 s).

glow.description: A halo around a SYMBOL (`cell` set), built from its own shape: 0 = none, 1 = a clear glow, 2+ = blazing. Banded into PSX steps when the spell has a texel grid.

glowSize.description: How far the halo reaches, as a fraction of the symbol's size.

glowColor.description: Halo colour: a palette slot or #rrggbb.

orbit.description: Metres the quad circles the anchor at, around its up axis. 0 = sits on the anchor.

orbitSpeed.description: Radians/sec along the orbit; negative runs the other way.

orbitPhase.description: Starting angle on the orbit, radians (0 = in front of the anchor). `repeat.turn` advances it per copy.

emitter.description: The emitter, in the `particles` component's own vocabulary. colorStart/colorEnd are overridden by the module's `color`/`colorEnd` unless they are left white.

burst.description: Particles spawned the moment the module starts.

stream.description: Keep emitting at the emitter's `rate` for the module's duration — channels, trails, auras.

radius.description: Outer radius in metres at scale 1.

inner.description: Inner radius as a fraction of the outer. 0 = a filled disc (a rune, a portal floor).

orient.description: ground lies on the terrain; vertical stands upright yawed toward the camera; facing stands upright with its face along the spell direction (a portal); billboard faces the camera.

expand.description: Scale at birth and at death: a shockwave runs 0.1 → 1, a rune holds 1 → 1. `sizeCurve` overrides.

soft.description: Edge softness. 0 is a hard band; 1 fades across the whole width.

texture.description: Texture asset id laid across the disc (a rune, a sigil). Omitted = a procedural soft band.

arc.description: Degrees of the disc that are drawn, centred on the spell direction: 360 is a full ring, 90 a wedge in front of the caster.

noise.description: Breaks the band with scrolling noise so it reads as energy rather than a drawn circle.

swirl.description: Spiral distortion strength — the portal look. 0 = none.

drape.description: Ground rings follow the terrain under them (needs the host's ground probe).

height.description: Vertical/billboard: metres above the anchor the centre sits.

sheet.description: Decal-sheet data-asset id (written by `fx.mjs decals`). Its texture is NOT plain art: R is WHEN each texel appears (0 = at the strike point, 1 = last), G is the art's own brightness, A is coverage.

cell.description: [col, row] of the decal on its sheet.

size.description: Metres across (the cell's width); depth follows `aspect`.

aspect.description: Width / depth. >1 stretches the mark across the spell direction.

grow.description: Seconds for the reveal front to run from the strike point to the rim. Cracks race along their own lines, vines creep, flowers open stem-first — the order is baked in the sheet. 0 = the whole mark at once.

edge.description: Width of the glowing growth front, in reveal units (0 = no front). It fades once growth completes.

edgeColor.description: Colour of the growth front: a palette slot or #rrggbb.

shade.description: How much the art's own brightness shades the colour: 0 flat, 1 the drawn detail at full contrast.

fadeOut.description: Seconds after its life the mark takes to go — faded, or run backwards when `recede`.

recede.description: Die by running the reveal backwards (vines withdraw, frost retreats to the centre) instead of fading.

yaw.description: Radians around up, on top of facing the spell direction.

randomYaw.description: Roll the yaw per play — repeated impacts stop looking stamped.

drape.description: Follow the terrain under the mark (needs the host's ground probe).

style.description: energy = noisy fresnel rim (barriers, orbs, charge-ups); glass = clean thin rim (bubbles, wards); smoke = dense normal-blended body (a cloud, a void); wire = a lattice of noise lines (arcane cages).

fresnel.description: Rim power — higher is a thinner, brighter edge. 0 = flat.

noise.description: How much scrolling 3D noise breaks the surface.

dissolve.description: [[t, threshold]] — the surface burns away where noise < threshold. A curve 0 → 1 is a shell that dissolves as it dies; 1 → 0 is one that assembles.

squash.description: Vertical scale: a dome on the ground is ~0.6, a tall bubble 1.4.

radius.description: Base radius, metres.

topRadius.description: Radius at the far end. Omitted = same as `radius` (a pillar); 0 = a cone to a point.

orient.description: up = a pillar out of the ground; forward = a cone along the spell direction (breath, spray); down = hanging from the sky onto the anchor.

scroll.description: Noise scroll speed along the axis; positive = base → far end.

edgeFade.description: Fade at the silhouette so the tube has no hard vertical edges.

capFade.description: Fraction of the height faded out at the base and at the far end.

length.description: Metres along the spell direction when there is no target (or `toTarget` is off).

toTarget.description: Span anchor → target when the frame has one.

core.description: Bright inner core as a fraction of width. 0 = none.

style.description: energy = soft noisy glow; laser = hard clean edge; plasma = fat writhing body.

scroll.description: Noise scroll speed toward the far end, metres/sec.

jitter.description: Metres of sideways displacement per segment.

refreshHz.description: How often the path re-rolls — the flicker.

count.description: Independent strands, each with its own path — a channelled storm rather than one arc.

spread.description: count > 1: metres the far ends scatter around the target.

arc.description: line = anchor to target/direction; sky = strikes DOWN onto the anchor from `length` metres up; ground = crawls along the terrain outward from the anchor in a random direction.

intensityCurve.description: [[t, multiplier]]. Default is a flash: spike, then decay.

asset.description: Model asset id. Omitted = the procedural `primitive`.

primitive.description: Procedural bodies for when no model is given.

size.description: Metres, longest extent.

motion.description: drop = falls from `from` metres up and lands as the module ends; rise = comes up out of the ground; hover = bobs in place; orbit = circles the anchor; launch = flies up and away; forward = glides `from` metres along the spell direction (a projection, an afterimage).

from.description: drop: start height above the anchor; rise: depth below it. 0 = auto.

spread.description: count > 1: radius they scatter or orbit within.

tint.description: Colour the body with the palette; off keeps the asset's own material.

sheet.description: Symbol sheet whose cells are drawn BODIES (role `object`: spikes, crystals, rocks, orbs, blades, upright, base at the bottom). When set, every body is a camera-facing drawing standing in the world instead of a 3D primitive — same motion, the spell's own art style.

cells.description: [col, row] cells of `sheet`; each body takes one in turn.

width.description: Camera-facing ribbon: metres across. Ignored with `edge` (the edge's two points set the width).

length.description: Seconds of history the ribbon covers.

taper.description: Narrow toward the tail. With `edge` the inner point slides toward the outer one as a sample ages, so a blade's smear thins to its tip's line.

falloff.description: How fast the ribbon dims behind its leading edge: brightness = (1 - age/length)^falloff. 1 = a linear fade over the whole history (a sheet); 2.5-4 keeps only the last stretch bright, so a fast swing reads as an edge cutting air with a short glowing wake instead of a filled fan.

coreColor.description: A third, HOT colour for the brightest band (palette slot or #rrggbb): the ribbon then ramps in hard steps core -> `color` -> `colorEnd` as it dims, and with `edge` the brightness also leans toward the outer point, so the hot core runs along the blade's leading edge near the tip. Omitted = the two-colour fade.

edge.description: SWEPT ribbon (a weapon trail): each frame samples TWO points on the anchor object and the ribbon spans them, so it is the surface the edge swept through, not a camera-facing strip. Anchor it on `caster` (the weapon's entity, or a body plus `bone`) with `follow`. Omitted = a camera-facing ribbon behind one moving point (a projectile's tail).

radius.description: circle: radius; cone: reach; line: length. Metres.

windup.description: Seconds the fill takes to reach the rim — the clock the target reads.

hold.description: Seconds the volume stays live after the windup.

growFrom.description: Live volumes that GROW: scale at the start of the hold, reaching 1 at its end.

curtain.description: Height of the vertical curtain, metres. 0 = auto from radius.

rimOpacity.description: The rim is the only number a dodge is judged against — keep it the brightest part, but not blown out.

dash.description: Rim dashing, 0..1: 0 is a solid band, 0.5 draws dashes as long as their gaps — the PSX marker look.

height.description: Vertical extent the drape is clamped to — keep it equal to the hit test's `delivery.height`.

radius.description: Outer reach of the arc, metres.

inner.description: Inner radius as a fraction of the outer: near 1 a thin crescent, near 0 a fat cleave.

sweep.description: Degrees the arc covers, centred on the spell direction.

tilt.description: Roll of the cutting plane around the spell direction: 0 = a horizontal cleave, 90 = a vertical overhead chop, ±45 diagonal.

reverse.description: Sweep the other way (right-to-left for a cleave, bottom-to-top for a chop).

sweepTime.description: Fraction of the life the leading edge takes to cross the arc; the rest is the tail fading out.

tail.description: Length of the trailing fade behind the leading edge, as a fraction of the sweep.

height.description: Metres above the anchor the arc's centre sits (chest height for a cleave).

core.description: How bright the leading edge is, toward the glow colour.

strength.description: Metres of camera displacement felt by a camera at the effect.

range.description: Metres over which the shake fades out. A camera at the effect feels the full `strength`, one at `range` or further feels nothing (quadratic falloff between). 0 disables the falloff — every camera in the world shakes, which is almost never what you want.

asset.description: Sound asset id, or a comma list of variants: one is picked at random per play.

__schema0.description: Stable key so a human tweak or an agent's note can name this module.

__schema2.description: The library preset this came from — provenance for tweak-and-regenerate, never read at runtime.

at.description: origin = where the spell resolves (the volume's centre, the impact point); caster = the casting body; target = the targeted body or point; path = the projectile in flight (travel phase); ground = origin projected onto the terrain.

socket.description: caster/target only: a named attach point — rightHand, leftHand, chest, head, feet — resolved by the host to a bone-socket entity under that body. A missing socket falls back to the body itself.

offset.description: metres in the anchor's own frame: x right, y up, z FORWARD along the spell direction.

local.description: caster/target only: `offset` is in the anchor OBJECT's own axes (its rotation, not its scale) and the module faces with it — a point on a held weapon, such as its tip, that turns with the blade. Pair with `follow` (and a particle emitter's `space: local`) to ride it. false = the spell frame described under `offset`.

follow.description: Keep tracking the anchor for the module's whole life (a hand mid-swing, a projectile in flight) instead of sampling it once at start.

__schema15.description: Seconds it lives. 0 = natural length (a flipbook's frames, a burst's longest particle) or, for sustained kinds, the phase length.

__schema19.description: Where colour fades toward over life, for kinds that fade (particles, trail, beam core).

__schema21.description: additive = light (nearly everything magical); normal = matter that occludes (smoke, a poison cloud).

__schema28.description: PSX look: quantise the procedural shading to this many cells across the shape (0 = off, 16–32 reads as pixel art). Rings, shells, columns and beams snap their noise and bands to the grid; masks and sprites switch to nearest filtering.

__schema30.description: PSX look in WORLD units: metres per texel (0 = off; overrides `pixel`). Every module of a spell shares one, so a 12 m shockwave and a 1 m slash are pixelated at the same size and stay so as they grow — 0.03 matches the symbol sheets' own density at typical sizes (coarser turns line art to mush). Textured kinds resample their art onto the same grid.

__schema32.description: Alpha steps (0 = smooth). 3–5 turns soft falloffs into hard bands — the other half of the PSX look.

__schema34.description: [[t, multiplier]] over life, on top of the module's own size.

__schema37.description: Play this module as a STEPPING sequence — spikes that erupt one after another along the strike, a column of circles, glyphs spread around the caster. The sequencer expands it into `count` copies; the audit counts them.

count.description: Copies played. 1 = the module plays once.

every.description: Seconds between copies — the STEP. Nothing tweens between them; each copy appears whole.

step.description: Metres each copy moves on from the last, in the spell frame (x right, y up, z forward): [0,0,1.4] marches spikes away from the caster, [0,0.5,0] stacks rings into a column.

turn.description: Degrees each copy is turned around the anchor's up axis relative to the last. With `step` [0,0,r] and turn 360/count the copies stand in a circle; on an orbiting sprite it advances the orbit phase instead.

alternate.description: Flip the spin (and a slash's tilt) on every other copy — a column of circles turning against each other.

scale.description: Size multiplier applied per copy: 0.85 tapers a stack, 1.3 steps a shockwave outward.

jitter.description: Metres of seeded horizontal scatter added to each copy.

when.description: Time of day the emitter runs: `night` scales `rate` by darkness (moths round a lantern, fireflies over a pond), `day` by daylight, fading through dusk and dawn with the day-night script. An emitter at rate 0 with nothing alive costs nothing, so night-only emitters are free by day.

spread.description: Half-angle, in degrees, that each particle's launch direction is randomised within — on ANY shape, unlike coneAngle. 0 fires every particle along `direction` in exact parallel, which is right for a jet and wrong for anything suspended: a box of specks all falling parallel reads as SNOW. 180 is a full sphere, the usual choice for dust hanging in the air.

turbulence.description: Strength of a smooth per-particle wander field, units/sec^2. This is what makes dust look airborne rather than falling — motes curl past each other instead of tracking straight lines. Pair it with `drag` so the wander stays a drift instead of accumulating into a drift-off.

turbulenceSpeed.description: How fast the wander field evolves. Low (~0.2) is a lazy indoor drift; high is agitated.

fadeIn.description: Fraction of each particle's life spent ramping up from nothing to `opacityStart`. Anything meant to already be there — dust, fog, embers — needs this: with 0 every particle POPS into existence at full strength, which is the single clearest tell that an ambient effect is being spawned at you.

radial.description: Aim each particle along the line from the emitter's centre to its own spawn point instead of along `direction`: out = an explosion (needs a sphere/box shape so there IS an offset); in = energy CONVERGING on the centre — the charge-up look, particles born on the shell and flying inward. `spread` still scatters around that line.

sprite.description: The procedural sprite used when no `texture` is given: soft = a radial falloff (smoke, glow); square = a hard-edged square with a one-texel fade (PSX sparks and rain); pixel = a chunky 6x6 blob with stepped alpha (retro embers, motes); flame = an 8x8 pixel-art flame tongue pointing up the screen (PSX fire); ring = a hollow annulus, which is what a splash on the ground actually looks like (pair it with `orient: ground` and a growing `sizeCurve`); streak = a vertical tapered line for rain and sparks (pair it with `orient: velocity`); noise = a torn, cloudy puff with real internal structure, for anything big and slow that would otherwise read as a smooth grey blob — dust banks, smoke fronts (give a noise puff some `spin`: the structure is only visible because it turns). Every sprite but soft is nearest-filtered, so its texels stay hard at any size.

filter.description: Magnification of a `texture` sheet. nearest keeps low-res pixel-art sheets hard-edged (the PSX look); linear smears them. The procedural sprites choose their own filtering and ignore this.

steps.description: PSX banding: colour, size and opacity change in this many hard jumps over a particle's life instead of gliding (each step shows the value at its middle). 0 = smooth. 3–5 is the retro look — a flame that goes white, orange, red, gone reads as 1998; one that fades through every shade in between does not.

snap.description: PSX grid snap, in metres: rendered positions snap to a world grid of this size and quad sizes to multiples of it (a living particle never snaps below one cell). The same wobble as PSX vertex precision. 0 = off. Size it to the effect — around a fifth of the particle size — or it reads as a lattice.

frameRate.description: PSX stepping: the simulation advances in whole ticks of 1/frameRate seconds, so particles jump rather than slide (billboards still face the camera every frame). 0 = every frame. 8–15 is the retro range; flames at 12, lazy smoke lower.

subUV.description: Play the texture as a SPRITE SHEET, per particle. A still sprite drifting is the clearest tell that an effect is dated — every modern smoke, fire or impact particle animates on its own clock.

softFade.description: Metres over which a particle fades as it approaches solid geometry. 0 = off. A quad slicing visibly into the ground is THE thing that reads as cheap, and nothing else fixes it. Costs a scene-depth read, so leave it off for effects that never touch a surface (sparks in mid-air) — and NEVER pair it with `orient: ground`, which lies a quad centimetres above the surface behind it: the fade then measures that gap and erases the whole thing, which looks exactly like the effect failing to spawn.

stretch.description: Stretch each particle along its own velocity, in seconds of travel. 0 = round. Sparks and debris read as DOTS without this — the streak is the motion.

orient.description: What each quad points at. camera = the usual billboard, always square to the viewer. velocity = the quad's long axis is locked to the particle's WORLD velocity and it spins about that axis to face the camera — the difference between rain that falls the way the wind blows and rain that tilts with wherever you happen to be looking, which is what camera+`stretch` gives you (that one rolls the billboard by the SCREEN-space velocity, so the streaks swing as you turn and never foreshorten). ground = laid flat in the XZ plane, facing up: splash rings, ripples, scorch marks. upright = billboard that turns about Y only, so a tall quad stays vertical when you look up — dust banks, distant haze.

sizeCurve.description: [[t, size], …] over normalized life, overriding sizeStart/sizeEnd. A two-point lerp cannot describe a flash — spike, fast falloff, long dim tail — which is most of what separates an impact from a fading blob.

opacityCurve.description: [[t, opacity], …] over normalized life, overriding opacityStart/End and fadeIn.

space.description: world = particles trail behind a moving emitter; local = they ride it.

ground.description: Terrain contact. The host answers 'how high is the ground here' from the streamed terrain, sampled once per particle at birth; a particle that falls to it dies or settles. Terrain only — props, roofs and water are not tested. Needs space: world. Settled particles count toward `max`, so a settling snowfall wants a large one.

mode.description: life = play the sheet once across the particle's lifetime (smoke that billows and dissipates); loop = play it repeatedly at `fps`; random = hold one frame chosen per particle, which is the cheap way to make a hundred identical quads stop looking identical; row = each particle keeps one random ROW (a variant: a brown leaf, a yellow one) and loops that row's columns at `fps` from its own random start — tumbling leaves, flapping moths.

firstRow.description: row mode only: the first sheet row this emitter may use. With `rowCount` it carves one shared sheet into per-emitter strips, so different effects (leaves, moths, ash) share ONE texture and draw in ONE batch.

rowCount.description: row mode only: how many rows from `firstRow` each particle picks its variant among. 0 = to the end of the sheet.

mode.description: kill = the particle ends on contact (a raindrop); settle = it stops where it landed, holds, then fades (snow).

hold.description: settle only: seconds a landed particle rests before fading.

fade.description: settle only: seconds the fade-out takes.

offset.description: Height above the ground a landed particle rests at.

splash.description: Emitters to burst at the contact point — a raindrop's splash. A comma-separated list of entity ids or tags, each optionally `*n` for n particles (`weather-splash-ring,weather-splash*3` = one ring plus three droplets per drop). Those emitters usually have rate 0 and are fired only by this.

splashChance.description: Fraction of landings that splash. Heavy rain lands more than a thousand drops a second and a splash for every one of them is both a fill-rate bill and visually WRONG — real rain reads as scattered rings, not a continuous sheet. 0.1–0.2 for a downpour.

from.description: Inner point (a blade's base, a fist's knuckles): METRES in the anchor object's own axes — its rotation, not its scale.

to.description: Outer point (a blade's tip, a claw's end), same frame.

bone.description: A node under the anchor object whose axes the points are in (a hand bone for a creature's claw): exact name first, else the first node whose name contains it, ignoring case. Omitted = the anchor object itself (a held weapon's entity).

rootOpacity.description: Opacity at `from` relative to `to`: low keeps the smear bright at the tip and see-through at the hilt.

subdivide.description: Points inserted between two frames' samples along a curve through them, so a fast swing draws an arc instead of a polygon.

minSpeed.description: Metres/second the OUTER point must move for a sample to show at full opacity; slower stretches fade toward nothing. A swing's slow raise and its pause at the top then leave no smear, its fast cut does. 0 = every sample at full opacity.

palette.description: Override the element's palette. Omitted = the element's own.

feel.description: Aesthetic bias used when this spell was generated.

texel.description: The spell's PSX grid in world metres per texel, applied to every module that leaves its own `texel` at 0 — so pieces added or rerolled later match the rest. 0 = off.

effect.description: What the payload DOES, as a look: root (vines, chains, holds), stun (stars, chains overhead), slow (hourglass, drips), haste (chevrons, speed lines), shield (hex wards), heal (crosses, rising motes), shadow (dark matter, fading).

channelled.description: buff/debuff: the aura holds for the duration while the caster channels, then fades. Off = the effect flashes when it lands and lingers only briefly.

shape.description: The volume. point = no volume (a single target, the caster).

radius.description: Metres. circle: radius; cone: reach; line: length; point: a body size. The REFERENCE size every visual scales from.

range.description: Metres from the caster the volume is centred at. 0 = on the caster.

windup.description: Seconds from cast start to the payload resolving.

duration.description: Sustained kinds (beam, zone, channel, pulse, buff, summon, portal): seconds the effect holds.

ticksPerSecond.description: Sustained kinds: payload applications per second.

volley.description: projectile: RAPID FIRE — several shots per cast, each with its own flight and impact.

wiggle.description: projectile: shots WEAVE instead of flying dead straight — each its own phase, easing in so it leaves the hand straight. The same curve drives the hit test (wiggleOffset), so a shot hits where it is drawn.

homing.description: projectile: SEEKING shots. Locked at release onto the target nearest the aim (what the crosshair is on); a slow turn rate is out-run by a sprint, a fast one only by cover.

growTo.description: Lingering volumes that grow: the final radius.

height.description: Vertical extent of the volume, metres either side.

intensity.description: How big a deal this spell is — drives module count, light, shake, and how much budget it may spend.

count.description: Shots per cast. 1 = a single shot.

spread.description: Degrees a shot may be turned off the aim. The scatter BLOOMS: the first shot flies at 0.3× this, the last at the full spread, so a burst reads as sustained fire rather than a shotgun.

jitter.description: Metres each shot's launch point is scattered around the hand — a barrage, not a single-file line.

amplitude.description: Metres a shot sways either side of its line. 0 = dead straight.

wavelength.description: Metres of flight per full sway.

vertical.description: Metres a shot bobs up and down, on its own phase and a slightly shorter wavelength — with a side sway the shot traces a loose corkscrew instead of a flat zig-zag. 0 = level.

turnRate.description: Degrees/sec a shot steers toward its target. 0 = flies straight.

acquire.description: Metres from the caster a target may be locked at.

cone.description: Degrees either side of the aim a target may be locked in.

sheet.description: Spritesheet data-asset id. Its grid is the flipbook: columns are frames, rows are colour variants.
