row.description: Sheet row. 5 is the greyscale variant in the purchased library — leave it and let `color` tint.

size.description: Metres — the quad's width; height follows `aspect`.

orient.description: billboard faces the camera; ground lies flat (marks, runes); vertical stands upright and yaws toward the camera (a slash, a wave); facing stands upright with its face along the spell direction (a portal); velocity is a camera-facing quad rolled onto the anchor's motion; world is fixed IN THE WORLD, never turning to the camera: the art's top along the motion (a projectile) or, at rest, upright and square to the spell direction (a stuck spear). Pair it with `crossed`.

crossed.description: world: a second quad crossed at 90° around the long axis, so the shape holds from every side (the PSX crossed-plane trick) instead of vanishing edge-on.

spin.description: Radians/sec the quad turns in its own plane. Lying on the ground that is a yaw; standing up it is a roll around a horizontal axis, which reads wrong on most symbols — the symbol catalog says which may.

yaw.description: Fixed rotation around the facing axis, radians.

randomYaw.description: Roll `yaw` per play — cheap variety for repeated impacts.

cell.description: [col, row] of ONE sheet cell shown as a static SYMBOL (a sigil, a glyph, an arrow) instead of playing the sheet as a flipbook. `fps`/`loop` are ignored; the symbol lives for `duration` (0 = the phase, or 0.6 s).

glow.description: A halo around a SYMBOL (`cell` set), built from its own shape: 0 = none, 1 = a clear glow, 2+ = blazing. Banded into PSX steps when the spell has a texel grid.

glowSize.description: How far the halo reaches, as a fraction of the symbol's size.

glowColor.description: Halo colour: a palette slot or #rrggbb.

orbit.description: Metres the quad circles the anchor at, around its up axis. 0 = sits on the anchor.

orbitSpeed.description: Radians/sec along the orbit; negative runs the other way.

orbitPhase.description: Starting angle on the orbit, radians (0 = in front of the anchor). `repeat.turn` advances it per copy.

emitter.description: The emitter, in the `particles` component's own vocabulary. colorStart/colorEnd are overridden by the module's `color`/`colorEnd` unless they are left white.

burst.description: Particles spawned the moment the module starts.

stream.description: Keep emitting at the emitter's `rate` for the module's duration — channels, trails, auras.

radius.description: Outer radius in metres at scale 1.

inner.description: Inner radius as a fraction of the outer. 0 = a filled disc (a rune, a portal floor).

orient.description: ground lies on the terrain; vertical stands upright yawed toward the camera; facing stands upright with its face along the spell direction (a portal); billboard faces the camera.

expand.description: Scale at birth and at death: a shockwave runs 0.1 → 1, a rune holds 1 → 1. `sizeCurve` overrides.

soft.description: Edge softness. 0 is a hard band; 1 fades across the whole width.

texture.description: Texture asset id laid across the disc (a rune, a sigil). Omitted = a procedural soft band.

arc.description: Degrees of the disc that are drawn, centred on the spell direction: 360 is a full ring, 90 a wedge in front of the caster.

noise.description: Breaks the band with scrolling noise so it reads as energy rather than a drawn circle.

swirl.description: Spiral distortion strength — the portal look. 0 = none.

drape.description: Ground rings follow the terrain under them (needs the host's ground probe).

height.description: Vertical/billboard: metres above the anchor the centre sits.

sheet.description: Decal-sheet data-asset id (written by `fx.mjs decals`). Its texture is NOT plain art: R is WHEN each texel appears (0 = at the strike point, 1 = last), G is the art's own brightness, A is coverage.

cell.description: [col, row] of the decal on its sheet.

size.description: Metres across (the cell's width); depth follows `aspect`.

aspect.description: Width / depth. >1 stretches the mark across the spell direction.

grow.description: Seconds for the reveal front to run from the strike point to the rim. Cracks race along their own lines, vines creep, flowers open stem-first — the order is baked in the sheet. 0 = the whole mark at once.

edge.description: Width of the glowing growth front, in reveal units (0 = no front). It fades once growth completes.

edgeColor.description: Colour of the growth front: a palette slot or #rrggbb.

shade.description: How much the art's own brightness shades the colour: 0 flat, 1 the drawn detail at full contrast.

fadeOut.description: Seconds after its life the mark takes to go — faded, or run backwards when `recede`.

recede.description: Die by running the reveal backwards (vines withdraw, frost retreats to the centre) instead of fading.

yaw.description: Radians around up, on top of facing the spell direction.

randomYaw.description: Roll the yaw per play — repeated impacts stop looking stamped.

drape.description: Follow the terrain under the mark (needs the host's ground probe).

style.description: energy = noisy fresnel rim (barriers, orbs, charge-ups); glass = clean thin rim (bubbles, wards); smoke = dense normal-blended body (a cloud, a void); wire = a lattice of noise lines (arcane cages).

fresnel.description: Rim power — higher is a thinner, brighter edge. 0 = flat.

noise.description: How much scrolling 3D noise breaks the surface.

dissolve.description: [[t, threshold]] — the surface burns away where noise < threshold. A curve 0 → 1 is a shell that dissolves as it dies; 1 → 0 is one that assembles.

squash.description: Vertical scale: a dome on the ground is ~0.6, a tall bubble 1.4.

radius.description: Base radius, metres.

topRadius.description: Radius at the far end. Omitted = same as `radius` (a pillar); 0 = a cone to a point.

orient.description: up = a pillar out of the ground; forward = a cone along the spell direction (breath, spray); down = hanging from the sky onto the anchor.

scroll.description: Noise scroll speed along the axis; positive = base → far end.

edgeFade.description: Fade at the silhouette so the tube has no hard vertical edges.

capFade.description: Fraction of the height faded out at the base and at the far end.

length.description: Metres along the spell direction when there is no target (or `toTarget` is off).

toTarget.description: Span anchor → target when the frame has one.

core.description: Bright inner core as a fraction of width. 0 = none.

style.description: energy = soft noisy glow; laser = hard clean edge; plasma = fat writhing body.

scroll.description: Noise scroll speed toward the far end, metres/sec.

jitter.description: Metres of sideways displacement per segment.

refreshHz.description: How often the path re-rolls — the flicker.

count.description: Independent strands, each with its own path — a channelled storm rather than one arc.

spread.description: count > 1: metres the far ends scatter around the target.

arc.description: line = anchor to target/direction; sky = strikes DOWN onto the anchor from `length` metres up; ground = crawls along the terrain outward from the anchor in a random direction.

intensityCurve.description: [[t, multiplier]]. Default is a flash: spike, then decay.

asset.description: Model asset id. Omitted = the procedural `primitive`.

primitive.description: Procedural bodies for when no model is given.

size.description: Metres, longest extent.

motion.description: drop = falls from `from` metres up and lands as the module ends; rise = comes up out of the ground; hover = bobs in place; orbit = circles the anchor; launch = flies up and away; forward = glides `from` metres along the spell direction (a projection, an afterimage).

from.description: drop: start height above the anchor; rise: depth below it. 0 = auto.

spread.description: count > 1: radius they scatter or orbit within.

tint.description: Colour the body with the palette; off keeps the asset's own material.

sheet.description: Symbol sheet whose cells are drawn BODIES (role `object`: spikes, crystals, rocks, orbs, blades, upright, base at the bottom). When set, every body is a camera-facing drawing standing in the world instead of a 3D primitive — same motion, the spell's own art style.

cells.description: [col, row] cells of `sheet`; each body takes one in turn.

width.description: Camera-facing ribbon: metres across. Ignored with `edge` (the edge's two points set the width).

length.description: Seconds of history the ribbon covers.

taper.description: Narrow toward the tail. With `edge` the inner point slides toward the outer one as a sample ages, so a blade's smear thins to its tip's line.

falloff.description: How fast the ribbon dims behind its leading edge: brightness = (1 - age/length)^falloff. 1 = a linear fade over the whole history (a sheet); 2.5-4 keeps only the last stretch bright, so a fast swing reads as an edge cutting air with a short glowing wake instead of a filled fan.

coreColor.description: A third, HOT colour for the brightest band (palette slot or #rrggbb): the ribbon then ramps in hard steps core -> `color` -> `colorEnd` as it dims, and with `edge` the brightness also leans toward the outer point, so the hot core runs along the blade's leading edge near the tip. Omitted = the two-colour fade.

edge.description: SWEPT ribbon (a weapon trail): each frame samples TWO points on the anchor object and the ribbon spans them, so it is the surface the edge swept through, not a camera-facing strip. Anchor it on `caster` (the weapon's entity, or a body plus `bone`) with `follow`. Omitted = a camera-facing ribbon behind one moving point (a projectile's tail).

radius.description: circle: radius; cone: reach; line: length. Metres.

windup.description: Seconds the fill takes to reach the rim — the clock the target reads.

hold.description: Seconds the volume stays live after the windup.

growFrom.description: Live volumes that GROW: scale at the start of the hold, reaching 1 at its end.

curtain.description: Height of the vertical curtain, metres. 0 = auto from radius.

rimOpacity.description: The rim is the only number a dodge is judged against — keep it the brightest part, but not blown out.

dash.description: Rim dashing, 0..1: 0 is a solid band, 0.5 draws dashes as long as their gaps — the PSX marker look.

height.description: Vertical extent the drape is clamped to — keep it equal to the hit test's `delivery.height`.

radius.description: Outer reach of the arc, metres.

inner.description: Inner radius as a fraction of the outer: near 1 a thin crescent, near 0 a fat cleave.

sweep.description: Degrees the arc covers, centred on the spell direction.

tilt.description: Roll of the cutting plane around the spell direction: 0 = a horizontal cleave, 90 = a vertical overhead chop, ±45 diagonal.

reverse.description: Sweep the other way (right-to-left for a cleave, bottom-to-top for a chop).

sweepTime.description: Fraction of the life the leading edge takes to cross the arc; the rest is the tail fading out.

tail.description: Length of the trailing fade behind the leading edge, as a fraction of the sweep.

height.description: Metres above the anchor the arc's centre sits (chest height for a cleave).

core.description: How bright the leading edge is, toward the glow colour.

strength.description: Metres of camera displacement felt by a camera at the effect.

range.description: Metres over which the shake fades out. A camera at the effect feels the full `strength`, one at `range` or further feels nothing (quadratic falloff between). 0 disables the falloff — every camera in the world shakes, which is almost never what you want.

asset.description: Sound asset id, or a comma list of variants: one is picked at random per play.

__schema33.description: Stable key so a human tweak or an agent's note can name this module.

__schema35.description: The library preset this came from — provenance for tweak-and-regenerate, never read at runtime.

at.description: origin = where the spell resolves (the volume's centre, the impact point); caster = the casting body; target = the targeted body or point; path = the projectile in flight (travel phase); ground = origin projected onto the terrain.

socket.description: caster/target only: a named attach point — rightHand, leftHand, chest, head, feet — resolved by the host to a bone-socket entity under that body. A missing socket falls back to the body itself.

offset.description: metres in the anchor's own frame: x right, y up, z FORWARD along the spell direction.

local.description: caster/target only: `offset` is in the anchor OBJECT's own axes (its rotation, not its scale) and the module faces with it — a point on a held weapon, such as its tip, that turns with the blade. Pair with `follow` (and a particle emitter's `space: local`) to ride it. false = the spell frame described under `offset`.

follow.description: Keep tracking the anchor for the module's whole life (a hand mid-swing, a projectile in flight) instead of sampling it once at start.

__schema48.description: Seconds it lives. 0 = natural length (a flipbook's frames, a burst's longest particle) or, for sustained kinds, the phase length.

__schema52.description: Where colour fades toward over life, for kinds that fade (particles, trail, beam core).

__schema54.description: additive = light (nearly everything magical); normal = matter that occludes (smoke, a poison cloud).

__schema61.description: PSX look: quantise the procedural shading to this many cells across the shape (0 = off, 16–32 reads as pixel art). Rings, shells, columns and beams snap their noise and bands to the grid; masks and sprites switch to nearest filtering.

__schema63.description: PSX look in WORLD units: metres per texel (0 = off; overrides `pixel`). Every module of a spell shares one, so a 12 m shockwave and a 1 m slash are pixelated at the same size and stay so as they grow — 0.03 matches the symbol sheets' own density at typical sizes (coarser turns line art to mush). Textured kinds resample their art onto the same grid.

__schema65.description: Alpha steps (0 = smooth). 3–5 turns soft falloffs into hard bands — the other half of the PSX look.

__schema67.description: [[t, multiplier]] over life, on top of the module's own size.

__schema70.description: Play this module as a STEPPING sequence — spikes that erupt one after another along the strike, a column of circles, glyphs spread around the caster. The sequencer expands it into `count` copies; the audit counts them.

count.description: Copies played. 1 = the module plays once.

every.description: Seconds between copies — the STEP. Nothing tweens between them; each copy appears whole.

step.description: Metres each copy moves on from the last, in the spell frame (x right, y up, z forward): [0,0,1.4] marches spikes away from the caster, [0,0.5,0] stacks rings into a column.

turn.description: Degrees each copy is turned around the anchor's up axis relative to the last. With `step` [0,0,r] and turn 360/count the copies stand in a circle; on an orbiting sprite it advances the orbit phase instead.

alternate.description: Flip the spin (and a slash's tilt) on every other copy — a column of circles turning against each other.

scale.description: Size multiplier applied per copy: 0.85 tapers a stack, 1.3 steps a shockwave outward.

jitter.description: Metres of seeded horizontal scatter added to each copy.

when.description: Time of day the emitter runs: `night` scales `rate` by darkness (moths round a lantern, fireflies over a pond), `day` by daylight, fading through dusk and dawn with the day-night script. An emitter at rate 0 with nothing alive costs nothing, so night-only emitters are free by day.

spread.description: Half-angle, in degrees, that each particle's launch direction is randomised within — on ANY shape, unlike coneAngle. 0 fires every particle along `direction` in exact parallel, which is right for a jet and wrong for anything suspended: a box of specks all falling parallel reads as SNOW. 180 is a full sphere, the usual choice for dust hanging in the air.

turbulence.description: Strength of a smooth per-particle wander field, units/sec^2. This is what makes dust look airborne rather than falling — motes curl past each other instead of tracking straight lines. Pair it with `drag` so the wander stays a drift instead of accumulating into a drift-off.

turbulenceSpeed.description: How fast the wander field evolves. Low (~0.2) is a lazy indoor drift; high is agitated.

fadeIn.description: Fraction of each particle's life spent ramping up from nothing to `opacityStart`. Anything meant to already be there — dust, fog, embers — needs this: with 0 every particle POPS into existence at full strength, which is the single clearest tell that an ambient effect is being spawned at you.

radial.description: Aim each particle along the line from the emitter's centre to its own spawn point instead of along `direction`: out = an explosion (needs a sphere/box shape so there IS an offset); in = energy CONVERGING on the centre — the charge-up look, particles born on the shell and flying inward. `spread` still scatters around that line.

sprite.description: The procedural sprite used when no `texture` is given: soft = a radial falloff (smoke, glow); square = a hard-edged square with a one-texel fade (PSX sparks and rain); pixel = a chunky 6x6 blob with stepped alpha (retro embers, motes); flame = an 8x8 pixel-art flame tongue pointing up the screen (PSX fire); ring = a hollow annulus, which is what a splash on the ground actually looks like (pair it with `orient: ground` and a growing `sizeCurve`); streak = a vertical tapered line for rain and sparks (pair it with `orient: velocity`); noise = a torn, cloudy puff with real internal structure, for anything big and slow that would otherwise read as a smooth grey blob — dust banks, smoke fronts (give a noise puff some `spin`: the structure is only visible because it turns). Every sprite but soft is nearest-filtered, so its texels stay hard at any size.

filter.description: Magnification of a `texture` sheet. nearest keeps low-res pixel-art sheets hard-edged (the PSX look); linear smears them. The procedural sprites choose their own filtering and ignore this.

steps.description: PSX banding: colour, size and opacity change in this many hard jumps over a particle's life instead of gliding (each step shows the value at its middle). 0 = smooth. 3–5 is the retro look — a flame that goes white, orange, red, gone reads as 1998; one that fades through every shade in between does not.

snap.description: PSX grid snap, in metres: rendered positions snap to a world grid of this size and quad sizes to multiples of it (a living particle never snaps below one cell). The same wobble as PSX vertex precision. 0 = off. Size it to the effect — around a fifth of the particle size — or it reads as a lattice.

frameRate.description: PSX stepping: the simulation advances in whole ticks of 1/frameRate seconds, so particles jump rather than slide (billboards still face the camera every frame). 0 = every frame. 8–15 is the retro range; flames at 12, lazy smoke lower.

subUV.description: Play the texture as a SPRITE SHEET, per particle. A still sprite drifting is the clearest tell that an effect is dated — every modern smoke, fire or impact particle animates on its own clock.

softFade.description: Metres over which a particle fades as it approaches solid geometry. 0 = off. A quad slicing visibly into the ground is THE thing that reads as cheap, and nothing else fixes it. Costs a scene-depth read, so leave it off for effects that never touch a surface (sparks in mid-air) — and NEVER pair it with `orient: ground`, which lies a quad centimetres above the surface behind it: the fade then measures that gap and erases the whole thing, which looks exactly like the effect failing to spawn.

stretch.description: Stretch each particle along its own velocity, in seconds of travel. 0 = round. Sparks and debris read as DOTS without this — the streak is the motion.

orient.description: What each quad points at. camera = the usual billboard, always square to the viewer. velocity = the quad's long axis is locked to the particle's WORLD velocity and it spins about that axis to face the camera — the difference between rain that falls the way the wind blows and rain that tilts with wherever you happen to be looking, which is what camera+`stretch` gives you (that one rolls the billboard by the SCREEN-space velocity, so the streaks swing as you turn and never foreshorten). ground = laid flat in the XZ plane, facing up: splash rings, ripples, scorch marks. upright = billboard that turns about Y only, so a tall quad stays vertical when you look up — dust banks, distant haze.

sizeCurve.description: [[t, size], …] over normalized life, overriding sizeStart/sizeEnd. A two-point lerp cannot describe a flash — spike, fast falloff, long dim tail — which is most of what separates an impact from a fading blob.

opacityCurve.description: [[t, opacity], …] over normalized life, overriding opacityStart/End and fadeIn.

space.description: world = particles trail behind a moving emitter; local = they ride it.

ground.description: Terrain contact. The host answers 'how high is the ground here' from the streamed terrain, sampled once per particle at birth; a particle that falls to it dies or settles. Terrain only — props, roofs and water are not tested. Needs space: world. Settled particles count toward `max`, so a settling snowfall wants a large one.

mode.description: life = play the sheet once across the particle's lifetime (smoke that billows and dissipates); loop = play it repeatedly at `fps`; random = hold one frame chosen per particle, which is the cheap way to make a hundred identical quads stop looking identical; row = each particle keeps one random ROW (a variant: a brown leaf, a yellow one) and loops that row's columns at `fps` from its own random start — tumbling leaves, flapping moths.

firstRow.description: row mode only: the first sheet row this emitter may use. With `rowCount` it carves one shared sheet into per-emitter strips, so different effects (leaves, moths, ash) share ONE texture and draw in ONE batch.

rowCount.description: row mode only: how many rows from `firstRow` each particle picks its variant among. 0 = to the end of the sheet.

mode.description: kill = the particle ends on contact (a raindrop); settle = it stops where it landed, holds, then fades (snow).

hold.description: settle only: seconds a landed particle rests before fading.

fade.description: settle only: seconds the fade-out takes.

offset.description: Height above the ground a landed particle rests at.

splash.description: Emitters to burst at the contact point — a raindrop's splash. A comma-separated list of entity ids or tags, each optionally `*n` for n particles (`weather-splash-ring,weather-splash*3` = one ring plus three droplets per drop). Those emitters usually have rate 0 and are fired only by this.

splashChance.description: Fraction of landings that splash. Heavy rain lands more than a thousand drops a second and a splash for every one of them is both a fill-rate bill and visually WRONG — real rain reads as scattered rings, not a continuous sheet. 0.1–0.2 for a downpour.

from.description: Inner point (a blade's base, a fist's knuckles): METRES in the anchor object's own axes — its rotation, not its scale.

to.description: Outer point (a blade's tip, a claw's end), same frame.

bone.description: A node under the anchor object whose axes the points are in (a hand bone for a creature's claw): exact name first, else the first node whose name contains it, ignoring case. Omitted = the anchor object itself (a held weapon's entity).

rootOpacity.description: Opacity at `from` relative to `to`: low keeps the smear bright at the tip and see-through at the hilt.

subdivide.description: Points inserted between two frames' samples along a curve through them, so a fast swing draws an arc instead of a polygon.

minSpeed.description: Metres/second the OUTER point must move for a sample to show at full opacity; slower stretches fade toward nothing. A swing's slow raise and its pause at the top then leave no smear, its fast cut does. 0 = every sample at full opacity.

item.description: An item definition (assets/items/<id>.json). Inventories hold { itemId, qty } stacks — one cell each — that point here, so editing a file updates every copy.

__schema2.description: Broad category for filtering and UI grouping; `slots` decides wearability, not this.

__schema4.description: Slot kinds this item may be worn in (a one-handed sword: [primary, secondary]; a charm: [trinket] fits either trinket slot). Empty = carry-only.

__schema6.description: Maximum quantity per stack (one grid cell). 1 = unique instances (every piece of gear).

__schema8.description: Kilograms per unit; carried AND worn items count against capacity.

__schema10.description: Base price of one unit in copper (100 copper = 1 silver, 100 silver = 1 gold). A shop sells at its `markup` of this and buys at its `buyRate`; 0 = worthless (vendors will not buy it).

__schema13.description: Maximum durability points (weapons, shields, armour). Each death costs every WORN item 10% of this (rounded up, at least 1); at 0 the item is BROKEN — still worn and drawn, but its modifiers stop applying until a repairer mends it (dialogue `openRepair`). Each owned instance keeps its current points on its stack (`durability`). Absent = never wears (food, materials, trade goods).

__schema15.description: Texture asset id (assets/textures/…) drawn in the inventory cell; absent = the name's initials.

__schema17.description: Accent colour for the cell/tooltip; defaults to the rarity colour.

__schema19.description: Flat additions applied while WORN: attributes (strength…) feed the formulas, derived stats (maxHp, armor, crit…) add after them. crit and spellCrit are percent points.

__schema21.description: Minimums to equip, checked against the character's level and EFFECTIVE attributes (base + allocated + worn).

__schema23.description: For `bag`-slot items: the grid this bag grants while worn. A bag must be empty to be swapped or removed.

__schema25.description: Held in BOTH hands (a greatsword, a greataxe, a staff, a bow). While it is worn in `primary`, the `offhand` item stays equipped but INACTIVE: no modifiers, not drawn, no stance (it still counts toward weight). The offhand slot shows greyed out. Nothing is unequipped either way.

__schema27.description: Skills an item carries: the verbs it puts on its wearer's bar while worn or held.

__schema28.description: Ability id on the primary attack (left click) while this item is the weapon in hand.

__schema30.description: Right click while this item is in hand: an ability id, or an `@`-prefixed verb the game reserves — a guard (`@block`, `@parry`, `@ward`) or another held verb (`@steady`, a bow's steady aim). An off-hand item's secondary overrides the main hand's (a shield's `@block` over a sword's `@parry`).

__schema32.description: Ability ids this item contributes to the hotbar while worn or held, in order. The allowance is by what it is: a ONE-handed weapon, an off-hand item and a trinket contribute ONE (the first); a TWO-handed weapon contributes TWO (both hands' worth). Entries past the allowance are ignored (`skillAllowance`, `auditItemSkills` report them). A heavy attack is just a skill the game tags heavy.

__schema35.description: What a CONSUMABLE does when used from the belt (`inventory.use`): an effect id the game resolves. Ignored on worn gear.

__schema37.description: The guard an item gives while held, with its own tuning.

__schema38.description: block = held, absorbs (a shield); parry = timed, turns a blow (a blade); ward = held against magic (a staff); none = the item has no defence (a bow, an offensive staff).

__schema39.description: Seconds after the guard is raised that count as a perfect parry. Absent = the game's default.

__schema41.description: Share of a blocked hit absorbed, 0..1. Absent = the game's default.

__schema43.description: The ward may be thrown onto an ally under the crosshair instead of raised on yourself.

__schema45.description: The ward's school of magic, a name from the game's own list. The game judges a ward against each spell's school (better against some, worse against others). Absent = a plain ward, neither better nor worse.

__schema47.description: What a perfectly timed ward pays back when its school is the right answer to the spell: mana = the cost returned plus mana from the cancelled spell; power = a short damage boost. Absent = no reward.

__schema49.description: Seconds to put this item on or take it off (the authority's timed inventory action; the UI shows progress). Replacing a worn item takes the longer of the two. Absent = the progression's `inventoryDurations`.

__schema51.description: Animation STANCES this item puts its wielder in while held, most specific first — a greataxe: ["Axe2H", "TwoHanded"] borrows every two-handed clip it has no axe version of. The character then plays `<Stance>_<clip>` wherever its model has one (GreatSword_Run, Staff_Attack1, SwordShield_Death). An off-hand item's stance COMBINES with the main hand's: a Sword with a Shield is "SwordShield", then "Sword". Read by the `weapon-stance` script. Empty = no stance (a ring, a potion).

__schema54.description: How this item LOOKS when worn: a choice of parts from a modular model plus a theme sheet. Presentation only — drawn by the `equipment-look` builtin on whatever entity holds the model (a sword in a hand socket), and absent for items with no visible form. Two items can share parts and differ by sheet, or share a sheet and differ by parts.

model.description: Model asset id of the UBERMESH this look is cut from (assets/models/…). The entity that shows it must already draw this model — a look changes parts and texture, never the model.

parts.description: Part NAMES to show, as the model's own part table spells them (unwrap-weapon writes it into the glTF and beside it as <model>-parts.json): one of each family for a weapon — a blade, a guard, a collar, a pommel, the grip. Every other part is hidden. Empty = nothing shows.

texture.description: Texture asset id of the theme sheet (assets/textures/…) — an atlas registered against this model's key. Absent = the sheet baked into the model.

glow.description: Emissive glow on an item. Costs no draw call on a batched (`moving`) model: it is a per-instance value in the same batch as every other item of that model.

effects.description: Standing effects this item carries while it is shown: embers off a blade, frost mist round a guard, a light at a staff's head. Each is a `vfx` asset played for as long as the item is equipped, at a point ON the item that follows it through every swing.

__schema58.description: Emissive colour added on top of the item's own texture.

__schema59.description: Multiplier on `color`. Above ~1 it reads as light; with bloom on it blooms.

__schema61.description: Part NAMES that glow (a blade, not its grip). Omitted = every part the item shows.

__schema63.description: Breathe the glow instead of holding it steady.

min.description: Fraction of full glow at the bottom of a pulse.

__schema67.description: Make the glow MOVE: pixelated noise scrolling over the glowing parts, stepped at 12 fps in 4 bands — the PSX look of the fire overlays. Omitted = a steady glow.

amount.description: 0 = a flat, even glow; 1 = all moving noise (dark gaps between the hot licks). The overlay the fire's ember bed uses.

scale.description: Noise cells across the WHOLE texture sheet — a blade is a thin strip of it, so this wants to be about the sheet's texel count (128 on a 128 px sheet = one cell per texel). Much lower and a blade gets one or two cells.

flow.description: Sheet-heights per second the noise runs along the part. Positive runs toward the blade's TIP (fire climbing), negative toward the guard (poison creeping down); 0 churns in place.

threshold.description: Noise below this adds nothing. High (0.7+) = sparse glints; low = a wash.

churn.description: How fast the pattern EVOLVES in place, on top of `flow`. 1 = the fire overlay's boil; 0.2–0.4 = a slow, oily creep (poison); 0 = a frozen pattern that only scrolls.

frameRate.description: Steps per second the noise advances in (PSX chop). Lower = choppier and slower-looking; 12 matches the fire.

__schema75.description: Fade the glow along the item's length (model +Y — a blade's base to its point): { from: 0.55, to: 0.85 } puts poison on only the last third of the blade, feathered in. With `noise` the edge dissolves through the moving heat rather than a straight line. Batched (`moving`) models only.

from.description: Where along the glowing parts' LENGTH (0 = base, 1 = tip) the glow starts from nothing.

to.description: Where it reaches full strength. Set it below `from` to fade toward the tip instead.

__schema80.description: A standing effect an item carries.

__schema81.description: vfx data-asset id (assets/vfx/<id>.json) — WHAT plays: which particles, their sprite or texture, size, opacity, colour ramp, rate, lifetime, plus rings, shells, beams or a light. The same assets as torches and spells. Keep item effects in one folder (e.g. `items/embers`) so every item using one is ONE asset: particles are batched by look, so a hundred ember swords draw their embers in one call.

__schema82.description: Material asset whose colours are the effect's palette (color → primary, emissive → glow, color darkened → secondary) — recolour an effect without copying it. Omitted = the effect's own element palette.

__schema84.description: A point on an item's model.

__schema85.description: Part NAME of the model (its part table). Omitted = the box of every part the item shows.

__schema87.description: Point in the part's bounding box. "tip"/"base" are the two ends of its LONGEST axis (a blade's point and its root; the ends of a guard's bar), "center" its middle. Or [x, y, z] fractions of the box in the model's own axes, 0..1 on each — [0.5, 0.9, 0.5] is nine tenths of the way up a blade. This is how an emitter is pinpointed.

__schema89.description: Nudge after `at`, in METRES along the model's own axes (they turn with the item).

__schema91.description: item = the effect turns with the item: its modules' offsets, emitter volume and `direction` are in the MODEL's axes — on the longsword +Y runs up the blade toward the tip, ±Z out of the two edges, ±X off the flats — so "up the blade" stays up the blade through every swing. world = upright in the world (yaw only), like a torch. Gravity is always world-down either way, so drips fall and flames rise.

__schema93.description: Size every particle emitter's volume (box/sphere half-extents) to the anchor part's box, so particles are born along the WHOLE blade instead of at one point. [x, y, z] scales each axis — [1, 0.5, 1] is half the blade's length (pair it with anchor at [0.5, 0.75, 0.5] for the upper half); 0 on an axis flattens it. false = the effect's own shapeSize.

__schema95.description: Metres from the camera past which the effect stops simulating (fades out, and back in on approach).

__schema98.description: ENTRUSTED: a specific quest item put in the character's keeping (a sealed package, a ring to deliver). It cannot be traded, dropped, put in the vault, sold or looted, and it stays with its holder through a death (never in a corpse). Ordinary quest loot ("six pelts") is NOT entrusted. Never on an item that can be worn (`slots` must be empty).

__schema100.description: With `entrusted`: the quest id it belongs to — every carried instance is taken back when that quest is handed in (dialogue `turnInQuest`). Absent = it leaves only through the quest's `consume` or a dialogue `take`.

progression.description: Levelling and stat rules (assets/progression/<id>.json). One per game; a character-sheet script names it by id.

__schema0.description: Level cap. Experience past the cap is kept but grants nothing.

__schema2.description: Attribute points granted per level gained; the player spends them one at a time.

__schema4.description: Where every attribute starts at level 1, before any points are spent.

__schema6.description: Experience to go from level L to L+1 = round(base × growth^(L−1)).

__schema8.description: The grid every character always has, bag or no bag.

__schema10.description: Authority-enforced inventory action times. One action per character; destinations and ownership are rechecked at completion.

transfer.description: Seconds for moving or splitting stacks between bag and pockets; rearranging within a container is immediate.

equip.description: Seconds before an equipment change takes effect, including replacing worn gear.

unequip.description: Seconds before removing worn gear takes effect.

__schema15.description: One linear formula per derived stat; a stat the file leaves out keeps the engine default.

maxStamina.description: Stamina pool: pays for physical commitment (swings, blocks).

maxMana.description: Mana pool: pays for casts and wards.

armor.description: Flat armour; a game's damage rules turn it into a share of each physical hit removed.

capacity.description: Carry weight in kilograms before the character is overweight.

crit.description: Chance in PERCENT POINTS (5 = 5%) that a weapon or shot hit is critical; an item's "+1 crit" adds 1.

spellCrit.description: Chance in PERCENT POINTS (5 = 5%) that a spell or heal is critical; an item's "+1 spellCrit" adds 1.

__schema17.description: base + Σ coefficient × effective attribute; worn-item modifiers add after.

creation.description: Character creation rules (assets/creation/<id>.json): archetypes, birth traits and appearance slots. One per game; the gateway and the character-sheet script name it by id.

__schema0.description: Optional look for the creation screen — the game's own UI pieces. Absent = the engine's plain dark look.

__schema1.description: Window frame around the choice panels.

__schema2.description: A 9-slice frame drawn with CSS border-image.

__schema3.description: Texture asset id of the 9-slice image.

__schema4.description: Pixels cut from each edge of the image for the corners/edges (CSS border-image-slice).

__schema5.description: Drawn width of those edges on screen, px (CSS border-image-width).

__schema6.description: How the edges fill: repeat/round for a riveted rail that must not smear.

__schema9.description: The primary button (Create) and a pressed button.

__schema10.description: Frame around an archetype/trait row and its icon (an inventory slot).

__schema11.description: The same frame when chosen (a lit slot).

__schema14.description: A painted picture filling the whole screen behind the character (the creation and character-select screens): the model and its 3D clearing stand in front of it. Absent = the tiled backdrop.

__schema16.description: Ornament drawn under section headings and the title.

__schema20.description: Image for the Back/close control in a panel corner.

__schema22.description: Stepper arrow pointing RIGHT; the left arrow is this mirrored.

__schema24.description: CSS font-family for everything on the screen.

__schema26.description: CSS colours: body text, secondary text, headings, the chosen/focus accent, input wells.

__schema28.description: The 3D clearing behind the creation and character-select screens, built from the game's own art. The engine owns the layout (forest rings, open corridor, cover density); this names the art. Absent = a bare clearing.

__schema29.description: Texture asset id of the ground surface running out to the fog. Absent = flat colour.

__schema31.description: Texture asset id of the worn patch under the character's feet.

__schema33.description: Models for the forest rings round the clearing, picked by weight. Empty = no forest.

__schema35.description: Fixed pieces placed as given (rocks, stumps).

at.description: Position; the character stands at the origin facing +Z.

__schema41.description: Ground-cover sprites round the clearing. Absent = none.

tiles.description: Tile indices (row-major from the top left) scattered as ground cover.

__schema44.description: Model asset id of the base body shown in the preview (and worn when no body slot overrides it).

__schema47.description: A starting lean — Brawn, Cunning, Wise. Adds a few attribute points; locks nothing out.

__schema48.description: Stable id — what a saved build stores. Renaming an id orphans every character that picked it.

__schema50.description: One or two sentences on the creation screen.

__schema52.description: Texture asset id for the archetype's emblem (optional).

__schema54.description: Points added to the progression's base attributes. Keep them small: an archetype is a lean, not a class.

__schema56.description: Names of the paths this archetype can grow into later (shown as a hint; not enforced yet).

__schema59.description: Items a FRESH character of this archetype is given — a starting armour set, equipped — BEFORE the character-sheet script's own startingItems, which never take a worn kit piece off. A restored sheet never gets them again.

__schema61.description: An item given to a fresh character.

__schema64.description: Wear it at once (the first slot that accepts it).

__schema66.description: Copper a FRESH character of this archetype starts with (100 = 1 silver). Absent = the character-sheet script's startingCoins.

items.description: An innate ability picked at creation.

__schema71.description: Ability id the character is born with. The game's combat layer resolves it; the engine only carries it.

__schema72.description: Texture asset id for the trait's icon (optional).

__schema74.description: Archetype ids that offer this trait (a Brawn trait, a Wise trait). Absent = every archetype.

__schema76.description: How many birth traits a character takes.

items.description: A row on the creation screen: sex, face, hair, beard…

__schema80.description: This slot swaps the whole body model (sex). Its option's `model` replaces the base model rather than riding a bone.

__schema82.description: Material NAME on the body that a colour option tints. "Skin" is special: the colour recolours the SKIN TEXELS of every sheet an option opts in with `skin` (the skin-tint contract: every sheet paints skin in one palette, docs/image-generation.md), keeping the painted shading. A body without that material shows no tint — the choice is still kept.

__schema84.description: A DEV PREVIEW row (outfits, armour, headgear — for looking at art on the creator's model): shown on the creation screen, never saved into a build and never drawn in game, where equipment dresses the character.

__schema86.description: A colour slot that recolours the WHOLE sheet of these models (hair colour → the hair ubermesh, whose every texel is hair: styles, beards and moustache alike, so one choice colours them all). The painted strand shading is kept. No `material` needed.

__schema89.description: One choice inside an appearance slot.

__schema91.description: Model asset id drawn for this choice. Absent = nothing to draw yet (placeholder art pending).

__schema93.description: Bone the model rides on (a face or hair piece → the head bone), with offset/rotationDeg/scale/mirrorTo beside it. Usually absent: the creation's `mounts` entry for the model places it, one place for every option and item. Absent with no mount = the option dresses the body model itself (an outfit).

__schema95.description: Position of the model in the socket bone's space (the `bone-socket` offset).

__schema97.description: Rotation of the model in the socket bone's space, XYZ Euler degrees (the `bone-socket` rotationDeg).

__schema99.description: Uniform scale of the model in the socket bone's space. On a BODY-slot option (sex), the scale of the whole character: the female body is the male skeleton at 0.96, so her head and shoulders come down with it.

__schema101.description: A second copy of the model, MIRRORED across its own Z (left/right), on another bone: a shoulder pad modelled for the left arm also sits on the right. Same parts, texture and scale; its own placement in that bone's space.

__schema103.description: Sheet id of the look on the model's packed page (its `tiles` table, as an item's appearance.texture): a face is one tile of the head's page. On a BODY-slot option (sex), with `parts`: the body's UNEQUIPPED look — what every empty equipment slot shows.

__schema105.description: Ubermesh parts of the model this choice shows (a hair style, a beard). Options in different slots that name the SAME model share one piece: their parts are shown together and the texture comes from whichever names one.

__schema107.description: Body triangles weighted to these bones (and every bone under them) are hidden while this piece is worn — a head module replacing the body's own head or hood.

__schema109.description: This option's sheet paints BARE SKIN, so the skin tone recolours it (opt-in: a sheet never opted in is never tinted, whatever its colours — leather and linen sit on skin's hue). true = anywhere on the sheet (the unequipped body); "face" = the whole sheet of a HEAD, with its mouth found and kept as painted (lips never take the tone); a list of part names = only on those parts' islands (the bare fingers of a gloved set).

__schema112.description: BODY-slot options only: how items written for another body (their part names and sheets) map onto this one — the female body wearing an item that names the man's parts.

__schema113.description: Maps looks written for one body onto this one (the female body wearing an item written for the male).

__schema114.description: Exact part name → this body's part ("Belt" → "F_Belt"). Tried before `prefixes`.

__schema116.description: Part-name prefix → replacement ("HumanMale_" → "HumanFemale_"); the longest matching prefix wins.

__schema118.description: Inserted before the extension of an item's sheet ("-f": mmo/human-body-vanguard.png → mmo/human-body-vanguard-f.png) when the model's page HAS that sheet; otherwise the item's own sheet is kept.

__schema120.description: A colour choice (skin tone, lip colour): drawn as a swatch, and tints the slot's `material` on the body.

__schema122.description: Only offered while other slots hold one of these options — { "sex": ["male"] }.

__schema125.description: Where each socketed model (head, hair, helm, shoulder pad) sits on the body — see the mount schema.

items.description: Where a socketed model sits on the body — ONE place for every option and item drawing it: the creator's face, hair and headgear rows and the in-game helm and shoulder items all read it. The first mount whose `requires` the wearer satisfies wins, so a per-sex placement is two entries.

__schema127.description: Model asset id this placement is for (mmo/human-head.glb).

__schema128.description: Bone the model rides on (the head bone for a face, hair or helm).

__schema129.description: Position of the model in the socket bone's OWN space (it inherits the bone's scale).

__schema131.description: Rotation of the model in the socket bone's space, XYZ Euler degrees.

__schema132.description: Uniform scale of the model in the socket bone's space.

__schema134.description: A second copy of the model, MIRRORED across its own Z (left/right), on another bone: a shoulder pad modelled for the left arm also sits on the right. Same parts, texture and scale; its own placement in that bone's space.

__schema136.description: Only for wearers whose appearance holds one of these options — { "sex": ["male"] } for a man's placement.

__schema139.description: Ends that hang — braids, long hair down the back — blended per vertex by the model's baked hang weight (TEXCOORD_1.y: 0 = rides `socket`, 1 = hangs). With no `socket` here they hang PLUMB: as modelled on the body's root, wherever the head is now, so a nod or a tilt bends the hair instead of swinging it. Still one instanced draw; a model without weights rides `socket` whole.

socket.description: Bone the hanging ends ride instead, as it sat against `socket` at the bind pose. Omit it (recommended): a bone that moves against the head in the idles (the chest breathing, hunching, arms folded) drags the ends with it.

game-hud.description: Game HUD skin, equipment layout, audio and navigation policy. Quest areas are compass-only; maps never contain quests or other POIs.

__schema2.description: CSS nine-slice: slice is measured in SOURCE pixels; border is the displayed width. Preserve alpha outside ornaments and keep corner proportions fixed.

__schema6.description: Edge sampling only; corner ornaments always retain their proportions. Use repeat with a seamless straight rail crop.

__schema13.description: Local chat receive filters and detached-window preferences. Filters operate only on messages delivered to this player; they never change server routing or membership.

idleOpacity.description: Background opacity while neither hovered nor focused; message text retains its contrast.

locked.description: Locks moving and resizing during play. Edit UI always unlocks the window.

channels.description: Receive-only feeds. Combat and loot are local gameplay notices, never sendable chat channels.

windowId.description: Owning chat window. Absent = migrate the legacy detached preference.

__schema29.description: Status artwork at source dimensions. Bar rectangles [x,y,width,height] clip the fill without scaling its texture as values change.

clockEntity.description: Entity owning the day-night script; HUD reads its live dayNightHour so offline and replicated clocks match the sky.

compassResponseMs.description: Visual heading smoothing time constant, in milliseconds; zero follows the camera immediately. Rendered every animation frame with wrap-safe angles.

quest.description: Quest definition (assets/quests/<id>.json). Progress belongs to authority-owned quest journals, not this asset.

__schema4.description: One step of a quest. `kind` is a registered action block (spec `questBlocks.action`); its extra fields are that block's.

__schema5.description: Stand inside the objective's `area` (falls back to the quest's).

__schema8.description: What the action is aimed at: an entity id (kill, talk, interact, read, deliver, perform) or an item id (collect). A kill may also name a spawn template id (every spawned copy counts) or `tag:<tag>` (every body carrying the tag, e.g. `tag:creature:wolf`).

__schema11.description: This step's own region (visit, endure, an untargeted perform); absent = the quest's `area`. A step in another town carries its own.

__schema12.description: Approximate search region [world X, world Z], never an exact objective marker. Only the compass may visualize this region. It is also where `visit`, `endure` and an untargeted `perform` count.

__schema16.description: places asset id this step's label tokens resolve against; empty = the quest's `places`. How one quest's steps span several towns.

__schema18.description: Objective ids of this quest that must be complete before this one can progress. Empty = no order.

__schema20.description: Scene this step happens in when it is not the quest's world scene: an instance reached through a `portal` (e.g. a dungeon). Informational — progress is counted wherever the character is (the journal travels with it); tools use it to route there. Absent = the world scene.

__schema22.description: Progress counts only while this holds, tested on the authority (clock, weather, flag, item, quest …; `met` and `bound` never hold here).

__schema23.description: A test against the character (and, for clock/weather, the world it stands in). Every field present must hold; {} is always true.

__schema26.description: With `quest`: none = never accepted; available = can be accepted NOW (not taken, its `requires` done); active = objectives open; ready = objectives done, not handed in; complete = handed in; taken = active or ready.

__schema28.description: A per-character memory flag (set by a `setFlag` action).

__schema30.description: With `flag`: the value it must have (default true).

__schema32.description: Dialogue only: whether this character had spoken to THIS NPC before the current conversation.

__schema36.description: Carries at least `qty` (default 1) of this item id.

__schema39.description: Carries at least this many copper.

__schema41.description: Dialogue only: whether this character's HEARTH is HERE: its respawn bind (netState bind/<bodyId>) is this NPC's `bindPoint` (within 1 m). An innkeeper's "Your bed by the fire is kept."

__schema43.description: Holds while the world clock (netState world/hour, written by the day-night builtin on the authority) is in [from, to). No clock in the scene = never holds.

__schema44.description: First hour of the window (0–24, fractions allowed).

__schema45.description: Hour the window closes. Smaller than `from` = it wraps midnight (20 → 4 is the night).

__schema46.description: Holds while the layer's weather (netState world/weather) is inside this band. No weather in the scene = never holds.

__schema47.description: Precipitation at least this (0 = clear, 1 = the heaviest this world does).

__schema49.description: Precipitation at most this (max 0.05 = dry weather).

__schema51.description: Storm (wind, gloom, lightning) at least this.

__schema53.description: Biome rule ids: holds only while the biome under the character (the winning one, ctx.biomeAt) is one of these. Weather is one state per layer and what it FALLS as is the biome's: `min` 0.3 over snow biomes means snowing HERE.

__schema60.description: Consequences run once, on the authority, the moment this objective completes.

items.description: What happens, on the authority and for this character only, the moment the objective completes.

__schema62.description: Remember something about this character (npc/<bodyId>.flags) — dialogue can then react to it.

__schema69.description: Defeat `target`: an entity id, its `<target>-` prefix, or a spawned `#<target>#` template id (from the project's killEvent).

__schema73.description: Open a conversation with the NPC whose entity id is `target`.

__schema75.description: Use entity `target` (tagged `interactable`): the client sends player.interact; the authority checks owner and range.

__schema77.description: Open the readable entity `target` (an `npc` builtin with `readable: true` — a sign, a slab, a book); its text resolves like dialogue.

__schema79.description: Leave `required` × `item` at entity `target`: interacting with it while carrying the item hands them over (taken from the bags).

__schema81.description: Item id handed over: each interact at `target` takes as many as are still `required` from the bags.

__schema82.description: Stay inside the objective's area (or the quest's) for `seconds`, unbroken, while `when` holds.

__schema84.description: Unbroken seconds to stay inside the area while `when` holds. Leaving or the condition breaking starts the count over.

__schema85.description: Perform the named action (player.perform: /dance, /dig) within `range` of entity `target`, else inside the objective's area (or the quest's); no target and no area = anywhere.

__schema87.description: Perform-action name ("dance", "dig"): the engine vocabulary plus the quest-log's `performActions` asset.

__schema88.description: With a `target`: metres from that entity the performance counts within.

__schema90.description: Approximate search region [world X, world Z], never an exact objective marker. Only the compass may visualize this region. Absent = no compass guidance (an errand inside a town).

__schema92.description: Coins paid on completion, in copper (100 copper = 1 silver, 100 silver = 1 gold).

__schema94.description: Items given on completion. A hand-in is refused while they do not fit the bags.

__schema96.description: Entity id of the NPC (or object, see `source`) who offers it (its dialogue's `acceptQuest`). Empty = granted by a script (quest-log `autoStart` / `autoOffer`).

__schema100.description: Quest ids that must be COMPLETE before this one can be accepted (a chain).

__schema102.description: On hand-in, take the `collect` objectives' items out of the bags (the ore is handed over).

__schema104.description: Suggested level, shown in the journal; never enforced.

__schema106.description: places asset id (assets/places/<town>.json) its text's {dir:id} / {far:id} / {place:id} tokens resolve against — never write a compass word by hand. A step in another town names its own (objective `places`).

__schema108.description: How the quest reaches the player. Absent = `npc` when `giver` is set, else `auto`. Only an `npc` source is advertised (a giver marker); object, presence and auto starts carry no marker, map or compass pointer.

__schema109.description: Offered by a person: an `acceptQuest` in that NPC's dialogue.

__schema111.description: NPC entity id; empty = the quest's `giver`.

__schema113.description: Offered by a thing, not a person: a notice board, a carved stone, a lost satchel — an entity running the `npc` builtin with `face: false` (and `readable: true` for text), whose dialogue carries the `acceptQuest`.

__schema115.description: Entity id of the object; empty = the quest's `giver`.

__schema117.description: Starts by itself, with no announcement of its own: the quest-log of a character watching it (`autoStart` for a fresh journal, `autoOffer` at any time) accepts it on the authority the moment `when` and `area` hold. Nothing advertises it: players find it through leads (rumour, lore, a sight), never a marker.

__schema119.description: Starts once this holds (clock, weather, flag, item, level …); absent = at once.

__schema120.description: Starts once the character stands inside this region.

__schema121.description: Offered by someone or something that is only THERE while a condition holds: an entity running the `npc` builtin plus the `presence` builtin (its `when`: an hour window, weather, a flag). Shared world: it is never removed, only hidden per player, and a conversation open with it holds it until the conversation ends.

performActions.description: A project's extra perform actions (data type `performActions`), added to the engine vocabulary by the quest-log's `performActions` param.

name.description: The word a player types without the slash ("dance").

dialogue.description: What an NPC says (assets/dialogues/<id>.json): a graph of nodes, each a line and the player's choices; choices can test the character (quests, flags, items, coins, hearth bind) and act on the server (quests, shop, vault, repair, hearth bind, soulbound slots, items, coins).

__schema0.description: Where a conversation opens: the FIRST entry whose `if` holds (put quest hand-ins and first meetings before the plain greeting).

__schema2.description: A test against the character (and, for clock/weather, the world it stands in). Every field present must hold; {} is always true.

__schema5.description: With `quest`: none = never accepted; available = can be accepted NOW (not taken, its `requires` done); active = objectives open; ready = objectives done, not handed in; complete = handed in; taken = active or ready.

__schema7.description: A per-character memory flag (set by a `setFlag` action).

__schema9.description: With `flag`: the value it must have (default true).

__schema11.description: Dialogue only: whether this character had spoken to THIS NPC before the current conversation.

__schema15.description: Carries at least `qty` (default 1) of this item id.

__schema18.description: Carries at least this many copper.

__schema20.description: Dialogue only: whether this character's HEARTH is HERE: its respawn bind (netState bind/<bodyId>) is this NPC's `bindPoint` (within 1 m). An innkeeper's "Your bed by the fire is kept."

__schema22.description: Holds while the world clock (netState world/hour, written by the day-night builtin on the authority) is in [from, to). No clock in the scene = never holds.

__schema23.description: First hour of the window (0–24, fractions allowed).

__schema24.description: Hour the window closes. Smaller than `from` = it wraps midnight (20 → 4 is the night).

__schema25.description: Holds while the layer's weather (netState world/weather) is inside this band. No weather in the scene = never holds.

__schema26.description: Precipitation at least this (0 = clear, 1 = the heaviest this world does).

__schema28.description: Precipitation at most this (max 0.05 = dry weather).

__schema30.description: Storm (wind, gloom, lightning) at least this.

__schema32.description: Biome rule ids: holds only while the biome under the character (the winning one, ctx.biomeAt) is one of these. Weather is one state per layer and what it FALLS as is the biome's: `min` 0.3 over snow biomes means snowing HERE.

text.description: What the NPC says. A list = one line picked per visit (small talk). `{name}` is the character's name, `{npc}` the NPC's.

items.description: Something a dialogue choice DOES on the server. A choice's actions run all-or-nothing.

goto.description: Node id to continue at; "end" closes the conversation.

__schema48.description: Add the quest to the journal (refused when it is not available).

__schema51.description: Hand a READY quest in: it completes and pays rewardXp/rewardCoins/rewardItems.

__schema54.description: Open the shop window (a `shop` asset id) on top of the conversation.

__schema59.description: HEARTH bind (the id is kept from when a soul binder did this): the character respawns HERE, at this NPC's `bindPoint` (npc param; default the NPC's own position), instead of the nearest sanctuary. Saved with the character (netState bind/<bodyId>). Every town's innkeeper offers it; the soul binder offers `openSoulbind`.

__schema61.description: Open the SOUL BINDER's window: choose up to `slots` equipment slots and attune each to the item worn there now (sheet `soulslots`; request soul.attune). That item cannot be looted from the character while it stays worn there.

__schema63.description: Most equipment slots a character may have soulbound.

__schema65.description: Copper charged when the character CHANGES which slots are soulbound (a first choice and re-attuning the same slots are free).

__schema67.description: Slots that cannot be chosen (default the worn bag and the belt, which are never looted anyway).

__schema69.description: Open the repair window: every damaged item the character wears or carries, a price each, and Repair all.

__schema71.description: Price factor: mending an item costs ceil(item value × missing/max × rate) copper, at least 1 for any damage.

__schema73.description: The NPC hands the character items (refused when the bags are full).

__schema77.description: The character hands items over (refused when it does not carry them).

__schema81.description: The character pays the NPC (refused when it cannot afford it).

__schema84.description: The NPC pays the character coins and/or experience.

shop.description: A vendor (assets/shops/<id>.json): what it owns, what it pays, what it charges. Live stock is netState shop/<id>.

__schema1.description: Selling price = item `value` × markup, rounded up (an entry's `price` overrides it).

__schema3.description: What the shop pays for an item: `value` × buyRate, rounded down. 0 = buys nothing.

__schema5.description: Item tags or kinds (equipment, consumable, material, misc) this shop buys; empty = anything with a value. Quest items are never bought.

__schema7.description: What the shop OWNS: its own goods, in display order.

qty.description: Units on the shelf; absent = never runs out.

price.description: Price in copper, overriding value × markup.

restockSeconds.description: With `qty`: one unit comes back this often until the shelf is full.

__schema12.description: How many distinct items players sold here it keeps for resale (at the selling price); 0 = sold goods vanish. Oldest go first.

places.description: A town's geography (assets/places/<town>.json), generated by tools/town-npcs.mts from the world: its residents, gates, named places and camps, nearby towns and every continent's capital. Dialogue and quest text refer to these as {dir:id} (north-west), {Dir:id} (North-west), {far:id} (a short walk), {place:id} / {Place:id} (its name).

__schema0.description: [x, z] the directions are measured FROM — the town's centre.

name.description: What people call it ("the Drowned Lantern", "Ashfall"); empty = unnamed.

kind.description: resident | gate | poi | camp | town | capital | point — what generated it.

tooltip.description: Presentation-only tooltip. Text is rendered literally, never as HTML.

socket-map.description: Where props may go in one space, measured from its geometry (authoring/dressing/sockets/<id>.json; written by `dress sockets`, never by hand; authoring-time only, never loaded by the runtime). Free floor, walls with their uninterrupted spans, headroom, and the stairs/doorways that must stay clear.

__schema0.description: Usually the building model's id; a street or plaza map uses its own.

model.description: Asset path of the geometry this was measured from.

sha256.description: Its hash when measured. A differing hash means the map is STALE and must be regenerated.

__schema2.description: The outside door. Route checks start here.

facing.description: Unit vector pointing INTO the building from the door.

__schema10.description: Local Y of the walking surface.

__schema11.description: Local XZ of the corner of cell (column 0, row 0). Columns run +X, rows +Z.

__schema12.description: Cell size in metres (0.25 by default).

__schema15.description: One string per row, one character per cell, from SOCKET_CELLS: ' ' outside, '.' free floor, '#' wall, 'o' unroofed floor, 'S' stair, 'W' well, 'D' doorway, 'E' entry lane, 'H' hearth clearance (walkable; no solid prop), 'A' stair approach/foot/head (walkable; no solid prop; must be reachable), 'x' reserved walking path (walkable; no solid prop; a rug may lie on it).

__schema17.description: Clear height above the floor per cell: one base-36 digit of quarter metres (HEAD_STEP); '.' where there is no floor.

__schema19.description: Room membership per cell: the room's `index` as a base-36 digit; '.' = no room (walls, thresholds).

__schema21.description: Outdoor sites only (`site-sockets`): ground height per cell relative to `floorY`, one base-36 digit of GROUND_STEP (0.05 m) with 'i' = floorY ('0' = -0.90 m, 'z' = +0.85 m); '.' = floorY. Floor props stand on the ground under their centre.

id.description: Unique in the map, e.g. "G-1" (ground) or "U1-2" (first upper floor).

index.description: This room's digit in the level's `room` raster (base 36).

bbox.description: [minX, maxX, minZ, maxZ] of its free cells.

minHead.description: Lowest clear height over the room's free floor, metres.

maxHead.description: Highest clear height: >= 5 m is where a chandelier can hang.

id.description: Unique in the map, e.g. "G-1.N" or "L0-W3". Plans place wall items and wall-backed furniture by this id.

room.description: The room this face looks into.

a.description: LEFT end of the wall face on the floor, as seen from inside the room facing the wall. `t` in a plan is metres from here toward `b` (left to right).

normal.description: Unit vector pointing from the wall INTO the room. A prop placed on this wall faces this way.

spans.description: Stretches [t0, t1] (metres from `a`) that are solid, uninterrupted wall: no door, window, stair or opening. A prop's whole width must fit in one.

height.description: Usable wall height above the floor before the ceiling or a slope starts, metres.

__schema30.description: The circulation mask's walking paths on this level (`circulate`, run by `dress sockets`): their cells are the 'x' cells (keep-clear cells they cross keep their own code). The resolver names the path a solid prop stands on.

name.description: What it is for, as a designer reads it: "the way from the door to the stair", "the walk through G-1".

width.description: Lane width, metres: the resolver's lane (player capsule plus comfort). Its cells are every cell this lane's body overlaps.

points.description: Centre line, local XZ metres: where it leaves the path network, every turn, and its end.

__schema32.description: Named single-prop points the geometry itself implies.

kind.description: What the point is for: "door-side", "sign-bracket", "hearth", "counter", "altar", "bed-nook", "stall". A plan places by id; the kind lets a designer find it.

position.description: Local metres. The placed prop's origin lands here.

yaw.description: Degrees about +Y the placed prop faces (0 = local +Z).

mount.description: Which prop mount this point takes.

outdoor.description: True for points outside the shell (door torches, a sign bracket, a stall pitch).

size.description: [w, h, d] metres of the fixture this point stands for, when the model says so (a hearth's fire opening, from its `.markers.json`). `dress fixtures` sizes the fire from it.

dressing-set.description: A reusable furnished group (authoring/dressing/sets/<id>.json): a desk with its chair, papers and candle; a bed with its chest. Authored once, placed as ONE plan item, so most of a room is chosen from a short menu rather than assembled prop by prop.

__schema2.description: Room roles this group furnishes (same vocabulary as the `dressing` component's `rooms`).

__schema6.description: Floor the whole group needs, [width X, depth Z] metres, in the anchor piece's frame (front = +Z). For the menu; the resolver still checks every member.

__schema10.description: Where each member falls relative to the anchor, in words the menu prints: left/right as seen standing in front of the anchor, facing it ("chest at the foot; nightstand on the left"). A plan item may mirror the set (`mirror: true`) to swap the sides.

__schema12.description: items[0] is the ANCHOR: a single prop whose own `place` is ignored, because the plan places it. Every other member is placed relative to the anchor: `floor` places use the anchor's local frame (`at` = offset from the anchor's centre, +Z = its front; `yaw` relative to it), `on` places name a sibling member. Members may not be sets, and `wall`/`ceiling`/`anchor` places are not allowed inside a set.

__schema14.description: Unique in the plan (or set). Becomes part of the scene entity id, so keep it stable.

__schema15.description: Prefab id of a prop carrying a `dressing` component. Exactly one of `prop` / `set`.

__schema17.description: A dressing-set id: the whole group is placed by its anchor piece and its members expand to items `<id>/<member>`.

at.description: Local XZ of the prop's centre.

yaw.description: Degrees about +Y the prop's front faces (0 = local +Z, 90 = local +X).

wall.description: A wall id from the socket map.

t.description: Metres along the wall from its `a` end to the prop's centre.

height.description: Wall-mounted props only: bottom edge above the floor. Omitted = the middle of the prop's `wallHeight`.

drop.description: Metres from the ceiling down to the prop's top. Only props with a `chain` may drop.

item.description: Id of the item (in this plan, or a sibling inside the same set) whose socket it goes on.

socket.description: Socket id on that item's prop. Empty = the first socket that accepts and still has room.

offset.description: surface only: metres from the socket centre, in the HOST's local X and Z. Omitted = auto-arranged left to right.

yaw.description: Degrees added to the socket's facing.

anchor.description: An anchor id from the socket map.

oneOf.description: Placement by intent: name the room and a preference; the resolver picks a free spot deterministically (never on a path, keep-clear zone or another item; inside the lane, buffer and density rules; honouring the prop's `against` and clearance). Items resolve in plan order, so earlier ones win; one that cannot fit is a violation that says how much room was left. `dress check` prints the spot chosen.

__schema26.description: The room (map room id, e.g. "G-1") it goes in. The resolver picks the spot.

__schema27.description: `wall`: back to a wall, centred on the longest free stretch. `corner`: back to a wall, tucked into a corner. `open`: in the open floor, aligned to the room, as far from everything as the room allows. `near`: as close to `near` as fits, facing it when in the open. Omitted: `wall` for wall-backed and either-way props, `open` for free-standing ones (`near` when `near` is given).

__schema29.description: An earlier item id in this plan, or an anchor kind of the map (hearth, door, stair, sconce...): the spot is chosen as close to it as fits.

__schema33.description: Sets only: true swaps the set's left and right (a nightstand on the left goes on the right; see the set's `shape`). Omitted with an `auto` place = the resolver may mirror the set to make it fit; omitted otherwise = as authored.

__schema35.description: Why it is here (whose desk, what trade). For the reviewer; never read by the resolver.

__schema37.description: This item is the room's declared SET PIECE (the throne, the great table): it may stand in the room's keep-clear centre. One per room, two in a great hall.

__schema39.description: Values for the placed prefab's declared props (a hearth fire's `size`), written onto the instance by `dress apply`. Single props only; omit to take the prefab's defaults, which is what keeps a shared look editable in one place.

dressing-plan.description: A designer's choices for one space (authoring/dressing/plans/<id>.json, checked by `dress check`, installed by `dress apply`): which props and sets, on which wall, floor point, ceiling point or socket. No transforms: the resolver computes them from the socket map and each prop's `dressing` declaration.

__schema2.description: The room programme, keyed by room id from the map. Every room must appear and be furnished; an empty room is a finding.

role.description: What the room is: bedroom, kitchen, shop, storage… (the `dressing` vocabulary).

also.description: Other things the same room is used for. A one-room cottage is kitchen, hall and storage at once: props tagged for any of these roles belong.

owner.description: Resident id(s) who use it, for the reviewer.

scale.description: This room's scale class when it differs from `space.scale` (a giant hall's ratkin-infested store).

cultures.description: This room's cultures when they differ from `space.cultures`.

keepCentre.description: Override `space`'s centre rule for this room: true keeps its middle clear, false lets furniture stand there (a tavern's tables).

__schema9.description: What kind of place this plan dresses, at what scale, for whom. The menu (`props menu --plan`) offers only matching props; the resolver refuses the rest.

__schema10.description: `dungeon`: every room keeps its MIDDLE clear (a central keep-clear zone sized from the room; only a centrepiece/set piece stands there), solid props keep `pathMargin` (default 0.4 m) off every walking path, doorway and stair, and the stair/doorway buffers are wider (1.0 / 1.6 m). `building`/`site`: the centre rule is off unless a room sets `keepCentre`; the review still scores centre clutter.

__schema12.description: The scale class of the people who live here (dressing vocabulary: tiny, small, human, large, giant). Props of another class (not `any`) are refused.

__schema14.description: Whose place this is (dressing vocabulary: civic, rural, bandit, crypt, giant, ratkin, anansi...). Props sharing none of them (and not `any`) are refused.

__schema16.description: Placed geometry on this space's floor that the socket map does not show (statues, pillars, set-piece models): no prop may overlap one.

at.description: Local XZ of the footprint centre.

size.description: [width X, depth Z] metres before yaw.

height.description: Metres above the floor it occupies.
