owner-overrides.description: The owner's hand edits to placed props (move, turn, scale, swap, delete, add), kept beside what placed them and applied LAST by every re-apply (`dress apply`, installers via `dress owner-apply`). Written by the editor, never by agents; agents read them as fixed (`dress overrides`).

__schema1.description: The dressing plan these edits sit on (`<plan>.owner.json`).

__schema3.description: The scene these edits sit on (`authoring/owner-overrides/<scene>.json`): installer-placed props.

__schema5.description: `map`: positions in the plan's map-local frame (apply adds --at/--yaw). `scene`: positions in the entity's parent frame, applied as they are.

__schema7.description: Plan files: the install frame (--at, --yaw degrees) the editor converted the owner's edits with. A re-apply with another frame re-bases them first (rebaseOwnerOverrides), so they stay where the owner put them in the scene.

__schema11.description: Plan file: the plan item / placement id (`<item>/<member>` for a set member; `owner-…` for an owner-added prop). Scene file: the entity id.

__schema12.description: The owner's values; omitted fields keep what the plan/installer resolves.

__schema13.description: A placed prop's state as the owner left it (or as the agent had placed it, under `from`).

__schema14.description: Where the prop's ORIGIN goes: the plan's map-local metres (plan file) or the scene frame (scene file).

__schema15.description: Degrees about +Y the prop faces, in the same frame.

__schema17.description: Uniform scale of the placed instance (1 = as catalogued).

__schema19.description: Prefab id: set = swapped for this catalogue prop.

__schema21.description: The owner deleted it: never re-added by any re-apply.

__schema23.description: Placed by the owner (not from the plan / installer): `set.prop` and `set.pos` are required.

__schema25.description: Scene entity id an owner-added prop is installed under (kept so the editor's id survives a re-apply).

__schema27.description: Plan file, owner-added: the map room it belongs to (its culling group); "" or omitted = outdoors.

__schema29.description: What the agent had placed before the owner's first edit: the learning signal compares the two.

__schema30.description: Reason classes (ownerReasons): floating = moved down, sunk = moved up, moved, rotated, scaled, swapped, deleted, added.

__schema33.description: ISO time of the last edit.

__schema35.description: Why, in the owner's words, when given.

theme.description: A theme data asset: the complete per-location skin. One dungeon plan + N themes = N locations. Generate the engine material docs from it with materialsForTheme(); resolve mesh world-UV scales with uvScaleFor().

__schema0.description: Human-readable theme name, e.g. "The Ossuary Vaults".

__schema1.description: One or two sentences of art direction — what this location should feel like.

__schema3.description: The colours this theme's light fixtures CAST — part of the dressing vocabulary, not the layout. Dressing passes read these when placing lights so a re-skin changes the light along with the walls.

__schema4.description: Colour cast by this theme's warm fixtures (torches, braziers, hearths).

__schema6.description: Colour cast by this theme's cold sources (moonlight shafts, fungus, sorcery).

__schema7.description: Colour cast by accent-slot fixtures (runes, crystals, shrines) — pairs with the `accent` slot.

__schema8.description: Role slot → texture set. Compilers and dressing passes reference SLOTS, never material ids, so swapping the theme re-skins everything built from the same plan.

__schema9.description: Walkable worked surfaces — room floors, corridor floors.

__schema10.description: Texture asset id — the relative path under assets/textures/ INCLUDING extension (e.g. "crypt-a/mossy-brick-wall.png"), which is how the asset loader keys textures. Omit for a flat-colour slot (graybox, or a slot this location genuinely leaves untextured).

__schema12.description: Base colour, multiplied with `map` when one is set (leave #ffffff to show the texture untinted; darken it to grime a whole slot). With no `map` this IS the slot's look.

__schema13.description: PBR roughness 0..1. Omitted = engine material default (0.85, near-matte — right for stone). Set it low only on slots that should read wet or polished.

__schema15.description: PBR metalness 0..1. Omitted = engine material default (0.05). Really only the `metal` slot wants a high value; metallic stone reads as oily.

__schema17.description: Texture asset id of a tangent-space normal map (OpenGL +Y convention), same id form as `map`. Shares `map`'s UV transform, so the theme's single `uvScale` covers both.

__schema19.description: METRES PER TEXTURE TILE [u, v] in world space — NOT a UV repeat count. [3, 3] = one tile every 3 m. REQUIRED whenever `map` is set: the shell materials generated from a theme pin `repeat` to [1, 1] and the mesh carries `uv: { mode: "world", scale }` instead, so this value is what keeps a re-skin from silently changing the texture's world size (the counting-stones bug). Compilers read it with `uvScaleFor(theme, slot)` and bake it into the mesh they emit.

__schema22.description: One role slot: which texture set a semantic surface role wears in this theme, plus the metres-per-tile that keeps its world scale stable across re-skins.

__schema24.description: Overhead shell surfaces — flat ceilings and vault faces.

__schema25.description: Carved edging: door frames, cornices, balustrades, pilasters — the detail band between shell slots.

__schema26.description: The theme's signature flourish — runes, bone, glow, gilt. Small doses; pairs with light.accent.

__schema27.description: Natural/unworked stone — cave walls, tunnel shells, rubble, stalagmites. The other half of the worked/natural mix; transition assemblies blend wall→rock.

__schema28.description: Structural and prop timber — beams, planking, crates, scaffolds.

__schema29.description: Ironmongery — grates, hinges, sconces, portcullises, banding.

__schema30.description: Stair treads and risers. Separate from `floor` because steps are cut pieces that read best with their own tighter texture, and stairs are exactly where a wrong uvScale is most visible.

__schema31.description: Water surfaces, when this location has any. The only optional slot — many dungeons are dry.

cancel.description: False starts a 20-second camp; true cancels it. The authority chooses the sending peer, requires stillness and no combat/loot lock, saves before acknowledging logout. Closing the connection uses the 60-second disconnect grace instead.

peerId.description: Its owner's peer id (the character id on a cluster).

name.description: Region name, what the player reads.

from.description: Region id left, or null when the body was in no zone.

hitreg.armor-atlas.name: Armor / Weapon Atlas
hitreg.armor-atlas.description: Register generated artwork against a UV key and write a game-ready atlas. Character armor uses a 256px sheet; longsword weapons use a 128px sheet with weapon-sized bleed by default.

key.label: UV key
key.description: The flat PNG color-key sheet supplied to the image generator.

art.label: Generated art
art.description: The generated PNG painted over the key layout. It must have exactly the same dimensions as the UV key.

sheet.label: Sheet
sheet.description: Which key this art was painted over. Character armor defaults to 256px output; longsword defaults to 128px output. Each sheet has its own slot table.

name.label: Output name
name.description: Texture id below assets/textures; folders are allowed. The .png suffix is added automatically.

size.label: Atlas size
size.description: Square output size in pixels. Presets are character armor 256px and longsword 128px; set this only when intentionally overriding the sheet preset.

bleed.label: Bleed
bleed.description: Padding texels dilated around UV islands. Presets are armor 8px and longsword 3px, keeping the same relative gutter after downsampling.

filter.label: Filter
filter.description: Box filtering is the normal downsampling path; nearest preserves hard source pixels.

slices.label: Keep slices
slices.description: Write per-island diagnostic PNGs into the local tool-run record.

artMargin.label: Artwork margin
artMargin.description: Include artwork outside the keyed islands when estimating registration.

skip.label: Skip regions
skip.description: Optional comma-separated island names that are absent from this set, such as hood,ornament.

hitreg.wfc-3d.name: 3D Prefab WFC
hitreg.wfc-3d.description: Collapse a 3D tile grid into a reusable composite prefab. Every occupied cell is a nested prefab instance; the tool never emits raw geometry. Tilesets are hand-authored (exact socket matching) or LEARNED from a modelled kit by tools/wfc-3d/kit.mjs (parts + example structures in, atlased modules + cell prefabs + a tileset with learned face pairs out).

tileset.label: Prefab tileset
tileset.description: JSON describing prefab tiles, their six face sockets, weights, allowed Y rotations, optional boundary sockets, and pinned cells — or a learned tileset written by the kit importer (assets/wfc/<kit>.tileset.json), which adds allowed face pairs, an outside tile and UV-alignment overrides. See tools/wfc-3d/README.md.

name.label: Output prefab
name.description: Prefab id below assets/prefabs; folders are allowed. The .json suffix is added automatically.

height.label: Height (Y)
height.description: Grid cells along world Y. Use 1 for a single-layer layout.

attempts.label: Retry attempts
attempts.description: Fresh deterministic collapses attempted after contradictions.

origin.label: Prefab origin
origin.description: Centered keeps the composite anchor at the bottom-center; minimum starts cell 0 at the anchor.

hitreg.mesh-dc.name: Blender to DC
hitreg.mesh-dc.description: Import grouped Blender solids as editable volumes with their original palette and an entrance anchor.

source.label: Blender mesh export
source.description: JSON created by the Blender exporter. Each group becomes an editable volume; a role-noise table embedded in it (source.noise) roughens natural-rock roles and leaves built work crisp.

name.label: Output name
name.description: A new name for the imported assets.

voxelSize.label: Surface resolution (m)
voxelSize.description: Smaller values preserve finer details and take longer to load.

maxCells.label: Maximum cells per group
maxCells.description: Limits import size. Split oversized groups or increase surface resolution.

materialId.label: Palette material ID
materialId.description: Optional new material ID. Defaults to the output name followed by /dc-palette.

group.label: Group name
group.description: Optional exact group name. Leave empty to import all groups.

hitreg.statue-maker.name: Statue Maker
hitreg.statue-maker.description: Freeze a character or creature into a smooth-shaded static sculpture and an anchored prefab. Accepts a portable recipe/model bundle made by the CLI.

bundle.label: Statue recipe bundle
bundle.description: Portable JSON containing recipe and embedded source GLBs. Create with statue-maker/cli.mjs pack. Material and optional pedestal must already exist in the target project.

hitreg.poi-review.name: POI Site Reviewer
hitreg.poi-review.description: Plan a sized POI workflow with construction handoffs, plan terrain access, and review final sites against terrain triangles and player capsules. Shared CLI/API, agent-agnostic. Read-only; actual construction and visual review remain required.

options.label: Plan POI workflow and measured brief

bundle.label: Portable review or route-search bundle
bundle.description: plan-poi: request matching poi-request-schema.json. review: portable bundle from cli.mjs pack. plan-route: world and search matching terrain-route-schema.json. See README.md for the agent-agnostic process.

default.description: Value used when an instance does not set this prop.

bindings.description: Where the value is written on expand: "<localEntityId>/components/<component>/<field>".

description.description: What this knob does, in one line — shown as inspector help and read by agents.

kind.description: Control type. Omit to infer from `default` (and from `options`, which implies enum).

label.description: Human-facing name. Omit to use the prop key.

group.description: Inspector section, e.g. "Handling" or "Damage". Ungrouped knobs come first.

min.description: Inclusive lower bound — with max, renders a slider.

max.description: Inclusive upper bound — with min, renders a slider.

unit.description: Unit suffix shown beside the value: "m", "m/s", "deg", "rpm", "%".

options.description: Allowed values — presence implies an enum dropdown.

assetKind.description: For kind "asset": which library to pick from ("material", "model", "prefab", …).

advanced.description: Hide behind the inspector's “advanced” disclosure; agents still see it.

name.description: Project id. Must match the folder name under projects/, since asset ids namespace by it.

title.description: Display name in the editor's project picker (e.g. "MMO"); the folder name when unset.

group.description: Editor project-picker group, e.g. "MMO", "Dungeons", "DC reference". Projects sharing a group list together; ungrouped projects list last.

menuOrder.description: Sort key in the project picker, lower first. A group sorts by its lowest member; unset sorts after set, then by name.

scenes.description: The editor's scene menu for this project, in order; the first entry is the main scene. Scene files on disk that no entry names still appear, under "other", so a new scene is never hidden.

id.description: Scene file id: the path under assets/scenes/ without .scene.json (e.g. "arena", "hollow-bastion/deepwake"). The file is the scene's identity; the doc's own `name` field is not.

label.description: What the menu shows instead of the id, e.g. "Combat lab" for arena.

note.description: One line on what the scene is for; shown as the menu tooltip.

variants.description: Pipeline stages or alternates of this scene (blockout, undercoat, editable, …). They list under it instead of as separate scenes; the menu labels each by what its id adds to the base id.

items.description: Scene file id: the path under assets/scenes/ without .scene.json (e.g. "arena", "hollow-bastion/deepwake"). The file is the scene's identity; the doc's own `name` field is not.

engine.description: Engine version or range this project was built against. Advisory.

multiplayer.description: How this game is played together. "p2p": the engine's peer rooms (a tab hosts; fine for co-op, prototypes, anything where a host cheating costs nobody). "server": dedicated/layered servers ONLY — the playground never forms a peer room for this project's scenes (a tab with no server plays alone), because a peer host is authoritative over everything it simulates. An MMO with a persistent world declares "server".

devConsole.description: Whether a PUBLISHED build of this game contains the developer console (/time, /weather, whatever its scripts declare). "dev": the editor has it, published bundles do not — the console module is not compiled in at all, so there is nothing for a player to find. "always": ship it (an internal build, a playtest bundle you want to drive from the chat box). "never": not even in the editor, for a game whose own scripts must not be pokeable. tools/publish.mjs reads this; --console / --no-console override it for one build.

tools.description: Registered tools this project needs installed under the engine's tools/ folder.

repo.description: Where to get it — a git URL or other clone/install source. Shown when it is missing.

version.description: Version or range the project was built against. Advisory: nothing enforces it yet.

optional.description: True if the project still runs without it (the tool only regenerates content).

reason.description: What this project uses it for. Worth writing: it is what tells a reader whether they need it.

dependsOn.description: Other projects whose assets this project's scenes use (a portal's instance scene, a borrowed model or material). Opening one of this project's scenes loads ONLY this project plus these, transitively — every other folder under projects/ costs nothing. A reference into a project not listed here is missing at runtime, so list it or copy the asset in.

items.description: Project id. Must match the folder name under projects/, since asset ids namespace by it.

npc.description: Offered by a person: an `acceptQuest` in that NPC's dialogue.

ref.description: NPC entity id; empty = the quest's `giver`.

schema.description: Offered by a person: an `acceptQuest` in that NPC's dialogue.

object.description: Offered by a thing, not a person: a notice board, a carved stone, a lost satchel — an entity running the `npc` builtin with `face: false` (and `readable: true` for text), whose dialogue carries the `acceptQuest`.

ref.description: Entity id of the object; empty = the quest's `giver`.

schema.description: Offered by a thing, not a person: a notice board, a carved stone, a lost satchel — an entity running the `npc` builtin with `face: false` (and `readable: true` for text), whose dialogue carries the `acceptQuest`.

auto.description: Starts by itself, with no announcement of its own: the quest-log of a character watching it (`autoStart` for a fresh journal, `autoOffer` at any time) accepts it on the authority the moment `when` and `area` hold. Nothing advertises it: players find it through leads (rumour, lore, a sight), never a marker.

when.description: Starts once this holds (clock, weather, flag, item, level …); absent = at once.

area.description: Starts once the character stands inside this region.

schema.description: Starts by itself, with no announcement of its own: the quest-log of a character watching it (`autoStart` for a fresh journal, `autoOffer` at any time) accepts it on the authority the moment `when` and `area` hold. Nothing advertises it: players find it through leads (rumour, lore, a sight), never a marker.

status.description: With `quest`: none = never accepted; available = can be accepted NOW (not taken, its `requires` done); active = objectives open; ready = objectives done, not handed in; complete = handed in; taken = active or ready.

flag.description: A per-character memory flag (set by a `setFlag` action).

is.description: With `flag`: the value it must have (default true).

met.description: Dialogue only: whether this character had spoken to THIS NPC before the current conversation.

item.description: Carries at least `qty` (default 1) of this item id.

coins.description: Carries at least this many copper.

bound.description: Dialogue only: whether this character's HEARTH is HERE: its respawn bind (netState bind/<bodyId>) is this NPC's `bindPoint` (within 1 m). An innkeeper's "Your bed by the fire is kept."

from.description: First hour of the window (0–24, fractions allowed).

to.description: Hour the window closes. Smaller than `from` = it wraps midnight (20 → 4 is the night).

clock.description: Holds while the world clock (netState world/hour, written by the day-night builtin on the authority) is in [from, to). No clock in the scene = never holds.

min.description: Precipitation at least this (0 = clear, 1 = the heaviest this world does).

max.description: Precipitation at most this (max 0.05 = dry weather).

storm.description: Storm (wind, gloom, lightning) at least this.

biomes.description: Biome rule ids: holds only while the biome under the character (the winning one, ctx.biomeAt) is one of these. Weather is one state per layer and what it FALLS as is the biome's: `min` 0.3 over snow biomes means snowing HERE.

weather.description: Holds while the layer's weather (netState world/weather) is inside this band. No weather in the scene = never holds.

__schema0.description: A test against the character (and, for clock/weather, the world it stands in). Every field present must hold; {} is always true.

presence.description: Offered by someone or something that is only THERE while a condition holds: an entity running the `npc` builtin plus the `presence` builtin (its `when`: an hour window, weather, a flag). Shared world: it is never removed, only hidden per player, and a conversation open with it holds it until the conversation ends.

schema.description: Offered by someone or something that is only THERE while a condition holds: an entity running the `npc` builtin plus the `presence` builtin (its `when`: an hour window, weather, a flag). Shared world: it is never removed, only hidden per player, and a conversation open with it holds it until the conversation ends.

clock.description: A field of the condition object (`when`, a dialogue `if`). Holds while the world clock (netState world/hour, written by the day-night builtin on the authority) is in [from, to). No clock in the scene = never holds.

from.description: First hour of the window (0–24, fractions allowed).

to.description: Hour the window closes. Smaller than `from` = it wraps midnight (20 → 4 is the night).

schema.description: Holds while the world clock (netState world/hour, written by the day-night builtin on the authority) is in [from, to). No clock in the scene = never holds.

weather.description: A field of the condition object (`when`, a dialogue `if`). Holds while the layer's weather (netState world/weather) is inside this band. No weather in the scene = never holds.

min.description: Precipitation at least this (0 = clear, 1 = the heaviest this world does).

max.description: Precipitation at most this (max 0.05 = dry weather).

storm.description: Storm (wind, gloom, lightning) at least this.

biomes.description: Biome rule ids: holds only while the biome under the character (the winning one, ctx.biomeAt) is one of these. Weather is one state per layer and what it FALLS as is the biome's: `min` 0.3 over snow biomes means snowing HERE.

schema.description: Holds while the layer's weather (netState world/weather) is inside this band. No weather in the scene = never holds.

quest.description: A field of the condition object (`when`, a dialogue `if`). Another quest's status in this character's journal.

flag.description: A field of the condition object (`when`, a dialogue `if`). A per-character memory flag.

level.description: A field of the condition object (`when`, a dialogue `if`). Character level at least this.

item.description: A field of the condition object (`when`, a dialogue `if`). Carries at least `qty` of the item.

coins.description: A field of the condition object (`when`, a dialogue `if`). Carries at least this many copper.

visit.description: Stand inside the objective's `area` (falls back to the quest's).

kill.description: Defeat `target`: an entity id, its `<target>-` prefix, or a spawned `#<target>#` template id (from the project's killEvent).

talk.description: Open a conversation with the NPC whose entity id is `target`.

interact.description: Use entity `target` (tagged `interactable`): the client sends player.interact; the authority checks owner and range.

read.description: Open the readable entity `target` (an `npc` builtin with `readable: true` — a sign, a slab, a book); its text resolves like dialogue.

deliver.description: Leave `required` × `item` at entity `target`: interacting with it while carrying the item hands them over (taken from the bags).

item.description: Item id handed over: each interact at `target` takes as many as are still `required` from the bags.

endure.description: Stay inside the objective's area (or the quest's) for `seconds`, unbroken, while `when` holds.

seconds.description: Unbroken seconds to stay inside the area while `when` holds. Leaving or the condition breaking starts the count over.

perform.description: Perform the named action (player.perform: /dance, /dig) within `range` of entity `target`, else inside the objective's area (or the quest's); no target and no area = anywhere.

action.description: Perform-action name ("dance", "dig"): the engine vocabulary plus the quest-log's `performActions` asset.

range.description: With a `target`: metres from that entity the performance counts within.

flag.description: setFlag / clearFlag on this character when the objective completes (per-character, saved with it).

oneOf.description: Remember something about this character (npc/<bodyId>.flags) — dialogue can then react to it.

schema.description: What happens, on the authority and for this character only, the moment the objective completes.

cave.description: Dig a walk-in cave into a slope or cliff: flared natural mouth with irregular carve-outs, a gently wandering bore (radius >= 3) and an optional chamber, routed for the most rock cover; refuses thin rock, sub-6 m bores and entries with no face. Compiles to `tunnels` op:<id>:cave-bore/mouth-flare + `blobs` op:<id>:mouth-notch-<k>/chamber.

entry.description: Mouth [x, z]: where the cave floor meets the open ground, at the foot of the face or on the slope.

y.description: Floor height at the mouth. Omit to use the ground there.

direction.description: Heading [dx, dz] INTO the rock (any length). Omit to dig straight uphill.

length.description: Horizontal length of the bore from the mouth, metres (the chamber, if any, is at its end).

radius.description: Bore radius, metres. At least 3 (a 6 m bore: the 6 m rule) — smaller is refused with the reason.

minCover.description: Smallest rock thickness, metres, over and beside the bore wall past the mouth. A route that cannot keep it is refused (thin rock).

grade.description: Rise/run of the floor along the bore (0.1 climbs gently into the hill; negative descends). Candidates jitter it by +-0.08.

bend.description: Degrees the candidate routes may turn off `direction` (start bearing and a gentle curve).

chamber.description: Radius of a chamber blob at the end, metres. Omit for a plain dead end.

seed.description: Wobble / mouth carve-out seed (combined with the world seed).

landmark.description: The general LANDMARK STAMP: any shape — a CSG spec (box/sphere/ellipsoid/cylinder/cone/capsule/torus/extrude/lathe/arch parts applied in order with add/sub/intersect + smooth blend, per-part roles and role noise), a Blender stamp (tools/mesh-dc) or a generator (`ledges`) — baked at a fine DC voxel (0.25-0.5 m; shells >= 3 voxels unless `thinOk`), one draw per material, own trimesh collider. Compiles to `landmarks` `op:<id>:landmark` + (bury/pad) one masked height patch `op:<id>:ground` >= 6 m wide. Bake: tools/landmark.mts.

at.description: World XZ of the spec's origin (its footprint centre).

y.description: World Y of spec y 0 (the foot). Omit: from `blend` (bury: lowest footprint ground - depth; pad: median; none: ground at `at`).

yaw.description: Degrees about +Y (spec +Z turns toward +X for positive yaw).

scale.description: Uniform scale of every spec length.

voxel.description: DC voxel, metres (0.5 for big rock; 0.25 for fine masonry). Shells must be >= 3 voxels.

roles.description: Per-role defaults. `rock` (and any role named rock/cliff/stone-natural) gets outward rock noise unless set; every other role is crisp.

scale.description: Feature size of the first octave, metres.

grow.description: Outward only (default): the noise never thins a wall.

file.description: Provenance: the project-relative spec file `worldgen op --apply` inlined into `csg`.
Project-relative CSG spec JSON. `worldgen op --apply` INLINES it into `csg` (keeping `file`), so the recipe always carries the solids.

blender.description: Project-relative .blend or Blender build .py: closed solids with roles from object names/collections, exported headless through tools/mesh-dc (export_blender.py).

resolved.description: Written by `tools/landmark.mts --resolve`: the exported solids' digest and extent (core cannot read a .blend).

generator.description: A registered landmark generator (`ledges`: the ledges solve as a landmark).

args.description: The generator's own params (for `ledges`: the `ledges` operator params).

source.description: The shape: `{ csg }` / `{ file }` (CSG spec), `{ blender }` (mesh-dc stamp), or `{ generator, args }`.

materials.description: Role -> `zone` (default: the zone's cliff stone on faces, its ground cover on tops, triplanar terrain material, ONE draw shared by every zone role), `zone-stone` (stone everywhere), `surface:<palette name>`, or a material asset id (its own draw).

blend.description: How the terrain meets the foot. Every terrain piece is >= 6 m wide (FINE_MIN).

mode.description: `bury`: spec y 0 sinks `depth` under the LOWEST ground of the footprint and a mound feathers the terrain up over the foot. `pad`: a flat apron at the foot level. `none`: spec y 0 = ground at `at`, no terrain edit.

depth.description: bury: metres the foot sinks under the lowest ground of the footprint (>= 1).

mound.description: bury: metres the terrain rises against the foot (hides the cut line), fading out over `feather`.

feather.description: Metres over which the edit fades back to the natural ground (>= 6: the FINE_MIN rule).

apron.description: pad: flat apron width around the foot (>= 6).

openings.description: Named doorways/portals kept CLEAR (carved after every part) and noise-free; each is also a reach target.

at.description: Spec-local FLOOR centre of the doorway.

yaw.description: Degrees; 0 = the opening passes along Z.

targets.description: Walkable points the BAKED collider must reach from the ground around (tools/landmark.mts reach loop). None and no openings = no reach loop.

seed.description: Noise seed (combined with the world seed).

name.description: Label (thin-wall faults and reports name it).

op.description: `add` (default) unions; `sub` carves air out of EVERYTHING BEFORE it in the list; `intersect` clips everything before it.

at.description: Position in the parent frame: the CENTRE of box/sphere/ellipsoid/torus, the BASE centre of cylinder/cone/capsule/extrude/lathe/arch and a group's origin.

role.description: Material/noise role (inherited from the group; default `rock`).

blend.description: Smooth-min radius against everything before it (smooth union / smooth carve), metres.

thinOk.description: Exempt from the thin-wall rule (a railing, a fin, a spire tip).

noise.description: Overrides the role's noise; null = crisp.

scale.description: Feature size of the first octave, metres.

grow.description: Outward only (default): the noise never thins a wall.

size.description: box / ellipsoid full extents [w, h, d].

r.description: Radius: sphere, cylinder, cone base, capsule; torus TUBE radius.

top.description: Cone top radius (a frustum; compiled as a lathe).

polygon.description: Extrude outline [x, z] (no repeated closing vertex).

profile.description: Lathe profile [radius, y] bottom to top (radius >= 0).

rise.description: Arch opening height above the springing.

legs.description: Arch springing height (straight jambs below the curve).

parts.description: Group children, in the group's frame.

node.description: A raw core CSG node passed through (generators); its position/rotation are in the parent frame.

ledges.description: A natural ledge system on a steep slope or cliff band: narrow noisy shelves, every ledge reachable by a ramp or, where none fits, a short cave climbing inside the rock (two mouths). Default mode `landmark`: real rock baked at a fine DC voxel (stacked rock masses, ramp notches, boulders, bored caves with flared mouths) — one `landmarks` piece `op:<id>:landmark` (bake: tools/ledge-landmark.mts) over one masked height patch `op:<id>:ground` kept inside the rock. Mode `height`: the 2.5D height edit (patch + `tunnels`/`blobs` `op:<id>:link-<n>-*`).

center.description: Centre [x, z] of a round area (with `radius`). Give this OR `polygon`.

radius.description: Radius of the round area, metres.

polygon.description: Area outline [x, z]. Give this OR center + radius.

bandHeight.description: Smallest height of one ledge band, metres. Grows on steep ground so a typical ledge keeps `minShelf` (riser = slope x ledge).

smooth.description: Metres of ground smoothing the ledges follow: ~6 hugs every spur and gully (ledges), ~18 gives long town bands (that is `terrace`).

jitter.description: Metres the ledge lips wander off the smoothed contour (three octaves of noise down to 5 m): ragged rock lips.

stagger.description: Panel width, metres, across the face: each panel shifts its ledges by its own part of a band, so ledges END, step down or overlap at the seams instead of running as one band across the face. Typical ledge length ~ 1-2 panels.

staggerAmount.description: Largest shift of a panel's ledges, as a fraction of a band (0 = continuous contour bands).

pinch.description: Every ledge pinches out (ends at a panel seam against a two-band riser, then picks up again) once in this many panels along the face; the next ledge up pinches two panels on. 0 = ledges run on through every panel.

tilt.description: Outward fall of each ledge from its back to its lip, as a fraction of the band height (a weathered shelf sheds water).

minShelf.description: Preferred smallest ledge depth, metres (never below 6: the 6 m rule).

riserSlope.description: Rise/run of the risers: steep (>= ~1.2) so they read as the zone's own cliff rock, not as grassy banks.

links.description: How ledges are joined: ramps only, caves first, or `auto` = a ramp where one fits, else a short cave climbing inside the rock (two mouths).

rampGrade.description: Rise/run of a ramp (0.3 = a steep path, 17 degrees).

caveRadius.description: Bore radius of a cave link (>= 3: the 6 m rule).

caveCover.description: Rock, metres, a cave link keeps over and beside its bore between its two mouths.

caveGrade.description: Steepest floor grade of a cave link (0.5 = 27 degrees, walkable).

blend.description: Metres past the (wobbled) outline over which the ledges fade back into the slope.

edgeNoise.description: Metres the outline wobbles in and out.

baseY.description: Level of the band at the area's median ground. Omit to use that median.

seed.description: Jitter / edge / mouth seed (combined with the world seed).

mode.description: `landmark` (default): the solved shelves become a LANDMARK — real rock baked at `voxel` (stacked rock masses per level with ragged battered stepped faces, ramp notches, a few boulders, caves bored through it; `features.landmarks`, baked by tools/ledge-landmark.mts) over a terrain patch that stays inside it. `height`: the older 2.5D height edit on the 2 m lattice (no overhangs; lips smear).

voxel.description: Landmark DC voxel, metres (0.5: a 4 m drop is 8 voxels).

lipNoise.description: Landmark: metres each level's outline wanders (ragged lips; a different noise per level).

batter.description: Landmark: degrees every rock face leans back from vertical (5-10 reads as a battered natural face).

chamfer.description: Landmark: metres of rounding on every rock mass's top edge.

boulders.description: Landmark: low, wide boulder masses fused into shelves at least ~6 m across, whole site (no pillars).

inset.description: Landmark: metres the terrain stays under the rock surface.

reachRepairs.description: Landmark: repair ramps (<= 0.5 grade, >= 2.6 m wide between >= 1.5 m cheeks) that the bake's collider walk added for core shelves it could not reach. Written by tools/ledge-landmark.mts (--fix-reach, on by default); not hand-authored.

from.description: Head [x, y, z]: a flat spot on the cut-off shelf's top.

to.description: Foot [x, y, z]: walkable ground the baked collider reaches.

path.description: A walkable path RIBBON along a spline (control points, width, dirt/cobble/slab, maxGrade): graded ground under it, steps or switchbacks where steep, retaining walls on high side drops; compiles to `op:<id>:ribbon` + the `op:<id>:grade` height patch. Paths are ribbons: never carve a path.

points.description: Control polyline, world XZ, in walking order. A centripetal Catmull-Rom spline runs through every point; 6-30 m apart is plenty.

width.description: Walkable width of the ribbon (m). Footpath 2-2.6, town lane 3-4, street 5-6.

style.description: dirt: trodden earth, the zone's `road` tile (else its `ground`) smoothed and lifted a little, a darker worn rim and a wide worn verge: it reads as a path from afar and still sits in the land. cobble: the zone's `paving` tile. slab: `paving` at a larger tile, a straight hard edge. Always the terrain's own tint: a ribbon never reads bluer than the ground it lies on, and only trodden dirt reads lighter.

surface.description: Palette surface NAME to pave with, overriding the zone tile the style picks (e.g. `gravel`).

maxGrade.description: Steepest longitudinal rise/run the ribbon may climb as a ramp. Steeper stretches become a switchback (inside `corridor`) or steps.

steep.description: Where the ground is steeper than maxGrade over a stretch: steps (flights + landings), switchback (zig-zag inside `corridor`, steps on any leg still too steep), auto = switchback when the corridor allows it, else steps.

corridor.description: Half-width (m) the path may wander sideways from the control line to detour gently (switchbacks). 0 = keep to the line.

maxCutFill.description: How far (m) the graded centre line may sit below/above the smoothed ground before the stretch is called steep.

shoulder.description: Minimum feather (m) each side of the levelled core over which the grade blends back into the ground. Widens automatically on a high side drop (bank no steeper than 1:2).

edge.description: verge: a worn edge (noise-offset 0.3-0.6 m, deterministic) that fades dithered into the ground; both ends taper, round off and fade into whatever paving or road they meet. hard: a straight edge with a small lip (laid slabs, kerbless street).

walls.description: auto: retaining walls from the world-kit retaining-wall kit on BOTH sides: the fill side where the drop exceeds `wallDrop`, the uphill cut where the bank exceeds `wallCut`. Runs end in the kit's stepped end pieces. none: banks only.

wallDrop.description: Side drop (m) beyond which the fill side gets a retaining wall instead of a bank.

wallCut.description: Uphill cut (m) beyond which the cut side gets a retaining wall holding the bank back instead of a raw earth slope.

wallStyle.description: Retaining-wall kit style: common (coursed rubble), stone (dressed ashlar).

wallSkin.description: Stone the walls wear: omitted = the zone's own stone (its `ground.cliff` surface, the rock-skins key: `worldgen-ribbon materials` writes `ribbon-wall/<cliff>-rubble|ashlar`); a palette cliff surface NAME to force one; `kit` = the kit's own grey stone.

terrace.description: Cut a slope into long contour shelves (a stepped town site, a hillside farm) joined by ramps, risers walled with world-kit retaining walls; compiles to one masked height patch `op:<id>:ground` + `kitWalls` runs `op:<id>:wall-<n>`.

center.description: Centre [x, z] of a round area (with `radius`). Give this OR `polygon`. The edge is wobbled and faded either way.

radius.description: Radius of the round area, metres.

polygon.description: Area outline [x, z] (any simple polygon). Give this OR center + radius.

stepHeight.description: Height of one contour band = one riser, metres (3 = the kit's h300 wall). Shelves that merge make a riser of two bands; never past the tallest kit wall (6.4 m).

smooth.description: Metres of ground smoothing the contours follow: ~18 gives long town/farm bands, ~8 hugs every spur.

baseY.description: Level of the band at the area's median ground. Omit to use that median.

jitter.description: Metres the riser lines wander off the smoothed contour (deterministic noise): 0 = clean contours.

minShelf.description: Preferred smallest shelf depth, metres. Shallower shelves merge into a neighbour unless the riser would pass the kit max; then they merge only down to 6 m (the 6 m rule).

riserSlope.description: Rise/run of an UNWALLED riser bank (in the fade and where walls are off).

rampWidth.description: Width of each ramp between shelves, metres (at least 6).

rampGrade.description: Rise/run of a ramp (0.15 = 8.5 degrees). Ramp length = riser height / rampGrade.

blend.description: Metres past the (wobbled) outline over which the shelves fade back into the hill.

edgeNoise.description: Metres the outline wobbles in and out (~40 m wavelength), so the terrace never ends on a drawn circle.

walls.description: World-kit retaining walls on risers inside the area (`features.kitWalls`), or none (plain banks).

wallMinDrop.description: Smallest riser drop, metres, that gets a wall.

seed.description: Jitter / edge-noise seed (combined with the world seed).
